<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(5)</span></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="S3.E6"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathrm{Lift}_{S}(m;a,\tau)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>Lift</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathrm{Lift}_{S}(m;a,\tau)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\mathrm{SESA}_{S}(m;a,\tau)-\mathrm{ESA}_{S}(a,\tau)." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>SESA</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>ESA</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\mathrm{SESA}_{S}(m;a,\tau)-\mathrm{ESA}_{S}(a,\tau).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(6)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.2" class="ltx_p">SESA is defined when the selected subset is nonempty; positive lift means that the predictor isolates coordinates whose latest observed direction is more reliable than the unselective baseline. Under our construction, DMD predictions remain in the recent-history span, linking their attainable directional alignment to FRR. Full predictor constructions, rank selection, null generation, grouping rules, and numerical conventions are deferred to the appendix.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Empirical Analysis</h2>

<section id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Experimental setup.</h5>

<div id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We analyze stored weight trajectories in two complementary training
regimes.
<em id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Multi-pass vision training.</em>
Our CIFAR-10 panel contains <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="30" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>30</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">30</annotation></semantics></math> model–optimizer cells, crossing five
architectures (a CIFAR-style ResNet, two ViT scales, AlexNet, and an
MLP) with six training configurations (SGD, SGD with momentum, SGD
with weight decay, SAM, Adam, and AdaGrad).
Models are trained for <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="50" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>50</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">50</annotation></semantics></math> epochs with batch size <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>128</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">128</annotation></semantics></math> and a cosine
learning-rate schedule, with weights recorded at every epoch boundary.
Unless otherwise stated, probes are evaluated at anchor epochs
<math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{5,10,20,30,40\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>30</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>40</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{5,10,20,30,40\}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Section <a href="#S4.SS4" title="4.4 Training conditions modulate state-dependent temporal redundancy ‣ 4 Empirical Analysis ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.4</span></a> additionally uses Muon and controlled
weight-decay and momentum dose arms.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">One-pass language-model pretraining.</em>
We analyze the public checkpoint trajectories of Pythia
70M, 160M, and 410M <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">Biderman et al. 2023</a>)</cite>.
For each model, checkpoints are spaced by <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}000</annotation></semantics></math> optimization steps;
we evaluate <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="123" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>123</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">123</annotation></semantics></math> admissible post-warmup anchors spanning steps
<math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="7{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>7,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7{,}000</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="129{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>129,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">129{,}000</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Unless otherwise stated, both regimes use horizon <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau=5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau=5</annotation></semantics></math> and history
length <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{\mathrm{past}}=5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>past</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{\mathrm{past}}=5</annotation></semantics></math>.
The measurement clock is regime-specific: one probe step corresponds
to one epoch for CIFAR and one released checkpoint for Pythia.
Vision tensors use flat <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=16</annotation></semantics></math> within-tensor groups by default, whereas
Pythia tensors use architecture-aligned groups within the <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="qkv" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">qkv</annotation></semantics></math>,
attention-output, MLP, and vector segments.
All probes are causal at the anchor and depend only on the preceding
weight history.
FRR- and LRGF-based results always state their grouping convention;
fixed-threshold <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{LRGF}_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>LRGF</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{LRGF}_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> is used for matched
cross-layer comparisons, while shuffle-calibrated
<math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{LRGF}_{\mathrm{cal}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>LRGF</mi><mi>cal</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{LRGF}_{\mathrm{cal}}</annotation></semantics></math> is used along the within-layer time
axis.
Complete configurations, checkpoint accounting, and measurement details are provided in Appendix A of the supplementary material.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1 </span>Probe families are coherent but non-equivalent</h3>

<section id="S4.SS1.SSSx1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection">Within-family coherence under explicit conventions</h4>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSSx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSSx1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We first examine within-family agreement to test whether alternative
readouts yield coherent measurements rather than idiosyncratic behavior
of a single readout. Figure <a href="#S4.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ Within-family coherence under explicit conventions ‣ 4.1 Probe families are coherent but non-equivalent ‣ 4 Empirical Analysis ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> summarizes one
comparison for each probe family over the controlled vision panel of
<math id="S4.SS1.SSSx1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="30" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>30</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">30</annotation></semantics></math> model–optimizer cells and five anchors.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F1" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2608.15483v1/fig_411_family_agreement_compact.svg" id="S4.F1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:663/207;" width="663" height="207"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 1: </span>
Within-family agreement on the controlled vision panel.
(a) ESA versus group-mean VCS;
(b) out-of-window versus in-window FRR;
(c) SESA under DMD and linear-trend selectors.
Circled points mark cells with near-zero-displacement coordinates.
</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS1.SSSx1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSSx1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="S4.SS1.SSSx1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Displacement-direction.</em>
ESA and group-mean VCS weight the same displacement pair differently:
ESA gives each coordinate one sign vote, whereas VCS weights coordinates
by displacement magnitude. Under a centered bivariate Gaussian
reference, the corresponding sign agreement and correlation satisfy
<math id="S4.SS1.SSSx1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{ESA}=1-\arccos(\mathrm{VCS})/\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ESA</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>arccos</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>VCS</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{ESA}=1-\arccos(\mathrm{VCS})/\pi</annotation></semantics></math>
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib49" title="" class="ltx_ref">Schmid and Schmidt 2007</a>)</cite>. As shown in
Fig. <a href="#S4.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ Within-family coherence under explicit conventions ‣ 4.1 Probe families are coherent but non-equivalent ‣ 4 Empirical Analysis ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>(a), 28 of the 30 cells closely follow this
parameter-free curve across anchors. Departures occur primarily in cells
with many near-zero-displacement coordinates (coordinates whose
displacement is zero or numerically negligible over one or both
intervals): these coordinates contribute little to VCS but remain
sensitive to ESA’s coordinate-wise sign convention, and restricting the
comparison to coordinates that move in both intervals largely restores
agreement.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.SSSx1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSSx1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="S4.SS1.SSSx1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Subspace-residual.</em>
Out-of-window and in-window FRR are strongly correlated
(median per-cell Spearman <math id="S4.SS1.SSSx1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{S}=0.83" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.83</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{S}=0.83</annotation></semantics></math>;
Fig. <a href="#S4.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ Within-family coherence under explicit conventions ‣ 4.1 Probe families are coherent but non-equivalent ‣ 4 Empirical Analysis ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>(b)), consistent with local smoothness across
nearby target windows. FRR is computed within contiguous,
structure-aligned parameter groups using a model-specific, empirically
selected granularity, which determines the spatial scale at which local
subspace structure and predictable pockets can be resolved.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.SSSx1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSSx1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="S4.SS1.SSSx1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Predictor-based.</em>
DMD and linear-trend selectors induce strongly consistent SESA
orderings (median per-cell <math id="S4.SS1.SSSx1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{S}=0.89" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.89</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{S}=0.89</annotation></semantics></math>), while DMD achieves
systematically higher values (Fig. <a href="#S4.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ Within-family coherence under explicit conventions ‣ 4.1 Probe families are coherent but non-equivalent ‣ 4 Empirical Analysis ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>(c)),
consistent with its ability to exploit coupled low-rank dynamics in the
recent trajectory rather than extrapolating a single linear trend.
Alternative grouping granularities and additional within-family checks
are reported in Appendix B.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS1.SSSx2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection">Cross-family relations across levels of complexity</h4>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSSx2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSSx2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We next compare representative readouts across probe families at the
tensor level. Correlations are computed across tensors within each
model–optimizer cell and summarized by the median over the 30 cells,
avoiding correlations induced by pooling different training recipes.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F2" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2608.15483v1/figures/fig_412_cross_panels.png" id="S4.F2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:663/228;" width="663" height="228" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 2: </span>
Cross-family relations on the controlled vision panel.
(a) ESA versus out-of-window FRR;
(b) out-of-window FRR versus DMD direction cosine;
(c) ESA versus DMD lift.
Circled points mark cells flagged by the near-zero-displacement
diagnostic.
</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS1.SSSx2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSSx2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="S4.SS1.SSSx2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Direction–subspace.</em>
ESA and out-of-window FRR are strongly anticorrelated
(median per-cell Spearman <math id="S4.SS1.SSSx2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{S}=-0.74" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.74</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{S}=-0.74</annotation></semantics></math>;
Fig. <a href="#S4.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ Cross-family relations across levels of complexity ‣ 4.1 Probe families are coherent but non-equivalent ‣ 4 Empirical Analysis ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>(a)): tensors with more persistent
coordinate-wise directions also tend to keep their future displacement
closer to the span of recent updates. The two probes therefore detect
closely related structure from different geometric perspectives.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.SSSx2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSSx2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="S4.SS1.SSSx2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Subspace–predictor.</em>
Under our construction, the DMD prediction lies in the recent-history
subspace, giving the geometric bound</p>
<table id="S4.Ex1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\cos_{\mathrm{DMD}}\leq\sqrt{1-\mathrm{FRR}^{2}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>DMD</mi></msub><mo>≤</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>FRR</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos_{\mathrm{DMD}}\leq\sqrt{1-\mathrm{FRR}^{2}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS1.SSSx2.p3.2" class="ltx_p">DMD direction cosine is correspondingly strongly anticorrelated with
FRR (median per-cell Spearman <math id="S4.SS1.SSSx2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{S}=-0.75" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.75</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{S}=-0.75</annotation></semantics></math>;
Fig. <a href="#S4.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ Cross-family relations across levels of complexity ‣ 4.1 Probe families are coherent but non-equivalent ‣ 4 Empirical Analysis ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>(b)), with 37% of tensor-level observations
lying within 0.15 of the bound. FRR thus characterizes the directional
headroom available to a predictor constructed from the recent-history
subspace.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.SSSx2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSSx2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="S4.SS1.SSSx2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Direction–predictor.</em>
DMD lift satisfies the headroom bound</p>
<table id="S4.Ex2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Lift}=\mathrm{SESA}-\mathrm{ESA}\leq 1-\mathrm{ESA}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>Lift</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>SESA</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>ESA</mi></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>ESA</mi></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Lift}=\mathrm{SESA}-\mathrm{ESA}\leq 1-\mathrm{ESA}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS1.SSSx2.p4.2" class="ltx_p">Its binned median peaks at <math id="S4.SS1.SSSx2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.118" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.118</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.118</annotation></semantics></math> for
<math id="S4.SS1.SSSx2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{ESA}\in[0.6,0.7]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ESA</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0.6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.7</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{ESA}\in[0.6,0.7]</annotation></semantics></math>, rather than at the highest ESA values
(Fig. <a href="#S4.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ Cross-family relations across levels of complexity ‣ 4.1 Probe families are coherent but non-equivalent ‣ 4 Empirical Analysis ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>(c)). High ESA already indicates strong
predictability from directional persistence alone, leaving little
residual error for DMD-based selection to remove; low lift in this
region therefore does not imply low predictability. At very low ESA,
the trajectory also offers less stable structure to exploit. The
largest lift occurs at intermediate ESA, where DMD can recover
additional low-rank temporal structure beyond coordinate-wise
persistence while sufficient headroom remains.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.SSSx2.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSSx2.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Together, these results show that predictability can be characterized
at complementary levels of complexity: coordinate-wise directional
persistence, local history-subspace structure, and additional temporal
structure recoverable by an explicit predictor.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2 </span>Predictability is spatially localized across parameter scales</h3>

<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We next ask where the measured short-horizon structure resides.
We partition trainable tensors into two predefined morphological
classes: <em id="S4.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">auxiliary</em> tensors include vector-like parameters such
as normalization parameters and biases, whereas <em id="S4.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">bulk</em> tensors
include matrix-like feature-transforming weights such as attention
projections, MLP weights, and convolutional kernels.
Exact tensor membership and partition audits are provided in
Appendix C.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F3" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2608.15483v1/fig_42_slope.svg" id="S4.F3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:419/216;" width="419" height="216"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 3: </span>
Auxiliary–bulk separation across training regimes.
Each line connects the auxiliary and bulk summaries within a
matched CIFAR run or Pythia trajectory; circles denote CIFAR runs
and stars denote Pythia trajectories.
Auxiliary tensors exceed bulk tensors in <math id="S4.F3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="29/32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>29</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>32</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">29/32</annotation></semantics></math> comparisons under
ESA and <math id="S4.F3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="32/32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>32</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>32</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32/32</annotation></semantics></math> under the selector-free DMD direction cosine.
Because the two regimes use different grouping protocols, we
compare the within-line ordering rather than absolute levels across
regimes.
</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#S4.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 4.2 Predictability is spatially localized across parameter scales ‣ 4 Empirical Analysis ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> shows a stable tensor-scale
separation within matched trajectories. Auxiliary tensors exceed bulk
tensors in <math id="S4.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="29/32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>29</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>32</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">29/32</annotation></semantics></math> trajectory-level comparisons under ESA and in
<math id="S4.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="32/32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>32</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>32</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32/32</annotation></semantics></math> comparisons under the DMD direction cosine. Before temporal
aggregation, the same ordering holds at all <math id="S4.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="246" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>246</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">246</annotation></semantics></math> Pythia
model–checkpoint snapshots under both probes. The recurring paired
ordering shows that this coarse spatial organization is shared across
multi-pass vision training and one-pass language-model pretraining,
rather than arising from a single probe or training regime. We do not
compare the magnitudes of the CIFAR and Pythia gaps because their
grouping and checkpoint protocols differ.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Despite their lower aggregate predictability, bulk tensors contain a
small minority of within-tensor groups with substantially elevated
predictability. We refer to these localized groups as
<em id="S4.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">predictable pockets</em>. Under the reported structural cuts and
reference convention, they account for approximately <math id="S4.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6\%</annotation></semantics></math> of pooled
group–anchor observations. Most pockets are transient: their
identities change across training anchors, although the degree of
persistence varies by parameter role. Detailed pocket trajectories and
persistence analyses are reported in
Appendix D.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F4" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2608.15483v1/figures/fig_42_pocket.png" id="S4.F4.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:628/457;" width="628" height="457" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 4: </span>
Distribution of FRR excess above the approximate isotropic reference
<math id="S4.F4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sqrt{(D-r)/D}-\mathrm{FRR}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></msqrt><mo>−</mo><mi>FRR</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{(D-r)/D}-\mathrm{FRR}</annotation></semantics></math> over structurally grouped bulk
parameters, with <math id="S4.F4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=5</annotation></semantics></math>. The highlighted tail
(<math id="S4.F4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{excess}&gt;0.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>excess</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0.3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{excess}&gt;0.3</annotation></semantics></math>) contains approximately <math id="S4.F4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6\%</annotation></semantics></math> of pooled
group–anchor observations.
</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.3 </span>Probe readings track the realized optimization state</h3>

<div id="S4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The proposed probes need not be interpreted in isolation. We compare
their readings with complementary diagnostics derived from realized
trajectory motion and training telemetry. For ESA, we use movement
directedness—the ratio of net displacement to path length over the
future window—and a loss-side estimate of gradient coherence based
on loss decrease, learning rates, and gradient norms. Across
heterogeneous CIFAR training conditions, ESA correlates with these
quantities at <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho=0.978" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.978</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho=0.978</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho=0.804" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.804</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho=0.804</annotation></semantics></math>, respectively. Formal
definitions, their relation to prior gradient-coherence and
signal-to-noise measures, and the complete comparisons are provided in
Appendix E.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We next use Pythia-70M as a case study to examine how these
state-level correspondences unfold within a one-pass pretraining
trajectory. Figure <a href="#S4.F5" title="Figure 5 ‣ 4.3 Probe readings track the realized optimization state ‣ 4 Empirical Analysis ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> jointly resolves the
public loss trajectory and probe readings across parameter roles,
layers, and grouping scales.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F5" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2608.15483v1/fig_43_pythia70m_case_study.png" id="S4.F5.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_portrait" style="aspect-ratio:698/1179;" width="698" height="1179" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 5: </span>
Pythia-70M case study.
(a) ESA by parameter role.
(b) Released training loss and its smoothed trajectory.
(c) Fraction of <math id="S4.F5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="qkv" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">qkv</annotation></semantics></math> row groups satisfying <math id="S4.F5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{FRR}&lt;0.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>FRR</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0.7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{FRR}&lt;0.7</annotation></semantics></math>.
(d) Head-aligned <math id="S4.F5.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="qkv" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">qkv</annotation></semantics></math> <math id="S4.F5.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{LRGF}_{\mathrm{cal}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>LRGF</mi><mi>cal</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{LRGF}_{\mathrm{cal}}</annotation></semantics></math> excess.
Vertical lines mark the early fading of head-aligned excess, the
loss minimum, and the later <math id="S4.F5.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="qkv" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">qkv</annotation></semantics></math> ESA rise.
</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The auxiliary vector segment remains clearly separated from the bulk
roles throughout training. Although the bulk tensors contain most of
the model parameters, all three bulk roles undergo a rapid initial
decline in ESA and cross below the <math id="S4.SS3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5</annotation></semantics></math> sign-agreement reference.
They continue to evolve within this sub-<math id="S4.SS3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5</annotation></semantics></math> regime rather than
settling to a common floor. The clearest mid-to-late turn occurs in
<math id="S4.SS3.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="qkv" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">qkv</annotation></semantics></math>: its ESA bends upward near the smoothed loss minimum around
<math id="S4.SS3.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="50" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>50</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">50</annotation></semantics></math>k steps, reaches a local maximum near <math id="S4.SS3.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="75" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>75</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">75</annotation></semantics></math>k after the loss has
begun to rise, and subsequently declines again. Attention-output and
MLP exhibit smaller, non-identical variations over the same interval.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p4.1" class="ltx_p">The finer-resolution views expose an earlier reorganization within
<math id="S4.SS3.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="qkv" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">qkv</annotation></semantics></math> at a different spatial scale. Head-aligned
<math id="S4.SS3.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{LRGF}_{\mathrm{cal}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>LRGF</mi><mi>cal</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{LRGF}_{\mathrm{cal}}</annotation></semantics></math> excess is concentrated near the
beginning of training and largely fades around <math id="S4.SS3.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>20</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">20</annotation></semantics></math>k steps. Row-level
low-FRR pockets, however, are initially sparse and emerge only after
some training, first in deeper layers and later across deep and
intermediate layers. The fading of head-aligned excess therefore
should not be read as a global disappearance of predictable
structure. Rather, the detectable <math id="S4.SS3.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="qkv" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">qkv</annotation></semantics></math> structure changes its
localization and its relation to the chosen grouping scale.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p5.1" class="ltx_p">The temporal proximity between the loss reversal and the later
<math id="S4.SS3.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="qkv" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">qkv</annotation></semantics></math> ESA excursion is a retrospective correspondence, not evidence
that either event causes or uniquely explains the other. The
role-, depth-, and grouping-resolved readings nevertheless reveal
trajectory reorganizations that are not localized by the scalar loss
curve alone. Complete results for the other Pythia scales, together
with cross-group diagnostics and pocket-evolution analyses, are
reported in Appendix F.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.4 </span>Training conditions modulate state-dependent temporal redundancy</h3>

<div id="S4.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Across our controlled CIFAR experiments, temporal redundancy varies
systematically with architecture, optimizer family, weight decay, and
momentum. Size-controlled architecture comparisons and controlled
weight-decay and momentum dose studies are reported in
Appendix G; here we use optimizer-family
variation as a compact main-text example.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F6" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2608.15483v1/figures/fig_44_optfam.png" id="S4.F6.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:698/550;" width="698" height="550" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 6: </span>
Optimizer-family profiles for ViT-mid along training loss
(horizontal axis reversed), with canonical bulk ESA on the vertical
axis. All-family comparisons use the common support
<math id="S4.F6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{loss}\approx 0.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>loss</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>0.9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{loss}\approx 0.9</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S4.F6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.4</annotation></semantics></math>; matched loss does not imply matched
optimizer state. Dashed line: <math id="S4.F6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5</annotation></semantics></math> sign-agreement reference.
</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Because optimizer families traverse the loss trajectory at different
rates, Figure <a href="#S4.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ 4.4 Training conditions modulate state-dependent temporal redundancy ‣ 4 Empirical Analysis ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> compares them along training loss
rather than checkpoint index. Distinct profiles remain visible over the
shared range: SAM occupies the highest-ESA regime, Muon remains near the
<math id="S4.SS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5</annotation></semantics></math> reference, Adam lies below SGD over most of their overlap, and SGD
and AdaGrad approach a similar low-loss plateau. Thus, optimization
position organizes the evolution of predictability, while the training
recipe also conditions its level and local directional structure.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS4.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Higher predictability should not be interpreted as better optimization:
optimizers with strong final performance occupy both high- and
low-predictability regimes. The complete optimizer panel,
predictability–accuracy comparison, and the architecture,
weight-decay, and momentum results are provided in
Appendix G.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Discussion, Limitations, and Future Directions</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The proposed measurements provide a parameter-resolved and time-local view of the temporal organization of training dynamics. They localize short-horizon structure across parameter roles, layers, tensors, and within-tensor groups, while tracking how that structure emerges, disappears, or changes its spatial organization. Directional, subspace, and predictor-based probes provide complementary views: their agreement supports shared trajectory structure, whereas their differences distinguish non-equivalent forms of temporal organization. The framework can therefore support retrospective analysis of checkpoint-rich runs with sufficiently fine temporal resolution.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The probes nevertheless capture a restricted class of dynamics, emphasizing low-order directional relations and structure representable within short, locally low-dimensional history spaces rather than arbitrary nonlinear, long-memory, or high-rank dependence. Their readings also depend on checkpoint spacing, horizon, history length, grouping convention, and null calibration, which define the scale of observation. Because ESA and FRR use realized post-anchor displacement, they are retrospective or delayed measurements rather than immediately available online signals, and temporal alignment with loss or other events should not be interpreted as mechanistic evidence. Our current coverage of controlled vision training and public Pythia trajectories also does not establish generality across larger models or other learning paradigms.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Future work should extend these measurements across broader scales and regimes, and study the emergence, migration, and disappearance of predictable pockets together with their alignment to representation formation, circuit development, and interpretable parameter communities. The sub-<math id="S5.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5</annotation></semantics></math> ESA regimes further motivate examining possible connections to edge-of-stability behavior <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cohen et al. 2021</a>)</cite> and Ornstein–Uhlenbeck-like mean reversion<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib50" title="" class="ltx_ref">Mandt et al. 2017</a>)</cite>. Another direction is to develop delayed-online or history-only diagnostics that complement scalar loss. Our preliminary online example suggests that restricting predictive write-back to a higher-confidence auxiliary subset can be more reliable than broad prediction (Appendix H), motivating future use of these instruments for adaptive prediction, selective updating, skipping, and compression.</p>
</div>
</section>

those of Section 3; references prefixed by “Section”,
“Figure”, or “Eq.” point into the main paper, and “Appendix A” to
“Appendix H” point into this document.</p>

<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Experimental Coverage and Protocol Details</h2>

<div id="A1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This appendix records the training corpus behind
Section 4, the checkpoint accounting for both regimes, and
the measurement constants shared by every probe.
Appendix <a href="#A1.SS1" title="A.1 Vision Panel: Architectures, Optimizers, and Recipes ‣ Appendix A Experimental Coverage and Protocol Details ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.1</span></a> covers the controlled vision
panel and Appendix <a href="#A1.SS2" title="A.2 Additional Run Families ‣ Appendix A Experimental Coverage and Protocol Details ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.2</span></a> the further run families that
Section 4.4 draws on. Appendix <a href="#A1.SS3" title="A.3 Pretraining Checkpoint Coverage ‣ Appendix A Experimental Coverage and Protocol Details ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.3</span></a> covers
the pretraining checkpoints, and
Appendix <a href="#A1.SS4" title="A.4 Measurement Clocks, Anchors, and Seeds ‣ Appendix A Experimental Coverage and Protocol Details ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.4</span></a> the measurement clocks, anchor
construction, and seeds.</p>
</div>
<section id="A1.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.1 </span>Vision Panel: Architectures, Optimizers, and Recipes</h3>

<div id="A1.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The controlled vision panel crosses five architectures with six training
configurations. The architectures span three structural families: an MLP;
AlexNet and a CIFAR-style ResNet-18 variant with its last stage removed;
and two ViT scales, written ViT and ViT-mid. The six configurations are
plain SGD, SGD with momentum, SGD with weight decay, Adam, AdaGrad, and
SAM. Table <a href="#A1.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ A.1 Vision Panel: Architectures, Optimizers, and Recipes ‣ Appendix A Experimental Coverage and Protocol Details ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> gives the shared recipe, the optimizer
definitions, and the learning rate of every cell together with the
parameter count of each architecture.</p>
</div>

<div class="ltx_flex_figure ltx_flex_table">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1">
<p id="A1.T1.1" class="ltx_p ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center">(a) Shared recipe</p></div><div class="ltx_flex_break"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1">
<table id="A1.T1.2" class="ltx_tabular ltx_figure_panel ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">

<td id="A1.T1.2.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_tt">Setting</td></tr>
<tr id="A1.T1.2.2" class="ltx_tr">

<td id="A1.T1.2.2.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_t">CIFAR-10 (full 50k train / 10k test); CIFAR-100 only in the transfer family</td></tr>
<tr id="A1.T1.2.3" class="ltx_tr">

<td id="A1.T1.2.3.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left">cross-entropy; batch size 128 everywhere</td></tr>

<p id="A1.T1.7" class="ltx_p ltx_figure_panel">All <math id="A1.T1.m50" class="ltx_Math" alttext="30" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>30</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">30</annotation></semantics></math> cells are trained from scratch under the shared recipe of panel (a) with
seed <math id="A1.T1.m51" class="ltx_Math" alttext="42" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>42</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">42</annotation></semantics></math>. Parameter counts are for the <math id="A1.T1.m52" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10</annotation></semantics></math>-class heads; ViT-mid has
<math id="A1.T1.m53" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2{,}875{,}812" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2,875,812</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2{,}875{,}812</annotation></semantics></math> parameters with the <math id="A1.T1.m54" class="ltx_Math" alttext="100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>100</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">100</annotation></semantics></math>-class head used in the transfer family.
Most cells take the model-default learning rate; a few were hand-tuned, including
ViT with SAM (<math id="A1.T1.m55" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.05</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.05</annotation></semantics></math>) and ViT-mid with SAM (<math id="A1.T1.m56" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.025" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.025</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.025</annotation></semantics></math>).
<sup id="A1.T1.7.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A1.T1.7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">s</span></sup> Cell additionally re-trained with seeds <math id="A1.T1.m58" class="ltx_Math" alttext="43" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>43</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">43</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.T1.m59" class="ltx_Math" alttext="44" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>44</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">44</annotation></semantics></math>.
<sup id="A1.T1.7.2" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A1.T1.7.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">†</span></sup> Those two SAM re-runs used the model-default learning rate
(<math id="A1.T1.m61" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.T1.m62" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.05</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.05</annotation></semantics></math>), twice the hand-tuned seed-<math id="A1.T1.m63" class="ltx_Math" alttext="42" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>42</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">42</annotation></semantics></math> value, so these two cells are
not learning-rate-matched across seeds.</p></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 1: </span>Vision panel: shared recipe, optimizer definitions, and per-cell
learning rates. <span id="A1.T1.11" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(a)</span> the recipe held fixed across every run in this
appendix; <span id="A1.T1.12" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(b)</span> the six training configurations of the panel;
<span id="A1.T1.13" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(c)</span> the five architectures with their parameter counts and the
learning rate of each cell.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A1.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">All cells train from scratch for <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="50" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>50</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">50</annotation></semantics></math> epochs at batch size <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>128</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">128</annotation></semantics></math> under a
cosine schedule stepped once per epoch, with seed <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="42" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>42</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">42</annotation></semantics></math>, and weights are
recorded at every epoch boundary. That epoch-level snapshot cadence is
what sets the probe time step on this side. Most cells take the
model-default learning rate; the hand-tuned exceptions are listed in the
table. AlexNet is the one architecture with a different input pipeline,
since it resizes to <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>128</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">128</annotation></semantics></math> pixels and trains without augmentation.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.2 </span>Additional Run Families</h3>

<div id="A1.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Around the panel, six further families vary one ingredient at a time
while holding the shared recipe fixed
(Table <a href="#A1.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ A.2 Additional Run Families ‣ Appendix A Experimental Coverage and Protocol Details ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>). Two of them supply the controlled
comparisons of Section 4.4: a Muon arm over the same five
architectures, and a weight-decay and momentum dose ladder on plain SGD.
The remaining families support the robustness and calibration checks:
seed replicates on five cells, a transfer-dynamics family between
CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, and a probe-calibration batch covering a schedule
zoo, basin slices, a learning-rate dose ladder, and a blind audit whose
configurations were withheld from the analysis side. The corpus is <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="139" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>139</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">139</annotation></semantics></math>
training runs and one frozen source checkpoint.</p>
</div>

<span id="A1.T2.1.7.3.1.1" class="ltx_p">Plain SGD, seed <math id="A1.T2.m32" class="ltx_Math" alttext="42" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>42</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">42</annotation></semantics></math>, CIFAR-10 statistics pinned. A <math id="A1.T2.m33" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>16</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16</annotation></semantics></math>-run schedule zoo
(ResNet and ViT-mid over linear, two step schedules, exponential,
warmup-cosine and cosine-with-floor, two ResNet constant-rate runs, a
<math id="A1.T2.m34" class="ltx_Math" alttext="100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>100</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">100</annotation></semantics></math>-epoch cosine run and a basin anneal); <math id="A1.T2.m35" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10</annotation></semantics></math> basin slices (early and late
basins crossed with five constant rates, <math id="A1.T2.m36" class="ltx_Math" alttext="12" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>12</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">12</annotation></semantics></math> epochs); a <math id="A1.T2.m37" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5</annotation></semantics></math>-run
learning-rate dose ladder (<math id="A1.T2.m38" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times\{\tfrac{1}{25},\tfrac{1}{10},\tfrac{1}{2},2,4\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>25</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>10</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times\{\tfrac{1}{25},\tfrac{1}{10},\tfrac{1}{2},2,4\}</annotation></semantics></math> of base <math id="A1.T2.m39" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.025" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.025</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.025</annotation></semantics></math>); two stationary continuations; and a <math id="A1.T2.m40" class="ltx_Math" alttext="12" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>12</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">12</annotation></semantics></math>-run blind
audit whose configurations were withheld from the analysis side.</span>

throughout Section 4.1 to Section 4.3; the Muon
arm and the dose ladders supply the controlled comparisons of
Section 4.4; the remaining families support the robustness and
calibration checks. The two collapsed momentum runs are kept on disk and
excluded from every readout.</figcaption>

<div id="A1.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Two runs in the momentum ladder collapsed and are excluded from every
readout while being kept on disk: MLP at momentum <math id="A1.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.95" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.95</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.95</annotation></semantics></math>, which ends at
<math id="A1.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.170" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.170</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.170</annotation></semantics></math> test accuracy, and AlexNet at momentum <math id="A1.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.95" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.95</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.95</annotation></semantics></math>, which ends at
<math id="A1.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.100</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.100</annotation></semantics></math>, the chance level for ten classes. Neither contributes to the
momentum comparisons.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.3 </span>Pretraining Checkpoint Coverage</h3>

<div id="A1.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A1.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ A.3 Pretraining Checkpoint Coverage ‣ Appendix A Experimental Coverage and Protocol Details ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> lists the released checkpoint series we
analyze, and Figure <a href="#A1.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ A.3 Pretraining Checkpoint Coverage ‣ Appendix A Experimental Coverage and Protocol Details ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> places the measured
anchor domain on the training-step axis of each size. The main panel is
Pythia-70M, 160M, and 410M. The extended sizes 14M, 31M, 1B, and 1.4B are
processed under the identical protocol. Six of the seven sizes
enter the cross-scale readings of
Appendix <a href="#A6" title="Appendix F Pythia Scale Extensions ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F</span></a>; 1B is covered by the coverage
accounting here but is excluded from every cross-scale reading, on the three
grounds given there.</p>
</div>

<p id="A1.T3.3" class="ltx_p ltx_figure_panel">“Total” counts pure parameters of the released fp16 weights, with no buffers;
“non-embedding” excludes the untied input and output embeddings (vocabulary
<math id="A1.T3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="50{,}304" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>50,304</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">50{,}304</annotation></semantics></math>). The 70M and 160M values are read from the verified reference card;
the five remaining sizes are recomputed from the on-disk group sizes, by a method
that reproduces the reference card exactly on 70M. The extended sizes were
processed at a second compute site under the identical engine and protocol, with
per-size equivalence gates passing at zero maximum relative error (<math id="A1.T3.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1260" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1260</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1260</annotation></semantics></math> units at
14M and 31M, <math id="A1.T3.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4824" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4824</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4824</annotation></semantics></math> at 410M and 1.4B, <math id="A1.T3.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3240" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3240</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3240</annotation></semantics></math> at 1B); the gate tables carry
non-empty exemption counts for degenerate units, and every non-exempt row passes.
Anchors are steps <math id="A1.T3.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="7000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>7000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7000</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A1.T3.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="129000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>129000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">129000</annotation></semantics></math> at spacing <math id="A1.T3.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1000</annotation></semantics></math>, and each anchor produces
one panel and one segment shard.</p></div><div class="ltx_flex_break"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1">
<p id="A1.T3.4" class="ltx_p ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center">(b) Public telemetry and evaluation provenance</p></div><div class="ltx_flex_break"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1">
