<p id="A1.T3.6" class="ltx_p ltx_figure_panel">All telemetry comes from the public training project of the checkpoint release, in
the run group matching the released weights, with configurations cross-checked item
by item against the published training configurations. The 1B chain starts at step
<math id="A1.T3.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2001" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2001</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2001</annotation></semantics></math>; steps <math id="A1.T3.m26" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A1.T3.m27" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2000</annotation></semantics></math> are missing and the analysis domain starts at <math id="A1.T3.m28" class="ltx_Math" alttext="7000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>7000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7000</annotation></semantics></math>, so
the gap is outside it. Official zero-shot evaluations come from the release
repository and were produced by an older harness, so only within-harness trends are
read from them.</p></div><div class="ltx_flex_break"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1">
<p id="A1.T3.7" class="ltx_p ltx_figure_panel"><sup id="A1.T3.7.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A1.T3.7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">†</span></sup> <span id="A1.T3.7.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Pythia-1B checkpoint defect.</span> Revision <span id="A1.T3.7.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">step116000</span> of
the 1B series has wrong content upstream: it is the only 1B revision exported by a
different release pipeline, and tensor forensics place it as an inserted state from
a different run, with <math id="A1.T3.m30" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{115\mathrm{k}}\approx w_{117\mathrm{k}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mn>115</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><mo>≈</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mn>117</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{115\mathrm{k}}\approx w_{117\mathrm{k}}</annotation></semantics></math>. The defect dates
from the first weight upload and is not repairable downstream. Affected cells are
masked at read time, by probe family: base-anchor rows at <math id="A1.T3.m31" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a{=}116" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>116</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a{=}116</annotation></semantics></math>k for all <math id="A1.T3.m32" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>;
history-window anchors <math id="A1.T3.m33" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a{=}116" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>116</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a{=}116</annotation></semantics></math>k to <math id="A1.T3.m34" class="ltx_Math" alttext="121" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>121</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">121</annotation></semantics></math>k for all <math id="A1.T3.m35" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>; the future-endpoint
cells <math id="A1.T3.m36" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(a,\tau)\in\{(115\mathrm{k},1),(114\mathrm{k},2),(113\mathrm{k},3),(111\mathrm{k},5),(106\mathrm{k},10),(102\mathrm{k},14)\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>115</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>114</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>113</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>111</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>106</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>10</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>102</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>14</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(a,\tau)\in\{(115\mathrm{k},1),(114\mathrm{k},2),(113\mathrm{k},3),(111\mathrm{k},5),(106\mathrm{k},10),(102\mathrm{k},14)\}</annotation></semantics></math>; and the
<span id="A1.T3.7.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">step116000</span> row of the embedding-spectrum series. Public telemetry and the
official evaluations are unaffected, since neither is derived from local
checkpoints.</p></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 3: </span>Pretraining checkpoint coverage. <span id="A1.T3.11" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(a)</span> parameter counts,
architecture, and on-disk coverage, split into the main panel and the
extended set reported in Appendix <a href="#A6" title="Appendix F Pythia Scale Extensions ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F</span></a>;
<span id="A1.T3.12" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(b)</span> public telemetry and evaluation provenance, including the
splice checks for the two series whose released telemetry is assembled from
more than one run. The 1B rows carry the <span id="A1.T3.13" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">step116000</span> checkpoint
defect and its masking windows.</figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="A1.F1" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2608.15483v1/appS5_pythia_coverage_map.svg" id="A1.F1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:698/295;" width="698" height="295"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 1: </span>Checkpoint and anchor coverage across the pretraining scales.
Each row is one model scale on a shared training-step axis, with tokens on
the top axis at <math id="A1.F1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2{,}097{,}152" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2,097,152</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2{,}097{,}152</annotation></semantics></math> per step. Ticks give the <math id="A1.F1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="154" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>154</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">154</annotation></semantics></math> public
checkpoint revisions, released on the schedule <math id="A1.F1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0,1,2,4,\ldots,512" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>512</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0,1,2,4,\ldots,512</annotation></semantics></math> and
every <math id="A1.F1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>k steps thereafter up to step <math id="A1.F1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="143" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>143</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">143</annotation></semantics></math>k. Bars give the anchor domain
actually measured, <math id="A1.F1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="123" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>123</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">123</annotation></semantics></math> anchors on a <math id="A1.F1.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>k grid spanning <math id="A1.F1.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>7</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7</annotation></semantics></math>k to <math id="A1.F1.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="129" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>129</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">129</annotation></semantics></math>k for
every scale. The domain is trimmed at both ends for protocol reasons rather
than for data availability: the head drops the warmup phase and leaves room
for the backward history window, and the tail reserves a complete future
window for the longest horizon (<math id="A1.F1.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="143\mathrm{k}-14\mathrm{k}=129\mathrm{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>143</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>14</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>129</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">143\mathrm{k}-14\mathrm{k}=129\mathrm{k}</annotation></semantics></math>
at <math id="A1.F1.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau{=}14" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>14</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau{=}14</annotation></semantics></math>). Lines give the span of public training-loss telemetry, and
the two smallest scales carry no line because no public run exists for
them. Triangles mark splices where the released telemetry is assembled from
more than one run. Hatching on the 1B row marks the step-<math id="A1.F1.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="116" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>116</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">116</annotation></semantics></math>k checkpoint
defect and the anchors masked because of it, with short ticks at the
horizon-specific future endpoints; the telemetry line and the official
evaluations are unaffected by the masking.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A1.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Checkpoints are released every <math id="A1.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}000</annotation></semantics></math> steps after a dense early grid,
giving <math id="A1.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="154" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>154</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">154</annotation></semantics></math> revisions up to step <math id="A1.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="143{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>143,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">143{,}000</annotation></semantics></math>. We evaluate <math id="A1.SS3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="123" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>123</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">123</annotation></semantics></math> anchors
on a <math id="A1.SS3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}000</annotation></semantics></math>-step grid spanning steps <math id="A1.SS3.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="7{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>7,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7{,}000</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A1.SS3.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="129{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>129,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">129{,}000</annotation></semantics></math>. Both
edges are protocol choices rather than data limits. The lower edge keeps
the five-checkpoint history window, which reaches back to step <math id="A1.SS3.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2{,}000</annotation></semantics></math>,
clear of the <math id="A1.SS3.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}430" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,430</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}430</annotation></semantics></math>-step learning-rate warmup. The upper edge leaves a
complete future window for the longest horizon, since
<math id="A1.SS3.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="143{,}000-14{,}000=129{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>143,000</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>14,000</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>129,000</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">143{,}000-14{,}000=129{,}000</annotation></semantics></math> at <math id="A1.SS3.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau=14" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>14</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau=14</annotation></semantics></math> checkpoints.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Public training-loss telemetry and the official zero-shot evaluations are
used only as external context, and their provenance is recorded in panel
(b) of the table, including the two sizes whose released telemetry is
assembled from more than one run. One size carries a checkpoint defect:
revision <span id="A1.SS3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">step116000</span> of the 1B series is wrong upstream, and the
cells whose history or future window touches it are masked at read time.
The masking windows are listed in the table footnote and are applied
wherever 1B appears.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.4 </span>Measurement Clocks, Anchors, and Seeds</h3>

<section id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Clocks.</h5>

<div id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">One probe step is one epoch on the vision side and one released
checkpoint on the pretraining side. A checkpoint step spans <math id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}000</annotation></semantics></math>
optimization steps, or about <math id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2.10</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.10</annotation></semantics></math> billion tokens at <math id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2{,}097{,}152" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2,097,152</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2{,}097{,}152</annotation></semantics></math>
tokens per step. The two clocks index different amounts of optimization,
which is why cross-regime readings compare the ordering within a matched
trajectory rather than levels across regimes.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Anchors and windows.</h5>

<div id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Both regimes use horizon <math id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau=5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau=5</annotation></semantics></math> and history length <math id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{\mathrm{past}}=5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>past</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{\mathrm{past}}=5</annotation></semantics></math> unless
stated otherwise, with the reference direction <math id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta w_{a-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta w_{a-1}</annotation></semantics></math> and the future
target <math id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta w_{a}^{(\tau)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>w</mi><mi>a</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta w_{a}^{(\tau)}</annotation></semantics></math> as defined in Section 3. Vision
probes are evaluated at anchor epochs <math id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{5,10,20,30,40\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>30</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>40</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{5,10,20,30,40\}</annotation></semantics></math>. An anchor is
admissible only when its full history window and its full future window
lie inside the recorded trajectory, which is what fixes the edges of the
pretraining anchor domain above. The pretraining panel additionally
records <math id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau\in\{1,2,3,5,10,14\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>14</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau\in\{1,2,3,5,10,14\}</annotation></semantics></math> so that horizon sensitivity can be
read from the same shards.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Seeds and determinism.</h5>

<div id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The panel trains at seed <math id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="42" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>42</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">42</annotation></semantics></math>, with replicates at <math id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="43" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>43</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">43</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="44" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>44</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">44</annotation></semantics></math> on the
five cells listed in Table <a href="#A1.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ A.2 Additional Run Families ‣ Appendix A Experimental Coverage and Protocol Details ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>. On the measurement
side, three seeds are fixed and shared across every lane so that a
recomputation reproduces the same numbers: the rank-selection sample
(Appendix <a href="#A2.SS3" title="B.3 Rank Selection ‣ Appendix B Probe Conventions, Calibration, and Robustness ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.3</span></a>), the per-layer group subsample
(Appendix <a href="#A2.SS1" title="B.1 Measurement Units and Grouping Conventions ‣ Appendix B Probe Conventions, Calibration, and Robustness ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.1</span></a>), and the permutation-null draws
(Appendix <a href="#A2.SS4" title="B.4 Null Generation and the Calibrated Readout ‣ Appendix B Probe Conventions, Calibration, and Robustness ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.4</span></a>), whose seed is composed from the
draw index, anchor, layer, and segment.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Compute.</h5>

<div id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The vision corpus was trained on a single workstation with two NVIDIA RTX
A6000 GPUs (<math id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="48" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>48</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">48</annotation></semantics></math> GB each), one run per GPU. Median wall-clock for a
<math id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="50" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>50</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">50</annotation></semantics></math>-epoch run, taken over each architecture’s optimizer cells, is about <math id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="12" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>12</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">12</annotation></semantics></math>
minutes for the MLP, <math id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>15</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">15</annotation></semantics></math> for ViT, <math id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="22" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>22</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">22</annotation></semantics></math> for AlexNet, <math id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="23" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>23</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">23</annotation></semantics></math> for ViT-mid, and
<math id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="38" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>38</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">38</annotation></semantics></math> for the ResNet; the slowest single run is AlexNet under Muon at about
<math id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4.8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.8</annotation></semantics></math> hours, where the orthogonalization step dominates on the largest weight
matrices. Probe and panel computation is CPU-only and in double precision, on
a <math id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>16</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16</annotation></semantics></math>-core machine with <math id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>128</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">128</annotation></semantics></math> GB of memory: one pretraining anchor of the
full panel protocol, including its permutation nulls, takes about <math id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10</annotation></semantics></math> minutes
at 160M and <math id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="25" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>25</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">25</annotation></semantics></math> at 410M. The panels for the two largest sizes ran on
large-memory CPU nodes (<math id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>64</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">64</annotation></semantics></math> cores, <math id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math> TB) with anchors processed in <math id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math> to
<math id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10</annotation></semantics></math> parallel lanes, at roughly <math id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="17" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>17</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">17</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="19" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>19</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">19</annotation></semantics></math> hours per size; the
embedding-spectrum sweep is checkpoint-bound, at seconds to about a minute per
revision. The stored checkpoint packs occupy <math id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="24" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>24</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">24</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="54" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>54</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">54</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="126" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>126</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">126</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="311" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>311</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">311</annotation></semantics></math>, and
<math id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="436" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>436</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">436</annotation></semantics></math> GB for 70M, 160M, 410M, 1B, and 1.4B. Software: Python 3 with PyTorch,
used only to deserialize checkpoints, together with NumPy, SciPy, and pandas.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix B </span>Probe Conventions, Calibration, and Robustness</h2>

<div id="A2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Section 3 defers five implementation details to this appendix:
the exact predictor constructions, the rank-selection rule, the null
generation procedure, the grouping rules, and the numerical conventions.
Appendices <a href="#A2.SS1" title="B.1 Measurement Units and Grouping Conventions ‣ Appendix B Probe Conventions, Calibration, and Robustness ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.1</span></a> to <a href="#A2.SS5" title="B.5 Numerical Conventions and the Sign Rule ‣ Appendix B Probe Conventions, Calibration, and Robustness ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.5</span></a> give
them, in that order. Appendix <a href="#A2.SS6" title="B.6 Grouping Sensitivity and Within-Family Checks ‣ Appendix B Probe Conventions, Calibration, and Robustness ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.6</span></a> then reports what
the group-level readouts do when the grouping convention is changed,
together with the full versions of the within-family comparisons
summarized in Section 4.1, and
Appendix <a href="#A2.SS7" title="B.7 Reporting Discipline ‣ Appendix B Probe Conventions, Calibration, and Robustness ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.7</span></a> states the reporting rules that
follow from those measurements.</p>
</div>
<section id="A2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.1 </span>Measurement Units and Grouping Conventions</h3>

<div id="A2.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Every group-level readout in this paper is conditional on a rule that
partitions a tensor’s scalars into measurement units. We call such a rule a
<em id="A2.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">cut</em>. Tables <a href="#A2.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ B.1 Measurement Units and Grouping Conventions ‣ Appendix B Probe Conventions, Calibration, and Robustness ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> and <a href="#A2.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ B.1 Measurement Units and Grouping Conventions ‣ Appendix B Probe Conventions, Calibration, and Robustness ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>
list all cuts used in the paper together with their group sizes and their
status with respect to chance passing.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A2.T4" class="ltx_table">
<table id="A2.T4.1" class="ltx_tabular ltx_align_middle">
<tbody class="ltx_tbody">
<tr id="A2.T4.1.1" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A2.T4.1.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_tt" style="padding:0.75pt 4.0pt;">Cut</td>
<td id="A2.T4.1.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_tt" style="padding:0.75pt 4.0pt;">
<span id="A2.T4.1.1.2.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:86.0pt;">
<span id="A2.T4.1.1.2.1.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left">One group is</span>
</span></td>
<td id="A2.T4.1.1.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_tt" style="padding:0.75pt 4.0pt;"><math id="A2.T4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="A2.T4.1.1.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_tt" style="padding:0.75pt 4.0pt;">
<span id="A2.T4.1.1.4.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top">
<span id="A2.T4.1.1.4.1.1" class="ltx_p">What it reads</span>
</span></td>
<td id="A2.T4.1.1.5" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_tt" style="padding:0.75pt 4.0pt;">
<span id="A2.T4.1.1.5.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:96.1pt;">
<span id="A2.T4.1.1.5.1.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left">Chance status at <math id="A2.T4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta{=}0.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta{=}0.7</annotation></semantics></math></span>
</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A2.T4.1.2" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A2.T4.1.2.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_t" style="padding:0.75pt 4.0pt;" colspan="5"><em id="A2.T4.1.2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Flat protocol, the main measurement convention</em></td></tr>
<tr id="A2.T4.1.3" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A2.T4.1.3.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left" style="padding:0.75pt 4.0pt;">flat <math id="A2.T4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K{=}16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K{=}16</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="A2.T4.1.3.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top" style="padding:0.75pt 4.0pt;">
<span id="A2.T4.1.3.2.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:86.0pt;">
<span id="A2.T4.1.3.2.1.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left"><math id="A2.T4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>16</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16</annotation></semantics></math> contiguous scalars of the row-major flattened tensor</span>
</span></td>
<td id="A2.T4.1.3.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left" style="padding:0.75pt 4.0pt;"><math id="A2.T4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>16</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="A2.T4.1.3.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left" style="padding:0.75pt 4.0pt;">
<span id="A2.T4.1.3.4.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top">
<span id="A2.T4.1.3.4.1.1" class="ltx_p">Between-group ESA dispersion sits at the binomial sampling floor
(<math id="A2.T4.m6" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.1\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.1</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.1\times</annotation></semantics></math>, median over <math id="A2.T4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="30" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>30</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">30</annotation></semantics></math> cells), so blocks are statistically
homogeneous. Bulk group-level FRR hugs the chance floor (median excess
<math id="A2.T4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".014" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>.014</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.014</annotation></semantics></math>, against <math id="A2.T4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".148" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>.148</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.148</annotation></semantics></math> for the auxiliary class). Cross-architecture
ordering claims do not survive recutting.</span>
</span></td>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 4: </span>Grouping conventions on the vision panel. <math id="A2.T4.m83" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math> is the number of
scalars per group. “Immune” means the membership-resample null passes
<math id="A2.T4.m84" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta{=}0.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta{=}0.7</annotation></semantics></math> at a rate near zero, so the raw pass fractions carry a negligible chance contribution. The flat <math id="A2.T4.m85" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K{=}16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K{=}16</annotation></semantics></math> protocol is the one cut where a large share of
raw passes is chance, which is what motivated the calibrated readout
<math id="A2.T4.m86" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{LRGF}_{\mathrm{cal}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>LRGF</mi><mi>cal</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{LRGF}_{\mathrm{cal}}</annotation></semantics></math>. Levels are not comparable across cuts,
since group sizes and chance floors differ, so every level claim in this
paper names its cut. Structural and magnitude readouts are pooled over the
<math id="A2.T4.m87" class="ltx_Math" alttext="18" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>18</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">18</annotation></semantics></math> recipe cells of the group-level lanes and anchors <math id="A2.T4.m88" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A2.T4.m89" class="ltx_Math" alttext="40" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>40</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">40</annotation></semantics></math>.</figcaption>
</figure>

<span id="A2.T5.1.5.4.1.1" class="ltx_p">Loses to head grouping on <math id="A2.T5.m34" class="ltx_Math" alttext="qkv" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">qkv</annotation></semantics></math> at step <math id="A2.T5.m35" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10</annotation></semantics></math>k
(<math id="A2.T5.m36" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{LRGF}_{\mathrm{cal}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>LRGF</mi><mi>cal</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{LRGF}_{\mathrm{cal}}</annotation></semantics></math> <math id="A2.T5.m37" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".333/.389" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>.333</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>.389</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.333/.389</annotation></semantics></math> against <math id="A2.T5.m38" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".104/.069" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>.104</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>.069</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.104/.069</annotation></semantics></math> at 70M
and 160M); MLP sensitivity is local (70M layer 5 mid-training, about
<math id="A2.T5.m39" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="3\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3\times</annotation></semantics></math>) with <math id="A2.T5.m40" class="ltx_Math" alttext="7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>7</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="A2.T5.m41" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10</annotation></semantics></math> grid cells negative; at most <math id="A2.T5.m42" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.12\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.12</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.12\%</annotation></semantics></math> on
absolute <math id="A2.T5.m43" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> across five sizes.</span>
</span></td>
<td id="A2.T5.1.5.5" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_left ltx_align_top" style="padding:0.75pt 4.0pt;">
<span id="A2.T5.1.5.5.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:96.1pt;">
<span id="A2.T5.1.5.5.1.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left">Null shared with the positional cut (grouping-independent).</span>
</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A2.T5.1.6" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A2.T5.1.6.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left" style="padding:0.75pt 4.0pt;">MLP input half</td>
<td id="A2.T5.1.6.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top" style="padding:0.75pt 4.0pt;">
<span id="A2.T5.1.6.2.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:86.0pt;">
<span id="A2.T5.1.6.2.1.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left">neuron input row (<math id="A2.T5.m44" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{\mathrm{in}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>in</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{\mathrm{in}}</annotation></semantics></math>)</span>
</span></td>
<td id="A2.T5.1.6.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left" style="padding:0.75pt 4.0pt;"><math id="A2.T5.m45" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{\mathrm{model}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>model</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{\mathrm{model}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="A2.T5.1.6.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left" style="padding:0.75pt 4.0pt;">
<span id="A2.T5.1.6.4.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top">
<span id="A2.T5.1.6.4.1.1" class="ltx_p">Reads near zero (mean <math id="A2.T5.m46" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.04\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.04</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.04\%</annotation></semantics></math>).</span>
</span></td>

</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A2.T5.1.7" class="ltx_tr">

<td id="A2.T5.1.7.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_bb" style="padding:0.75pt 4.0pt;">

<span id="A2.T5.1.7.4.1.1" class="ltx_p">Real emergence carried by the deepest layer: the 70M layer-5 wave rises
from <math id="A2.T5.m50" class="ltx_Math" alttext="64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>64</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">64</annotation></semantics></math>k to a peak of <math id="A2.T5.m51" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5.4\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5.4</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5.4\%</annotation></semantics></math> at <math id="A2.T5.m52" class="ltx_Math" alttext="96" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>96</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">96</annotation></semantics></math>k. Across five model sizes the
output half is the only MLP cut with signal (peaks <math id="A2.T5.m53" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.8</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A2.T5.m54" class="ltx_Math" alttext="15.7\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>15.7</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">15.7\%</annotation></semantics></math>),
with the input half and the magnitude cut near zero.</span>

</span></td></tr>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 5: </span>Grouping conventions on the Pythia side. All Pythia readings are
registered as correspondences and are not used to certify one another.
Column conventions follow Table <a href="#A2.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ B.1 Measurement Units and Grouping Conventions ‣ Appendix B Probe Conventions, Calibration, and Robustness ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>. The last two
rows are the recut used for the granularity ladder in
Appendix <a href="#A2.SS6" title="B.6 Grouping Sensitivity and Within-Family Checks ‣ Appendix B Probe Conventions, Calibration, and Robustness ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.6</span></a>.</figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Flat <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K{=}16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K{=}16</annotation></semantics></math>, the main protocol.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Each tensor’s parameter vector is flattened in row-major order and split
into consecutive disjoint blocks of <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K{=}16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K{=}16</annotation></semantics></math> scalars. A trailing block
shorter than <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> is dropped, and a tensor holding fewer than <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> scalars
carries no group at all; on the vision panel this removes only the
ten-parameter classifier bias of each model. The cut is cheap, uniform in
group size, and identical across architectures, which is what keeps the
group size, and therefore the chance geometry, matched in cross-architecture
comparisons. It is not aligned to the architecture. In row-major layout a
flat block of a convolutional tensor is approximately one <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3{\times}3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3{\times}3</annotation></semantics></math>
kernel, whereas for a feature-dimension linear tensor it is <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>16</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16</annotation></semantics></math> adjacent
input dimensions with no functional identity, and the two readings are not
the same measurement.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Structural cuts (vision).</h5>

<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Structural cuts take the unit from the architecture instead of from the
memory layout. For the ViT family a group is one head’s q, k, or v row
block of the fused <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="qkv" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">qkv</annotation></semantics></math> tensor, one head’s projection rows, or one hidden
neuron’s fan-in and fan-out concatenated. For ResNet a group is one output
channel’s full <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3{\times}3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3{\times}3</annotation></semantics></math> kernel stack, or one <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{\times}1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{\times}1</annotation></semantics></math> convolution
row. Group sizes run from <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="27" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>27</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">27</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="12{,}544" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>12,544</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">12{,}544</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Magnitude cut (vision).</h5>

<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Within each tensor, coordinates are ranked by the <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> norm of their
pre-anchor update window and split into <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>16</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16</annotation></semantics></math> equal bins. The ranking reads
only pre-anchor history, so the cut is causal and carries no information
from the target window.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Pythia segments.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Each transformer layer contributes four segments. The fused <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[3d,d]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[3d,d]</annotation></semantics></math> <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="qkv" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">qkv</annotation></semantics></math>
tensor is stored head-major, and one group is the block belonging to one
head and one of q, k, v, of size <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{\mathrm{head}}\,d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>head</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{\mathrm{head}}\,d</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="32{,}768" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>32,768</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32{,}768</annotation></semantics></math> at
70M); groups are enumerated part-major, that is, all q blocks, then all k,
then all v. In <span id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">attention.dense</span> the input axis carries the
concatenated head outputs, so one group is one head’s column block. In the
MLP one group is a neuron pair: row <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math> of <span id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">dense_h_to_4h</span>
joined with column <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math> of <span id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">dense_4h_to_h</span>, of size <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2d</annotation></semantics></math>. In the
vector segment each vector parameter is its own group. The two embedding
matrices form separate segments and stay outside every aggregation
(Appendix <a href="#A3.SS3" title="C.3 Pythia: Segment Taxonomy and the Vector Segment ‣ Appendix C Spatial Localization: the Auxiliary–Bulk Partition ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.3</span></a>). Two finer conventions are used for
the granularity studies in Appendix <a href="#A2.SS6" title="B.6 Grouping Sensitivity and Within-Family Checks ‣ Appendix B Probe Conventions, Calibration, and Robustness ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.6</span></a>: one <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{qkv}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>W</mi><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{qkv}</annotation></semantics></math>
row (<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D{=}d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D{=}d</annotation></semantics></math>), and the two MLP halves taken separately.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Group subsampling.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Layers with more than <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}500" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,500</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}500</annotation></semantics></math> groups are subsampled to that cap before
group-level statistics are formed, with a seed derived from the layer name
so that the same groups are drawn on any recomputation. Tensor-level and
pooled readouts use all groups.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.2 </span>Predictor Constructions</h3>

<div id="A2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">All three predictors read only the <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{\mathrm{past}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>past</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{\mathrm{past}}</annotation></semantics></math> one-step updates before the
anchor. For a unit <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math> write the history columns as <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{1},\ldots,h_{m}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>m</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{1},\ldots,h_{m}</annotation></semantics></math> with
<math id="A2.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m=n_{\mathrm{past}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>past</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m=n_{\mathrm{past}}</annotation></semantics></math>, so that <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{m}=\Delta w_{a-1,S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{m}=\Delta w_{a-1,S}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<section id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Inertia.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widehat{f}_{\mathrm{in}}=\tau\,h_{m}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>in</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>m</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widehat{f}_{\mathrm{in}}=\tau\,h_{m}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Linear trend.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Per coordinate, an affine model <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{s}\approx\alpha+\beta s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{s}\approx\alpha+\beta s</annotation></semantics></math> is fitted by
least squares over <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s=0,\ldots,m-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s=0,\ldots,m-1</annotation></semantics></math>, and the fitted updates are summed over
the next <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> steps,</p>
<table id="A2.E1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widehat{f}_{\mathrm{lin}}=\sum_{q=0}^{\tau-1}\bigl(\alpha+\beta(m+q)\bigr)=\tau\alpha+\beta\sum_{q=0}^{\tau-1}(m+q)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>lin</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></munderover><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></munderover><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widehat{f}_{\mathrm{lin}}=\sum_{q=0}^{\tau-1}\bigl(\alpha+\beta(m+q)\bigr)=\tau\alpha+\beta\sum_{q=0}^{\tau-1}(m+q).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(1)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">The fit is on updates rather than on weights, so the output is a
displacement and not an extrapolated checkpoint.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">DMD.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The construction has three steps.
<em id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">(i) Standardization.</em> Each coordinate row of the history is divided
by its standard deviation over the <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math> columns. Rows whose standard
deviation falls below <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{-30}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>30</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{-30}</annotation></semantics></math> are left unscaled, and any unit containing
such a row is predicted as zero. Write <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{H}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>H</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{H}</annotation></semantics></math> for the standardized
history.
<em id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">(ii) Fit.</em> With <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X=[\tilde{h}_{1},\ldots,\tilde{h}_{m-1}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X=[\tilde{h}_{1},\ldots,\tilde{h}_{m-1}]</annotation></semantics></math> and
<math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y=[\tilde{h}_{2},\ldots,\tilde{h}_{m}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>m</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y=[\tilde{h}_{2},\ldots,\tilde{h}_{m}]</annotation></semantics></math>, take the thin SVD
<math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X=U\Sigma V^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>V</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X=U\Sigma V^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math>, truncate to <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=\min(|S|,m-1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>min</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>S</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=\min(|S|,m-1)</annotation></semantics></math>, which is four columns
under the default protocol, and form the reduced map</p>
<table id="A2.E2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{A}=U_{r}^{\top}\,Y\,V_{r}\,\Sigma_{r}^{-1}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>A</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>U</mi><mi>r</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mi>r</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{A}=U_{r}^{\top}\,Y\,V_{r}\,\Sigma_{r}^{-1},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(2)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">with singular values below <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{-10}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{-10}</annotation></semantics></math> inverted to zero.
<em id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.2.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">(iii) Rollout.</em> Eigendecompose <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{A}=W\Lambda W^{-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>A</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>W</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>W</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{A}=W\Lambda W^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math>, lift the
eigenvectors to <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Phi=U_{r}W" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>W</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Phi=U_{r}W</annotation></semantics></math>, and expand the last standardized update in
them, <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b=\Phi^{\dagger}\tilde{h}_{m}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mo>†</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>m</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b=\Phi^{\dagger}\tilde{h}_{m}</annotation></semantics></math>. The <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>-step prediction is</p>
<table id="A2.E3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widehat{f}_{\mathrm{DMD}}=\Re\Bigl\{\Phi\Bigl(\sum_{k=1}^{\tau}\Lambda^{k}\Bigr)b\Bigr\}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>DMD</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℜ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">(</mo><mrow><munderover><mo lspace="0em" movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>τ</mi></munderover><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mi>k</mi></msup></mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widehat{f}_{\mathrm{DMD}}=\Re\Bigl\{\Phi\Bigl(\sum_{k=1}^{\tau}\Lambda^{k}\Bigr)b\Bigr\},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(3)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.3" class="ltx_p">with each coordinate rescaled by the standard deviation removed in step
(i). Summing <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Lambda^{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mi>k</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Lambda^{k}</annotation></semantics></math> over <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=1,\ldots,\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=1,\ldots,\tau</annotation></semantics></math> instead of applying
<math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Lambda^{\tau}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mi>τ</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Lambda^{\tau}</annotation></semantics></math> is what makes the output the cumulative displacement over
the horizon, which is the quantity the target <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta w_{a,S}^{(\tau)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta w_{a,S}^{(\tau)}</annotation></semantics></math>
measures.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Containment in the recent-history span.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Because <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Phi=U_{r}W" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>W</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Phi=U_{r}W</annotation></semantics></math>, the prediction lies in the column space of <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{r}</annotation></semantics></math>, and
the row standardization cancels exactly between the fit in step (ii) and
the rescaling in step (iii). The DMD prediction therefore lies in the span
of the first <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m-1</annotation></semantics></math> raw history columns, which is contained in the span the
FRR projector retains whenever that projector covers the full history
rank. This is the containment behind reading FRR as the directional
headroom available to a predictor built from the recent history, as in
Section 4.1: the residual fraction that FRR measures
bounds how well any vector drawn from that span can align with the
realized displacement.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.3 </span>Rank Selection</h3>

<div id="A2.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The FRR projector retains a rank chosen by the Gavish–Donoho optimal hard
threshold. For a unit whose history matrix has singular values
<math id="A2.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{1}\geq\cdots\geq s_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo rspace="0.1389em">≥</mo><mo lspace="0.1389em" rspace="0.1389em">⋯</mo><mo lspace="0.1389em">≥</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{1}\geq\cdots\geq s_{p}</annotation></semantics></math> and aspect ratio
<math id="A2.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta=\min(|S|,m)/\max(|S|,m)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>min</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>S</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mi>max</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>S</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta=\min(|S|,m)/\max(|S|,m)</annotation></semantics></math>, the threshold is</p>
<table id="A2.E4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\begin{split}\theta_{\mathrm{GD}}&amp;=\omega(\beta)\,\mathrm{median}(s),\\
\omega(\beta)&amp;=0.56\beta^{3}-0.95\beta^{2}+1.82\beta+1.43,\end{split}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mtable columnspacing="0pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_right" columnalign="right"><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>GD</mi></msub></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>ω</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>β</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.340em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>median</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_right" columnalign="right"><mrow><mi>ω</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>β</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>0.56</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>0.95</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>1.82</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1.43</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\begin{split}\theta_{\mathrm{GD}}&amp;=\omega(\beta)\,\mathrm{median}(s),\\
\omega(\beta)&amp;=0.56\beta^{3}-0.95\beta^{2}+1.82\beta+1.43,\end{split}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(4)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">and the retained rank is <math id="A2.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\max\bigl(2,\lvert\{i:s_{i}&gt;\theta_{\mathrm{GD}}\}\rvert\bigr)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>max</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>GD</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\max\bigl(2,\lvert\{i:s_{i}&gt;\theta_{\mathrm{GD}}\}\rvert\bigr)</annotation></semantics></math>. The floor of two is part of the protocol rather than a
numerical guard, and the rank is capped at the number of history columns.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Applying the rule per unit would force one projection per group. The
default rule instead draws <math id="A2.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="256" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>256</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">256</annotation></semantics></math> units per model–anchor cell with a fixed
seed, computes their Gavish–Donoho ranks, and applies the median rank
uniformly to all units of that cell, which keeps the projection batched at
one rank per cell. The flat-protocol group readouts reported in this paper
are computed at the full history rank <math id="A2.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=n_{\mathrm{past}}=5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>past</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=n_{\mathrm{past}}=5</annotation></semantics></math>. The pooled bulk
group-level FRR median is <math id="A2.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.815" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.815</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.815</annotation></semantics></math>, just below the isotropic reference
<math id="A2.SS3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sqrt{(D-r)/D}=0.829" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>0.829</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{(D-r)/D}=0.829</annotation></semantics></math> that this rank and <math id="A2.SS3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D{=}16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D{=}16</annotation></semantics></math> imply. This is the same
isotropic-reference construction that Figure 4 measures
excess against, evaluated there at each structural group’s own size rather
than at <math id="A2.SS3.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D{=}16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D{=}16</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.4 </span>Null Generation and the Calibrated Readout</h3>

<div id="A2.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">FRR compares a <math id="A2.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional target with an <math id="A2.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional subspace, so
a target with no temporal structure at all still passes a fixed threshold
at a rate that depends on <math id="A2.SS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>. A readout compared across group
sizes therefore needs a chance reference computed at its own geometry.</p>
</div>
<section id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Membership resampling.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Within one pool of comparable units, a tensor on the vision side and a
(layer, segment) block on the Pythia side, all scalar coordinate histories
are collected, permuted, and re-chunked into groups whose size multiset is
exactly that of the observed cut. FRR is then recomputed on the permuted
groups under the same window, horizon, rank rule, and normalization. The
permutation leaves every coordinate’s own trajectory untouched and destroys
only which coordinates share a group, so the resulting distribution
isolates the contribution of group membership and nothing else.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Pooling and seeds.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Null values are pooled per (segment, group size, horizon, protocol). The
number of draws per segment is
<math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\max\bigl(5,\lceil 200/n_{\mathrm{groups}}\rceil\bigr)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>max</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⌈</mo><mrow><mn>200</mn><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>groups</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⌉</mo></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\max\bigl(5,\lceil 200/n_{\mathrm{groups}}\rceil\bigr)</annotation></semantics></math>, so that at least
