about <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="200" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>200</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">200</annotation></semantics></math> null values stand behind every threshold. Each draw takes a
seed composed from the draw index, anchor, layer, and segment, so any lane
that recomputes the null reproduces it.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">The two readouts.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The fixed-threshold readout <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{LRGF}_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>LRGF</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{LRGF}_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> counts groups with
<math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{FRR}&lt;\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>FRR</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{FRR}&lt;\theta</annotation></semantics></math>, with <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta=0.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta=0.7</annotation></semantics></math> throughout. The calibrated readout
<math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{LRGF}_{\mathrm{cal}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>LRGF</mi><mi>cal</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{LRGF}_{\mathrm{cal}}</annotation></semantics></math> replaces <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> by the <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=0.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.05</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=0.05</annotation></semantics></math>
quantile of the matched null pool and is reported as excess over <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math>.
<math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{LRGF}_{\mathrm{cal}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>LRGF</mi><mi>cal</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{LRGF}_{\mathrm{cal}}</annotation></semantics></math> is a comparability convention: it places
segments whose group size and null geometry differ on a single axis. It
does not correct individual FRR values, and it does not make a level
comparable to a level read under a different cut. Where the fixed threshold
is used, we also report the null pool’s own pass rate at <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math>, written
<math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{null}_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>null</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{null}_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>, which is the share of the observed fraction that
membership alone would produce.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.5 </span>Numerical Conventions and the Sign Rule</h3>

<section id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">The sign rule and zero displacement.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Signs are compared exactly on the stored floating-point values, with
<math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{sign}(0)=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>sign</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{sign}(0)=0</annotation></semantics></math> and no tolerance band. A coordinate that does
not move in either interval therefore counts as an agreement, and a
coordinate that moves in exactly one of the two counts as a disagreement.
We keep the exact rule because it leaves ESA a parameter-free function of
the realized trajectory, but it makes ESA sensitive to coordinates whose
displacement is zero or numerically negligible over one or both intervals,
in a way that VCS is not: VCS weights each coordinate by its displacement
magnitude, so those coordinates barely enter it.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">This is the mechanism behind the two departures from the parameter-free
reference curve <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{ESA}=1-\arccos(\mathrm{VCS})/\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ESA</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>arccos</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>VCS</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{ESA}=1-\arccos(\mathrm{VCS})/\pi</annotation></semantics></math> in
Figure 1(a). At the five reported anchors the two
departing cells are AlexNet with AdaGrad and AlexNet with Adam, in which up
to <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="79\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>79</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">79\%</annotation></semantics></math> of coordinates have zero reference displacement and up to <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="69\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>69</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">69\%</annotation></semantics></math>
are zero over both intervals. Their median vertical departure from the
reference curve is <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.276" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.276</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.276</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.221" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.221</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.221</annotation></semantics></math>. Restricting both probes to the
coordinates that move in both intervals reduces those departures to
<math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.008" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.008</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.008</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.007" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.007</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.007</annotation></semantics></math>, while the median absolute departure over the
remaining <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="28" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>28</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">28</annotation></semantics></math> cells is <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.003" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.003</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.003</annotation></semantics></math> and is unchanged by the restriction.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Degenerate units.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">VCS is undefined when either vector has norm below <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{-30}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>30</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{-30}</annotation></semantics></math>; such units
are recorded as missing and dropped from denominators rather than counted
as zero. SESA is undefined when the selector is empty, and those units are
dropped in the same way. Non-finite FRR values leave the <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{LRGF}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>LRGF</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{LRGF}</annotation></semantics></math>
denominator.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Other numerical choices.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The probe layer works in double precision. FRR denominators carry an
additive <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{-12}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{-12}</annotation></semantics></math> guard. FRR is computed on the raw history, whereas the
DMD fit standardizes coordinate rows. On the Pythia side a second FRR
protocol normalizes each history column to unit norm within the group, with
a <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{-30}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>30</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{-30}</annotation></semantics></math> guard, and degenerate columns are counted rather than
absorbed; both FRR protocols are reported side by side wherever the
column-normalized variant is used.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Group-mean and full-vector VCS.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure 1(a) plots one point per model–configuration cell
and anchor, pairing that cell’s ESA with its <em id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">group-mean</em> VCS, the mean
of the per-group cosines. The full-vector cosine of the same cell is recorded
alongside it and differs because it weights coordinates by magnitude across
the whole unit rather than within each group. The two are close on most cells
(median difference <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.006" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.006</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.006</annotation></semantics></math>, interquartile range <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.017" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.017</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.017</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.023" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.023</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.023</annotation></semantics></math>) but
diverge sharply on a few, up to <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm 0.45" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>0.45</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm 0.45</annotation></semantics></math>. The group mean is the readout that
belongs on the parameter-free reference curve: its median absolute departure
from <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1-\arccos(\mathrm{VCS})/\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>arccos</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>VCS</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1-\arccos(\mathrm{VCS})/\pi</annotation></semantics></math> is <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.005" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.005</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.005</annotation></semantics></math>, against <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.011" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.011</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.011</annotation></semantics></math> for the
full-vector cosine on the same cells.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.6 </span>Grouping Sensitivity and Within-Family Checks</h3>

<section id="A2.SS6.SSSx1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection">What the Flat Protocol Reads</h4>

<div id="A2.SS6.SSSx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS6.SSSx1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A dedicated audit compared the flat readout with three probes that involve
no grouping at all: element-level ESA, tensor-level VCS, and tensor-level
FRR. On all three, ViT-mid reads as more predictable than ResNet at every
anchor of every matched pair, whereas the flat <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{LRGF}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>LRGF</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{LRGF}</annotation></semantics></math> reference
orders the same runs and anchors the other way
(Figure <a href="#A2.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ What the Flat Protocol Reads ‣ B.6 Grouping Sensitivity and Within-Family Checks ‣ Appendix B Probe Conventions, Calibration, and Robustness ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>). Under a within-tensor membership permutation
the flat ordering reverses to ViT-mid at or above ResNet in <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="24" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>24</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">24</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="24" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>24</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">24</annotation></semantics></math>
pair–anchor comparisons.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A2.F2" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2608.15483v1/app02_e1_blocking_free.svg" id="A2.F2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:698/195;" width="698" height="195"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 2: </span>Probes that use no grouping convention, against the flat
readout (bulk scope; one line per run, <math id="A2.F2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math> matched ViT-mid and ResNet
pairs; the long-cosine ViT-mid run extends to epoch <math id="A2.F2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="90" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>90</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">90</annotation></semantics></math>). On all three
cut-free probes, (a) element-level ESA, (b) tensor-level VCS, and
(c) tensor-level FRR, where lower means more predictable, ViT-mid reads
as more predictable than ResNet at every anchor, while (d) the flat
<math id="A2.F2.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K{=}16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K{=}16</annotation></semantics></math> <math id="A2.F2.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{LRGF}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>LRGF</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{LRGF}</annotation></semantics></math> reference orders the same runs and anchors the
other way (<math id="A2.F2.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>7</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A2.F2.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="A2.F2.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math> pairs). Canonical protocol
(<math id="A2.F2.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{\mathrm{past}}{=}5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>past</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{\mathrm{past}}{=}5</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A2.F2.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau{=}5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau{=}5</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A2.F2.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta{=}0.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta{=}0.7</annotation></semantics></math>); dashed grey lines mark
chance (ESA <math id="A2.F2.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5</annotation></semantics></math>, VCS <math id="A2.F2.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math>).</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A2.SS6.SSSx1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS6.SSSx1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The decomposition names the mechanism (Figure <a href="#A2.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ What the Flat Protocol Reads ‣ B.6 Grouping Sensitivity and Within-Family Checks ‣ Appendix B Probe Conventions, Calibration, and Robustness ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>).
Permuting block membership destroys <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="66" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>66</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">66</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="87\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>87</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">87\%</annotation></semantics></math> of ResNet’s flat
<math id="A2.SS6.SSSx1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{LRGF}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>LRGF</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{LRGF}</annotation></semantics></math>, and the destroyed part localizes on the <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3{\times}3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3{\times}3</annotation></semantics></math>
kernels, with <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{\times}1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{\times}1</annotation></semantics></math> shortcut convolutions contributing
<math id="A2.SS6.SSSx1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta\approx.003" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>.003</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta\approx.003</annotation></semantics></math>. On ViT-mid, <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="82" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>82</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">82</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="94\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>94</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">94\%</annotation></semantics></math> of the reading survives the
same permutation. A flat-<math id="A2.SS6.SSSx1.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{LRGF}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>LRGF</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{LRGF}</annotation></semantics></math> level is therefore a statement
about a grouping convention as much as about an architecture.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A2.F3" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2608.15483v1/app02_e2_permutation_null.svg" id="A2.F3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:698/210;" width="698" height="210"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 3: </span>Permutation-null decomposition of the flat <math id="A2.F3.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K{=}16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K{=}16</annotation></semantics></math>
<math id="A2.F3.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{LRGF}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>LRGF</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{LRGF}</annotation></semantics></math> (bulk scope; one line per run): (a) structural blocking,
(b) the membership-permutation null (mean of <math id="A2.F3.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5</annotation></semantics></math> draws, shading gives min
to max), and (c) their difference <math id="A2.F3.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math>, which is the intra-block
coherence contribution. Permutation destroys <math id="A2.F3.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="66" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>66</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">66</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A2.F3.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="87\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>87</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">87\%</annotation></semantics></math> of ResNet’s
flat readout and the destroyed part localizes on the <math id="A2.F3.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3{\times}3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3{\times}3</annotation></semantics></math>
kernels (<math id="A2.F3.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{\times}1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{\times}1</annotation></semantics></math> shortcut convolutions: <math id="A2.F3.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta\approx.003" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>.003</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta\approx.003</annotation></semantics></math>),
whereas <math id="A2.F3.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="82" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>82</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">82</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A2.F3.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="94\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>94</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">94\%</annotation></semantics></math> of ViT-mid’s readout survives and the
architecture ordering flips to ViT-mid at or above ResNet on the null
column (<math id="A2.F3.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="24/24" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>24</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>24</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">24/24</annotation></semantics></math> pairs). A flat-<math id="A2.F3.m26" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{LRGF}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>LRGF</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{LRGF}</annotation></semantics></math> level is therefore a
statement about a grouping convention as well as about an
architecture.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A2.SS6.SSSx1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS6.SSSx1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Two further properties of the flat protocol matter for reading the main
paper. Between-group ESA dispersion sits at the binomial sampling floor
(<math id="A2.SS6.SSSx1.p3.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.1\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.1</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.1\times</annotation></semantics></math>, median over <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="30" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>30</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">30</annotation></semantics></math> cells), so flat blocks are statistically
homogeneous, and group-level coupling between ESA and FRR is largely erased
(cell-wide median <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-.16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>.16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-.16</annotation></semantics></math>). And bulk group-level FRR sits close to its
chance floor: of the <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="31.2\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>31.2</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">31.2\%</annotation></semantics></math> of bulk groups passing <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta{=}0.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta{=}0.7</annotation></semantics></math>, about
<math id="A2.SS6.SSSx1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="25" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>25</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">25</annotation></semantics></math> percentage points are chance passing (<math id="A2.SS6.SSSx1.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{null}_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>null</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{null}_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> median
<math id="A2.SS6.SSSx1.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".23" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>.23</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.23</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx1.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".25" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>.25</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.25</annotation></semantics></math>). This is the concrete reason the time-axis readouts use
<math id="A2.SS6.SSSx1.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{LRGF}_{\mathrm{cal}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>LRGF</mi><mi>cal</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{LRGF}_{\mathrm{cal}}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS6.SSSx2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection">Structural and Magnitude Cuts on the Vision Panel</h4>

<div id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Recutting along physical or functional axes changes what the instrument
resolves. Structural units raise between-group ESA dispersion off the floor
(head <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="qkv" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">qkv</annotation></semantics></math> <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="4.4\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>4.4</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.4\times</annotation></semantics></math>, filter <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3{\times}3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3{\times}3</annotation></semantics></math> <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p1.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.9\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.9</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.9\times</annotation></semantics></math>, neuron pair
<math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p1.m5" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.7\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.7</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.7\times</annotation></semantics></math>, row <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{\times}1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{\times}1</annotation></semantics></math> <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p1.m7" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.2\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.2</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.2\times</annotation></semantics></math>, against <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p1.m8" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.1\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.1</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.1\times</annotation></semantics></math> for flat)
and restore group-level ESA–FRR coupling (cell-wide median <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-.42" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>.42</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-.42</annotation></semantics></math> against
<math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-.16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>.16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-.16</annotation></semantics></math>). The restoration is architecture-resolved: ViT and ViT-mid couple
in every recipe cell (<math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-.28" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>.28</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-.28</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-.77" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>.77</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-.77</annotation></semantics></math>), while ResNet’s plain recipes stay
flat (SGD <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-.14" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>.14</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-.14</annotation></semantics></math>; momentum, Adam, and Muon near <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math>) and only the recipe
cells couple (weight decay <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-.45" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>.45</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-.45</annotation></semantics></math>, SAM <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-.35" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>.35</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-.35</annotation></semantics></math>, AdaGrad <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-.30" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>.30</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-.30</annotation></semantics></math>). Under the
calibrated readout the same reordering is visible over training anchors
(Figure <a href="#A2.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ Structural and Magnitude Cuts on the Vision Panel ‣ B.6 Grouping Sensitivity and Within-Family Checks ‣ Appendix B Probe Conventions, Calibration, and Robustness ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>): whole patch filters and head-level <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="qkv" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">qkv</annotation></semantics></math> groups
carry clear above-chance excess, while slab and projection cuts sit near
chance.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A2.F4" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2608.15483v1/app02_c1_structural.svg" id="A2.F4.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:698/250;" width="698" height="250"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 4: </span>Structural-axis cuts under the calibrated readout: excess
<math id="A2.F4.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="=\mathrm{LRGF}_{\mathrm{cal}}-\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>LRGF</mi><mi>cal</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">=\mathrm{LRGF}_{\mathrm{cal}}-\alpha</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="A2.F4.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha{=}0.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.05</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha{=}0.05</annotation></semantics></math>, so zero is
chance), median over runs. (a) ViT-mid: physically defined groups surface
above-chance structure that the flat axis does not resolve, with whole
patch filters reaching <math id="A2.F4.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".61" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>.61</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.61</annotation></semantics></math> and head-level <math id="A2.F4.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="qkv" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">qkv</annotation></semantics></math> groups <math id="A2.F4.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".21" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>.21</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.21</annotation></semantics></math> at anchor
<math id="A2.F4.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="45" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>45</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">45</annotation></semantics></math>, while slab and projection cuts sit near chance. (b) ResNet: whole
<math id="A2.F4.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3{\times}3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3{\times}3</annotation></semantics></math> filters reach <math id="A2.F4.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".55" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>.55</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.55</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A2.F4.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".62" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>.62</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.62</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.F4.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{\times}1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{\times}1</annotation></semantics></math> rows <math id="A2.F4.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".18" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>.18</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.18</annotation></semantics></math>.
Each cut carries a size-matched membership-permutation null that
preserves the group-size multiset, and groups use only pre-anchor
information. Group size differs across cuts, so levels are comparable
only through the calibrated excess.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Pocket density under structural cuts is architecture-stratified
(Figure <a href="#A2.F5" title="Figure 5 ‣ Structural and Magnitude Cuts on the Vision Panel ‣ B.6 Grouping Sensitivity and Within-Family Checks ‣ Appendix B Probe Conventions, Calibration, and Robustness ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>): <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{FRR}&lt;0.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>FRR</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0.7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{FRR}&lt;0.7</annotation></semantics></math> reaches <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="19.8\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>19.8</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">19.8\%</annotation></semantics></math> of
ViT-mid head-<math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="qkv" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">qkv</annotation></semantics></math> groups and <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="12.7\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>12.7</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">12.7\%</annotation></semantics></math> of neuron pairs, against <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.5\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.5</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.5\%</annotation></semantics></math> for
ResNet kernels and <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.1\%</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{\times}1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{\times}1</annotation></semantics></math> rows. These cuts have large
group sizes, where the membership-resample null passes <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta{=}0.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta{=}0.7</annotation></semantics></math> at a
rate near zero, so essentially none of the passes is attributable to chance, unlike the flat bars in the same figure. Structural excess decays over training, from a
median of <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".070" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>.070</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.070</annotation></semantics></math> at anchor <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".036" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>.036</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.036</annotation></semantics></math> at anchor <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="40" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>40</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">40</annotation></semantics></math>, which places
pockets in an early-to-mid-training population.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A2.F5" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2608.15483v1/app02_pocket_density_by_cut.svg" id="A2.F5.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:698/550;" width="698" height="550"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 5: </span>Pocket density by grouping cut and architecture on the vision
panel: share of groups with <math id="A2.F5.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{FRR}&lt;0.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>FRR</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0.7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{FRR}&lt;0.7</annotation></semantics></math>, pooled over the <math id="A2.F5.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="18" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>18</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">18</annotation></semantics></math>
recipe cells and anchors <math id="A2.F5.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A2.F5.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="40" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>40</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">40</annotation></semantics></math> of the group-level lanes (bulk
tensors, out-of-window target). The structural cuts and the magnitude cut
(top three of <math id="A2.F5.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>16</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16</annotation></semantics></math> causal bins) are chance-immune at <math id="A2.F5.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta{=}0.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta{=}0.7</annotation></semantics></math>, so the chance contribution to their bars is negligible. The flat <math id="A2.F5.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K{=}16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K{=}16</annotation></semantics></math> bars are pooled
over the same <math id="A2.F5.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="18" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>18</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">18</annotation></semantics></math> cells weighted by group count and are stacked: the
hatched portion is the measured chance-pass fraction under the
membership-resample null (<math id="A2.F5.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>6.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6.0</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A2.F5.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="15.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>15.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">15.5</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A2.F5.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="26.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>26.6</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">26.6</annotation></semantics></math> pp of the
<math id="A2.F5.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="23.5/18.6/29.8\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>23.5</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>18.6</mn><mo>/</mo><mrow><mn>29.8</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">23.5/18.6/29.8\%</annotation></semantics></math> totals for ResNet, ViT, and ViT-mid). Most of the
ViT-family flat readout is chance passing, and most of the ResNet flat
readout is intra-kernel coherence. Group size differs across cuts, so
levels are comparable within a bar group only in the chance-immune
sense.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The magnitude cut is the strongest single-axis sorter of pocket density and
not a raiser of totals. Totals sit slightly below the structural cut
(<math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.4/3.2/8.1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.4</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>3.2</mn><mo>/</mo><mrow><mn>8.1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.4/3.2/8.1\%</annotation></semantics></math> against <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.3/6.7/12.9\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.3</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>6.7</mn><mo>/</mo><mrow><mn>12.9</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.3/6.7/12.9\%</annotation></semantics></math> for ResNet, ViT, and ViT-mid),
but the density gradient is monotone across all <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>16</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16</annotation></semantics></math> bins and steep at the
top: pooled <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{FRR}&lt;0.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>FRR</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0.7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{FRR}&lt;0.7</annotation></semantics></math> rises from <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0\%</annotation></semantics></math> at bin <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="20.1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>20.1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">20.1\%</annotation></semantics></math> at
bin <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>15</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">15</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{ESA}&gt;0.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ESA</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0.7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{ESA}&gt;0.7</annotation></semantics></math> from <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.1\%</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p3.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="27.2\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>27.2</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">27.2\%</annotation></semantics></math>, and
<math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p3.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{VCS}&gt;0.4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>VCS</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0.4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{VCS}&gt;0.4</annotation></semantics></math> from <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p3.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.2\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.2</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.2\%</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p3.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="36.4\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>36.4</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">36.4\%</annotation></semantics></math>, three instrument families
ordered the same way along one causal axis (Figure <a href="#A2.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ Structural and Magnitude Cuts on the Vision Panel ‣ B.6 Grouping Sensitivity and Within-Family Checks ‣ Appendix B Probe Conventions, Calibration, and Robustness ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>). The
top three bins concentrate density beyond the best structural cut (ViT-mid
<math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p3.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="27.9\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>27.9</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">27.9\%</annotation></semantics></math> against head <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p3.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="qkv" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">qkv</annotation></semantics></math> <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p3.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="19.8\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>19.8</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">19.8\%</annotation></semantics></math>). ResNet stays low under every probe of
the magnitude cut (<math id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p3.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.1/4.4/12.4\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2.1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>4.4</mn><mo>/</mo><mrow><mn>12.4</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.1/4.4/12.4\%</annotation></semantics></math> for FRR, ESA, and VCS on the top three
bins), so the architecture stratification is itself cut-robust.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A2.F6" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2608.15483v1/app02_c2b_magnitude.svg" id="A2.F6.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:698/230;" width="698" height="230"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 6: </span>Magnitude-stratified cut at anchor <math id="A2.F6.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="45" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>45</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">45</annotation></semantics></math>: groups are <math id="A2.F6.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>16</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16</annotation></semantics></math>
equal-width bins of the per-tensor pre-anchor <math id="A2.F6.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lVert\Delta w\rVert_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo fence="true" rspace="0em">∥</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>w</mi></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em">∥</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lVert\Delta w\rVert_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> rank
(bin <math id="A2.F6.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> weakest, bin <math id="A2.F6.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>15</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">15</annotation></semantics></math> strongest), reported as excess over chance,
median over runs; the floor at <math id="A2.F6.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.05</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.05</annotation></semantics></math> means no group passes.
(a) ViT-mid feature-dimension tensors show a monotone concentration
signature (top bins <math id="A2.F6.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".38" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>.38</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.38</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A2.F6.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".66" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>.66</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.66</annotation></semantics></math>), while the patch embedding stays at
the floor because its structure lies on the spatial axis
(Figure <a href="#A2.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ Structural and Magnitude Cuts on the Vision Panel ‣ B.6 Grouping Sensitivity and Within-Family Checks ‣ Appendix B Probe Conventions, Calibration, and Robustness ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>). (b) ResNet reads near zero under the same
cut. This is the strongest single-axis sorter on the ViT side, and its
architecture contrast runs opposite to the flat readout.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS6.SSSx2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">An axis-independent check bounds what any cut could reach
(Figure <a href="#A2.F7" title="Figure 7 ‣ Structural and Magnitude Cuts on the Vision Panel ‣ B.6 Grouping Sensitivity and Within-Family Checks ‣ Appendix B Probe Conventions, Calibration, and Robustness ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>): the top-five eigenvalue mass of the
coordinate-trajectory correlation spectrum exceeds a matched independent
null by two to four times in every tensor family of all three
architectures. Co-moving structure is present everywhere; which grouping
axis can access it is what differs by architecture.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A2.F7" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2608.15483v1/app02_c3_spectrum.svg" id="A2.F7.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:698/698;" width="698" height="698"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 7: </span>Spectrum diagnostic at the late anchors (anchor <math id="A2.F7.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="45" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>45</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">45</annotation></semantics></math> on the
vision panel, step <math id="A2.F7.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="70" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>70</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">70</annotation></semantics></math>k on Pythia): top-five eigenvalue mass of the
coordinate-trajectory correlation spectrum per tensor family, against a
simulated independent null of matching shape (grey band gives min to max
over <math id="A2.F7.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5</annotation></semantics></math> draws), median over runs. Every family of all three
architectures exceeds the null by two to four times, so co-moving
structure is present in every family; which grouping axis can access it
is what differs by architecture.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS6.SSSx3" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection">Pythia Cuts and the Granularity Ladder</h4>

<div id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The Pythia readings are registered as correspondences and are not used to
certify one another. The flat audit finds a third permutation signature
here, distinct from both vision architectures: on <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="qkv" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">qkv</annotation></semantics></math>, permuting block
membership <em id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">raises</em> the flat reading (<math id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta=-.140" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>.140</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta=-.140</annotation></semantics></math>, structural
<math id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".099" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>.099</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.099</annotation></semantics></math> against permuted <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".239" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>.239</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.239</annotation></semantics></math>), which is what comoving mass concentrated
in a few strong coordinates produces when random blocks inherit it and
contiguous blocks isolate it.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Head grouping and magnitude grouping are adjudicated at anchor <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10</annotation></semantics></math>k. Head grouping retains far stronger calibrated signal on <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="qkv" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">qkv</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{LRGF}_{\mathrm{cal}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>LRGF</mi><mi>cal</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{LRGF}_{\mathrm{cal}}</annotation></semantics></math>
<math id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".333/.389" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>.333</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>.389</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.333/.389</annotation></semantics></math> against <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".104/.069" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>.104</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>.069</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.104/.069</annotation></semantics></math> at 70M and 160M), so the head unit is an
organizational axis of its own rather than a shadow of coordinate
magnitude. On the MLP, magnitude sensitivity is local (70M layer 5 in
mid-training, about <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p2.m6" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="3\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3\times</annotation></semantics></math>) and the grid is negative in <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>7</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10</annotation></semantics></math>
cells, so the MLP’s modest calibrated readout is modest under both
conventions.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Granularity is a separate axis. At head granularity (<math id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D{=}32{,}768" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>32,768</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D{=}32{,}768</annotation></semantics></math>) the
absolute <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> columns read near zero while calibrated excess is large,
for instance <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+.263" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>.263</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+.263</annotation></semantics></math> for <span id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">attn_out</span> at anchor <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="70" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>70</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">70</annotation></semantics></math>k, which is the
sharpest case of large-<math id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math> blindness in the fixed threshold. Stepping down
to one <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{qkv}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>W</mi><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{qkv}</annotation></semantics></math> row (<math id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D{=}512" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>512</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D{=}512</annotation></semantics></math>) revives an absolute pocket population,
with <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{FRR}&lt;0.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>FRR</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0.7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{FRR}&lt;0.7</annotation></semantics></math> stable at <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5\%</annotation></semantics></math> of rows and the <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p3.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D{=}512" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>512</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D{=}512</annotation></semantics></math>
and <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p3.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D{=}128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>128</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D{=}128</annotation></semantics></math> distributions nearly coincident. The row convention is
invariant across <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p3.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D{=}128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>128</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D{=}128</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p3.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3072" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3072</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3072</annotation></semantics></math> (410M peak fractions <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p3.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".432/.434/.438" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>.432</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>.434</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>.438</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.432/.434/.438</annotation></semantics></math>
at <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p3.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D{=}1024/512/256" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1024</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>512</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>256</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D{=}1024/512/256</annotation></semantics></math>; a 160M scan over the same range; 1B below <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p3.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.5</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5\%</annotation></semantics></math>
throughout after masking), so no per-size adjustment is needed. Recutting
the MLP resolves an asymmetry between its halves: the input half and the
magnitude cut read near zero on absolute <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p3.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> (means <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p3.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.04\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.04</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.04\%</annotation></semantics></math> and
<math id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p3.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.01\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.01</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.01\%</annotation></semantics></math>), while the output half carries a late wave in the deepest layer
(70M layer 5: rising from <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p3.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>64</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">64</annotation></semantics></math>k to a peak of <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p3.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5.4\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5.4</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5.4\%</annotation></semantics></math> at <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p3.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="96" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>96</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">96</annotation></semantics></math>k, fading by
<math id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p3.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>128</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">128</annotation></semantics></math>k). Across five model sizes the output half is the only MLP cut with
signal (peaks <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p3.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.8</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx3.p3.m26" class="ltx_Math" alttext="15.7\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>15.7</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">15.7\%</annotation></semantics></math>).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS6.SSSx4" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection">Within-Family Agreement, per Cell</h4>

<div id="A2.SS6.SSSx4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS6.SSSx4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The two within-family summaries quoted in Section 4.1
are medians over per-cell Spearman correlations, each computed across the
tensors of one model–configuration cell. Their dispersion is as follows.
Out-of-window and in-window FRR correlate at a median <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{S}=0.83" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.83</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{S}=0.83</annotation></semantics></math>, with
per-cell values from <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.53" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.53</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.53</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.97" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.97</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.97</annotation></semantics></math>; the low end is occupied by AdaGrad
cells (ViT <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.62" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.62</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.62</annotation></semantics></math>, ViT-mid <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.63" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.63</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.63</annotation></semantics></math>) together with one further cell at
<math id="A2.SS6.SSSx4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.53" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.53</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.53</annotation></semantics></math>. SESA under the DMD and linear-trend selectors correlates at a
median <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{S}=0.89" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.89</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{S}=0.89</annotation></semantics></math>, with per-cell values from <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.44" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.44</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.44</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx4.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.00" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.00</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.00</annotation></semantics></math>; the one
low value is AlexNet with AdaGrad (<math id="A2.SS6.SSSx4.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.44" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.44</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.44</annotation></semantics></math>), which is also one of the two
cells identified in Appendix <a href="#A2.SS5" title="B.5 Numerical Conventions and the Sign Rule ‣ Appendix B Probe Conventions, Calibration, and Robustness ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.5</span></a>. The two displacement-
direction readouts correlate at a median <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx4.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{S}=0.93" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.93</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{S}=0.93</annotation></semantics></math>. Correlations
between the DMD and linear-trend <em id="A2.SS6.SSSx4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">lift</em> readouts are much weaker
(median <math id="A2.SS6.SSSx4.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.15</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.15</annotation></semantics></math>); lift is a within-predictor quantity, and the two
selectors define different denominators, so the comparison is reported
only as dispersion and not as an agreement check.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS7" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.7 </span>Reporting Discipline</h3>

<div id="A2.SS7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Five rules follow from the measurements above, and every group-level
statement in this paper obeys them.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS7.p2" class="ltx_para">
<ol id="A2.I1" class="ltx_enumerate" style="--ltx-enum-leftmargin:1.4em;">
<li id="A2.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="A2.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Claims travel with the grouping convention.</span> Any group-level
ordering or level statement names its cut, and an ordering that reverses
under recutting is reported as conditional on the convention rather than as
a property of the architectures.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="A2.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Levels are not comparable across cuts.</span> Paired flat and
structural FRR readouts rank consistently (<math id="A2.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{S}=.79" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>.79</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{S}=.79</annotation></semantics></math>) but carry a
systematic level offset (median <math id="A2.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta=+.082" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>.082</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta=+.082</annotation></semantics></math>, structural above flat), so
cross-cut comparisons use ranks or calibrated excess and never raw levels.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="A2.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Chance immunity is cut-dependent.</span> Large-group cuts make
<math id="A2.I1.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta{=}0.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta{=}0.7</annotation></semantics></math> essentially chance-free, while the flat protocol passes
about <math id="A2.I1.i3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="25" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>25</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">25</annotation></semantics></math> percentage points of bulk groups by chance. Raw <math id="A2.I1.i3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math>
fractions are quoted only for cuts whose null pass rate is near zero, and
calibrated excess is used otherwise.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">4.</span> 
<div id="A2.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I1.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Time-axis readouts use <math id="A2.I1.i4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{LRGF}_{\mathrm{cal}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>LRGF</mi><mi>cal</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{LRGF}_{\mathrm{cal}}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span> Where
a bare <math id="A2.I1.i4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> fraction is reported across layers, it is accompanied by
its <math id="A2.I1.i4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{null}_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>null</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{null}_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> reference.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I1.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">5.</span> 
<div id="A2.I1.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I1.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I1.i5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Selectivity lift is not compared across predictors.</span> Lift is
a within-predictor quantity, since SESA is evaluated on the selector that
predictor produces.</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A3" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix C </span>Spatial Localization: the Auxiliary–Bulk Partition</h2>

<div id="A3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Section 4.2 splits trainable tensors into two morphological
classes and reads the auxiliary–bulk separation within matched
trajectories. This appendix gives the membership rule, the tensor-by-tensor
attribution it produces in each training regime, and the audits that bound
how much the choice of rule could matter.</p>
</div>
<section id="A3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.1 </span>The Partition Rule</h3>

<div id="A3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The primary definition is morphological. A parameter tensor is
<em id="A3.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">auxiliary</em> if it is vector-like, which covers normalization scales
and shifts, biases, and token and positional embedding vectors, and
<em id="A3.SS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">bulk</em> if it is a matrix-like weight, which covers linear and
attention projections, MLP weights, and convolutional kernels. The
definition refers to the shape and function of the tensor, not to its size.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The vision pipeline realizes this rule through a size threshold on coarse
role classes: a tensor is auxiliary if the total parameter count of its
role class within that model falls below <math id="A3.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>5</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{5}</annotation></semantics></math>. The threshold applies to
role-class totals rather than to individual tensors, so a small individual
matrix inside a large class, such as the <math id="A3.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}280" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,280</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}280</annotation></semantics></math>-parameter ViT classifier
head, stays bulk. Every quantitative auxiliary–bulk readout in the paper
uses this operational assignment, and
Appendix <a href="#A3.SS2" title="C.2 Vision Panel: Attribution and Dual-Definition Audit ‣ Appendix C Spatial Localization: the Auxiliary–Bulk Partition ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.2</span></a> audits it against the morphological
definition. On Pythia the same rule is expressed through a segment taxonomy
rather than a threshold, because the segment structure already separates
matrices from vectors exactly (Appendix <a href="#A3.SS3" title="C.3 Pythia: Segment Taxonomy and the Vector Segment ‣ Appendix C Spatial Localization: the Auxiliary–Bulk Partition ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.3</span></a>). The Pythia partition additionally coincides with optimizer treatment: normalization parameters and all biases are exempt from weight decay under the released recipe, so auxiliary–bulk contrasts at that scale register a parameter-role difference under the recipe rather than an isolated effect of tensor shape.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.2 </span>Vision Panel: Attribution and Dual-Definition Audit</h3>

<div id="A3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A3.T6" title="Table 6 ‣ C.2 Vision Panel: Attribution and Dual-Definition Audit ‣ Appendix C Spatial Localization: the Auxiliary–Bulk Partition ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> lists the attribution per model, the
composition of the auxiliary class by coarse role, and the audit of the two
definitions against each other.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A3.T6" class="ltx_table">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure ltx_flex_table">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1">
<p id="A3.T6.1" class="ltx_p ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center">(a) Per-model attribution</p></div><div class="ltx_flex_break"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1">
<table id="A3.T6.2" class="ltx_tabular ltx_figure_panel ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<tbody class="ltx_tbody">
<tr id="A3.T6.2.1" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A3.T6.2.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_border_tt"></td>
<th id="A3.T6.2.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt" colspan="2">Tensors</th>
<th id="A3.T6.2.1.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt" colspan="2">Parameters</th>
