<th id="A3.T6.2.1.4" class="ltx_td ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt"></th>
<td id="A3.T6.2.1.5" class="ltx_td ltx_border_tt"></td></tr>
<tr id="A3.T6.2.2" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="A3.T6.2.2.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_column">Model</th>
<th id="A3.T6.2.2.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_t">aux</th>
<th id="A3.T6.2.2.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_t">bulk</th>
<th id="A3.T6.2.2.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_t">aux</th>
<th id="A3.T6.2.2.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_t">bulk</th>
<th id="A3.T6.2.2.6" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_th ltx_th_column">aux share</th>
<th id="A3.T6.2.2.7" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_column">aux composition (tensors)</th></tr>
<tr id="A3.T6.2.3" class="ltx_tr">

<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 6: </span>Auxiliary–bulk attribution and dual-definition audit on the
vision panel. <span id="A3.T6.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(a)</span> Per-model tensor attribution under the
operational split, with the composition of the auxiliary class by coarse
role (ln/bn/bias/tok; the single defector appears as <em id="A3.T6.9" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">linear</em>).
<span id="A3.T6.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(b)</span> Agreement between the morphological and operational
definitions at three audit levels; the complete defector list is the single
tensor discussed in Appendix <a href="#A3.SS2" title="C.2 Vision Panel: Attribution and Dual-Definition Audit ‣ Appendix C Spatial Localization: the Auxiliary–Bulk Partition ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.2</span></a>. Definitions are
given in Appendix <a href="#A3.SS1" title="C.1 The Partition Rule ‣ Appendix C Spatial Localization: the Auxiliary–Bulk Partition ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.1</span></a>. Data: the tensor-level table of
the canonical group-level panel, with attribution fields constant across
anchors and optimizer cells. Parameter counts cover the parameter vector
only, with no batch-normalization running statistics.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A3.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The two definitions agree on <math id="A3.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="213" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>213</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">213</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="A3.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="214" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>214</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">214</annotation></semantics></math> unique model–tensor pairs
(<math id="A3.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="99.5\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>99.5</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">99.5\%</annotation></semantics></math>), and on <math id="A3.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}196" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,196</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}196</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="A3.SS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}203" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,203</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}203</annotation></semantics></math> cell–tensor instances
(<math id="A3.SS2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="99.4\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>99.4</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">99.4\%</annotation></semantics></math>). The defector list is a single tensor: the ResNet final
classifier head <span id="A3.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">linear.weight</span> (<math id="A3.SS2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2{,}560" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2,560</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2{,}560</annotation></semantics></math> parameters), which is
matrix-like under the morphological definition but auxiliary under the
operational one, because its <span id="A3.SS2.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">linear</span> role class totals only those
same <math id="A3.SS2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2{,}560" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2,560</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2{,}560</annotation></semantics></math> parameters. It recurs in all seven ResNet optimizer cells,
which is <math id="A3.SS2.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="35" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>35</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">35</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="A3.SS2.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6{,}015" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>6,015</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6{,}015</annotation></semantics></math> panel rows. Because the reported readouts use
the operational assignment, this tensor is counted as auxiliary throughout.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Two properties of the audit are worth stating explicitly. First, the
agreement is a property of the role-class form of the threshold: applying
the same <math id="A3.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>5</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{5}</annotation></semantics></math> threshold per tensor instead of per role class would
agree with the morphological definition on only <math id="A3.SS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="175" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>175</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">175</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="A3.SS2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="214" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>214</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">214</annotation></semantics></math> tensors
(<math id="A3.SS2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="81.8\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>81.8</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">81.8\%</annotation></semantics></math>). Second, the four ResNet tensors filed under the <span id="A3.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">bias</span>
bucket are the shortcut batch-normalization affine parameters, which the
coarse name rule places there because their names carry no <span id="A3.SS2.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">bn</span>
marker. They are vector-like under either reading, so the audit is
unaffected.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">The panel covers the parameter vector only, with no batch-normalization
running statistics, and excludes tensors holding fewer than <math id="A3.SS2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>16</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16</annotation></semantics></math> scalars,
because the <math id="A3.SS2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K{=}16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K{=}16</annotation></semantics></math> grouping cannot be formed there. On the vision side
this excludes exactly one tensor per model, the ten-parameter classifier
bias, for <math id="A3.SS2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="50" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>50</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">50</annotation></semantics></math> parameters in total.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">

<div id="A3.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">

counts, and parameter shares at 70M, and Figure <a href="#A3.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ C.3 Pythia: Segment Taxonomy and the Vector Segment ‣ Appendix C Spatial Localization: the Auxiliary–Bulk Partition ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>
places every parameter tensor in the architecture.</p>
</div>

<p id="A3.T7.2" class="ltx_p ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center">Per-layer patterns carry the prefix <span id="A3.T7.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gpt_neox.layers.<math id="A3.T7.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>.</span> and
repeat over the <math id="A3.T7.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L=6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L=6</annotation></semantics></math> layers; <sup id="A3.T7.2.2" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A3.T7.2.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">∗</span></sup> marks whole-model tensors, with
<span id="A3.T7.2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">final_layer_norm</span> counted inside vec and the two embedding
matrices forming their own segments. Shapes are the 70M reference and scale
with model size (160M: <math id="A3.T7.m27" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d{=}768" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>768</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d{=}768</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A3.T7.m28" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L{=}12" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L{=}12</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A3.T7.m29" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{\mathrm{mlp}}{=}3072" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>mlp</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>3072</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{\mathrm{mlp}}{=}3072</annotation></semantics></math>, so
the <math id="A3.T7.m30" class="ltx_Math" alttext="qkv" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">qkv</annotation></semantics></math> weights become <math id="A3.T7.m31" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2304\times 768" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2304</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>768</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2304\times 768</annotation></semantics></math>); shares are of the 70M parameter
total <math id="A3.T7.m32" class="ltx_Math" alttext="70{,}426{,}624" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>70,426,624</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">70{,}426{,}624</annotation></semantics></math>. <sup id="A3.T7.2.4" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A3.T7.2.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">≡</span></sup> <span id="A3.T7.2.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">attention.dense.bias</span> and
<span id="A3.T7.2.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">mlp.dense_4h_to_h.bias</span> coincide under the parallel residual, so
both rows are kept in the panel with a duplicate flag and all aggregates
count the pair once. The auxiliary series of the aggregation is an alias of
the vec segment, with a per-anchor difference identically <math id="A3.T7.m34" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.0</annotation></semantics></math>. The vec
segment is exempt from weight decay in the released pretraining recipe,
while the matrix segments and both embeddings take <math id="A3.T7.m35" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{wd}=0.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>wd</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{wd}=0.1</annotation></semantics></math>.</p></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 7: </span>Pythia segment scheme and its mapping to the auxiliary–bulk
partition, with shapes and parameter counts at 70M.</figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="A3.F8" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2608.15483v1/app03_pythia_structure.svg" id="A3.F8.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:499/513;" width="499" height="513"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 8: </span>Where the auxiliary–bulk partition sits in the architecture.
One box per parameter tensor (LayerNorm boxes carry weight and bias
jointly; linear biases are drawn as chips on their matrix box), with fill
colour giving the partition class: orange for auxiliary, which is the
vector segment and covers all vector-like parameters including the final
LayerNorm; blue for bulk, the weight matrices (<math id="A3.F8.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="qkv" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">qkv</annotation></semantics></math>, <span id="A3.F8.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">attn_out</span>,
MLP); hatched grey for tensors excluded from the aggregation.
<span id="A3.F8.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(a)</span> Pythia-70M: one parallel-residual block, repeated six times,
plus the top level; the two untied embedding matrices are their own
segments and are excluded. The marked bias pair (<math id="A3.F8.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\equiv" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>≡</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\equiv</annotation></semantics></math>) coincides
under the parallel residual, so both rows are kept in the panel while
aggregates count the pair once. <span id="A3.F8.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(b)</span> ViT-mid: sequential
residuals, repeated seven times; here the token and positional embedding
vectors are vector-like and therefore auxiliary, which is the one
cross-regime difference from (a), and the ten-parameter head bias
(<math id="A3.F8.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\dagger" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>†</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\dagger</annotation></semantics></math>) is below the <math id="A3.F8.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K{=}16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K{=}16</annotation></semantics></math> grouping minimum and is the only
tensor excluded on the vision side. Shapes are the 70M reference.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A3.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Each transformer layer contributes three matrix segments, <math id="A3.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="qkv" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">qkv</annotation></semantics></math>
(<span id="A3.SS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">attention.query_key_value.weight</span>), <span id="A3.SS3.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">attn_out</span>
(<span id="A3.SS3.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">attention.dense.weight</span>), and <span id="A3.SS3.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">mlp</span>
(<span id="A3.SS3.p2.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">dense_h_to_4h</span> and <span id="A3.SS3.p2.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">dense_4h_to_h</span> weights), which
together constitute bulk, and one vector segment collecting the two
per-layer LayerNorms with their weights and biases, all four linear biases,
and the final LayerNorm. The auxiliary series of the aggregation is an
alias of the vector segment, with a per-anchor difference identically
<math id="A3.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.0</annotation></semantics></math>, so the vector segment is the auxiliary class: all vector-like
parameters including the final LayerNorm. At 70M this is <math id="A3.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="50" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>50</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">50</annotation></semantics></math> tensors and
<math id="A3.SS3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="40{,}960" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>40,960</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">40{,}960</annotation></semantics></math> parameters, against <math id="A3.SS3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="24" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>24</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">24</annotation></semantics></math> tensors and <math id="A3.SS3.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="18{,}874{,}368" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>18,874,368</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">18{,}874{,}368</annotation></semantics></math> parameters
for bulk.</p>
</div>
<section id="A3.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Embeddings.</h5>

<div id="A3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The two untied embedding matrices, <span id="A3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">embed_in</span> and
<span id="A3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">embed_out</span>, form their own segments and stay outside the
auxiliary–bulk aggregation. They hold <math id="A3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="73.1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>73.1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">73.1\%</annotation></semantics></math> of the parameter count, so
the aggregation covers the remaining <math id="A3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="26.9\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>26.9</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">26.9\%</annotation></semantics></math>. One labeling imprecision is
registered: in the existing level–time aggregation the embedding rows
enter the bulk side with <math id="A3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.016\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.016</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.016\%</annotation></semantics></math> row weight, which has no numerical
effect on any reported readout.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS3.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">The duplicate bias pair.</h5>

<div id="A3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Under the parallel residual of GPT-NeoX, <span id="A3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">attention.dense.bias</span> and
<span id="A3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">mlp.dense_4h_to_h.bias</span> receive identical per-step gradients,
and their trajectories coincide: bitwise on 70M over all released
checkpoints, and within one half-precision unit in the last place on 160M.
Both rows are kept in the panel with a duplicate flag, and every aggregate
counts the pair once.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS3.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Weight decay.</h5>

<div id="A3.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The vector segment is entirely exempt from weight decay in the released
pretraining configuration, while the matrix segments and both embeddings
take <math id="A3.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{wd}=0.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>wd</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{wd}=0.1</annotation></semantics></math>. This is a property of the public training recipe
rather than a choice of ours, and it is one of the conditions under which
the auxiliary–bulk contrast in Figure 3 is read.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.4 </span>Cross-Regime Comparability</h3>

<div id="A3.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The membership rule, vector-like to auxiliary, is the same in both regimes.
The one difference is which embedding-adjacent tensors exist and where they
land. On the vision side the token and positional embedding <em id="A3.SS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">vectors</em>
are vector-like and therefore auxiliary. On Pythia the embedding
<em id="A3.SS4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">matrices</em> are not vector-like, and they are excluded as separate
segments rather than assigned to bulk.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Two further protocol differences keep absolute levels from being compared
across regimes, and Figure 3 accordingly compares the
within-line ordering rather than levels. The vision panel uses flat
<math id="A3.SS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K{=}16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K{=}16</annotation></semantics></math> groups on an epoch clock, whereas the Pythia panel uses
architecture-aligned segment groups on a released-checkpoint clock, and the
two clocks index different amounts of optimization per probe step.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A4" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix D </span>Pocket Trajectories, Persistence, and Overlap Registrations</h2>

<div id="A4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Section 4.2 reports that predictable pockets are a small
minority of bulk group–anchor observations, that most of them are
transient, and that the degree of persistence varies by parameter role.
This appendix gives the trajectories behind those statements: what the
pocket population looks like at a given time, when it appears and how
long individual pockets survive, the one event on the pretraining side at
which the population changes discontinuously, and the measured overlaps
between pocket membership and indicators defined outside the
subspace-residual family.</p>
</div>
<section id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Units.</h5>

<div id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">As everywhere in this paper, each readout below names the unit it is read
on and the threshold convention it uses
(Appendix <a href="#A2.SS7" title="B.7 Reporting Discipline ‣ Appendix B Probe Conventions, Calibration, and Robustness ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.7</span></a>). Two units appear. At
<em id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">group level</em> a pocket is a functional group whose FRR falls below
the size-matched <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5\%</annotation></semantics></math> null quantile at that anchor (<math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau{=}5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau{=}5</annotation></semantics></math>, raw
protocol); this is the census unit, and it is read as excess over the
null. At <em id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">row level</em>, meaning one <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{qkv}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>W</mi><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{qkv}</annotation></semantics></math> row, one
<math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{\mathrm{head}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>head</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{\mathrm{head}}</annotation></semantics></math> slice of the attention output projection, or one
output column of an MLP neuron, the reported quantity is the fraction of
rows with <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{FRR}&lt;0.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>FRR</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0.7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{FRR}&lt;0.7</annotation></semantics></math>; at those group sizes the
membership-resample pass rate is near zero
(Appendix <a href="#A2.SS4" title="B.4 Null Generation and the Calibrated Readout ‣ Appendix B Probe Conventions, Calibration, and Robustness ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.4</span></a>), so that fraction is read as an
absolute population. The two are not interchangeable and are never
pooled.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Reading discipline.</h5>

<div id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The overlap subsection is written as a registry. Each entry is a measured
overlap between pocket membership and one indicator; the entries are not
treated as evidence for one another, and none of them supports a
statement about what pocket membership represents.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.1 </span>Census and Residence</h3>

<section id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Group-level census.</h5>

<div id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The census covers <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="123" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>123</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">123</annotation></semantics></math> anchors at <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>k-step spacing for both 70M and
160M. The population is stratified by segment and, within a segment,
concentrated in a few layers: averaging the bulk-segment share over
anchors, 70M runs from <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.056" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.056</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.056</annotation></semantics></math> at layer 2 to <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.173" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.173</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.173</annotation></semantics></math> at layer 4, and 160M
from <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.046" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.046</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.046</annotation></semantics></math> at layer 5 to <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.155" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.155</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.155</annotation></semantics></math> at layer 11, a factor of about three
between the quietest and the busiest layer at both sizes.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Stability follows the same stratification.
Table <a href="#A4.T8" title="Table 8 ‣ Size-ordered timing. ‣ D.2 Emergence and Survival ‣ Appendix D Pocket Trajectories, Persistence, and Overlap Registrations ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> reports membership overlap between
consecutive anchors together with residence run lengths. Vector and <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="qkv" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">qkv</annotation></semantics></math>
pockets are close to persistent (vector Jaccard <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.000</annotation></semantics></math> at <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k{=}1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k{=}1</annotation></semantics></math>, with
residence median <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="7.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>7.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7.5</annotation></semantics></math> anchors at 70M and maximum <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="62" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>62</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">62</annotation></semantics></math> at 160M; <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="qkv" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">qkv</annotation></semantics></math>
Jaccard <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".875" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>.875</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.875</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".842" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>.842</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.842</annotation></semantics></math>, with residence median <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5</annotation></semantics></math> at 70M, <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{95}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>95</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{95}</annotation></semantics></math> of
<math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="19" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>19</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">19</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>20</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">20</annotation></semantics></math>, and maximum <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="56" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>56</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">56</annotation></semantics></math>), attention-output is intermediate
(<math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".333" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>.333</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.333</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".476" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>.476</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.476</annotation></semantics></math>), and MLP pockets are strongly transient (Jaccard
<math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".141" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>.141</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.141</annotation></semantics></math> at both sizes, residence median <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> anchor).</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Counted over residence runs rather than over segments, the population is
dominated by the MLP: <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="103{,}465" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>103,465</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">103{,}465</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="104{,}030" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>104,030</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">104{,}030</annotation></semantics></math> runs at 70M and
<math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="239{,}191" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>239,191</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">239{,}191</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="240{,}808" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>240,808</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">240{,}808</annotation></semantics></math> at 160M, more than <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="99\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>99</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">99\%</annotation></semantics></math> at both sizes, and
those runs have median length one anchor. The transient majority reported
in Section 4.2 is therefore a statement about the pocket
population by count, and the segment-resolved view here is what the same
sentence means by persistence varying with parameter role.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Multi-pass recomputation.</h5>

<div id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The same census recomputed on two vision runs with the same functional
units, over anchors <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="45" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>45</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">45</annotation></semantics></math> at <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau{=}5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau{=}5</annotation></semantics></math> epochs, moves in opposite
directions for the two architectures. On ViT-mid the MLP, vector, and
<math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="qkv" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">qkv</annotation></semantics></math> shares decay (<math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".233\to.104" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>.233</mn><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>.104</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.233\to.104</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".250\to.095" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>.250</mn><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>.095</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.250\to.095</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".219\to.182" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>.219</mn><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>.182</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.219\to.182</annotation></semantics></math> from the
early to the tail period) while the patch share rises steeply
(<math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".194\to.487\to.791" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>.194</mn><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>.487</mn><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>.791</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.194\to.487\to.791</annotation></semantics></math>). On ResNet both convolutional families rise
(<math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3{\times}3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3{\times}3</annotation></semantics></math> <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".143\to.381\to.472" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>.143</mn><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>.381</mn><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>.472</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.143\to.381\to.472</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{\times}1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{\times}1</annotation></semantics></math> <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".106\to.162\to.261" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>.106</mn><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>.162</mn><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>.261</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.106\to.162\to.261</annotation></semantics></math>)
while the vector share decays (<math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".283\to.100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>.283</mn><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>.100</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.283\to.100</annotation></semantics></math>). Adjacent-anchor Jaccard is
<math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".658" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>.658</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.658</annotation></semantics></math> for ViT-mid <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="qkv" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">qkv</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".733" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>.733</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.733</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".750" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>.750</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.750</annotation></semantics></math> for vector groups, <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".480" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>.480</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.480</annotation></semantics></math> for
ViT-mid MLP, <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".446" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>.446</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.446</annotation></semantics></math> for ResNet <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3{\times}3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3{\times}3</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".244" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>.244</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.244</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{\times}1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{\times}1</annotation></semantics></math>.
The frozen-coordinate fraction is zero throughout both runs, so no
reading in this census is carried by inactive units.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Two riders travel with the cross-regime comparison. The time unit
differs: one pretraining anchor spans about <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.8\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.8</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.8\%</annotation></semantics></math> of training against
about <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\%</annotation></semantics></math> for one vision epoch, so the sparser vision sampling
mechanically depresses its Jaccard values. The contrast that survives
that bias is the transient MLP population (<math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".141" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>.141</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.141</annotation></semantics></math> against ViT-mid MLP
<math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".480" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>.480</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.480</annotation></semantics></math>), which runs against the direction of the bias; the <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="qkv" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">qkv</annotation></semantics></math> contrast
is partly attributable to it. And a blanket reading that one-pass pockets
are more stable does not hold, because the stratification pattern itself
differs between the two regimes.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Dependence on the unit.</h5>

<div id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Persistence is a property of the unit as much as of the run. Under a
top-<math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math> <em id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">group</em>-level agreement definition, the transfer family gives
cross-run Jaccard <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.115" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.115</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.115</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.135" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.135</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.135</annotation></semantics></math> against a chance level of <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.111" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.111</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.111</annotation></semantics></math>,
with a within-run adjacent-anchor ceiling of only <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.127" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.127</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.127</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.156" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.156</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.156</annotation></semantics></math>: at
that unit the objects have almost no memory. Moving to <em id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">tensor</em>-level
units on the same runs, at the same chance level, gives within-run
persistence <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.57" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.57</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.57</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.73" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.73</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.73</annotation></semantics></math> in every condition. On the tensor-level
definition the late-training pocket location is also conserved across
transfer regimes: the three continuing-descent arms converge to <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.57" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.57</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.57</annotation></semantics></math> to
<math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.71" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.71</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.71</annotation></semantics></math> against a same-anchor cross-seed reference band of <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.58" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.58</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.58</annotation></semantics></math> to
<math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.80" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.80</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.80</annotation></semantics></math>, while at early anchors every cross-regime overlap sits at <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.23" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.23</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.23</annotation></semantics></math>
to <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.38" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.38</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.38</annotation></semantics></math>, far below the band, and the two anti-persistent arms stay
below it throughout. We register that as a time-resolved reading: early
pocket locations are regime-specific and late ones are not.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.2 </span>Emergence and Survival</h3>

<section id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Size-ordered timing.</h5>

<div id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A4.T9" title="Table 9 ‣ Size-ordered timing. ‣ D.2 Emergence and Survival ‣ Appendix D Pocket Trajectories, Persistence, and Overlap Registrations ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a> collects the row-level emergence readings
for five sizes and Figure <a href="#A4.F9" title="Figure 9 ‣ Size-ordered timing. ‣ D.2 Emergence and Survival ‣ Appendix D Pocket Trajectories, Persistence, and Overlap Registrations ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a> shows the underlying
depth-by-time maps. Both the pool-coherence onset, which is where the
null line descends, and the row-level pocket onset move later with model
size, and the two do not move together. 70M has both at <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>20</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">20</annotation></semantics></math>k. 160M has a
two-stage null-line descent, moderate at <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="13" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>13</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">13</annotation></semantics></math>k and deep over about <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="72" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>72</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">72</annotation></semantics></math>
to <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="76" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>76</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">76</annotation></semantics></math>k, with pocket onset at <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>20</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">20</annotation></semantics></math>k. 410M has pocket onset at <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="48" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>48</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">48</annotation></semantics></math>k with
the null-line onset only at <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="92" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>92</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">92</annotation></semantics></math>k. Neither 1B nor 1.4B meets either
criterion inside the <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="129" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>129</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">129</annotation></semantics></math>k window. The ordering is not a function of
parameter count alone: at equal width <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2048" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2048</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2048</annotation></semantics></math> the deeper model starts
(1.4B, <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="24" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>24</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">24</annotation></semantics></math> layers, rising from about <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>100</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">100</annotation></semantics></math>k) while the shallower one
does not (1B, <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>16</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16</annotation></semantics></math> layers), and at equal depth <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="24" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>24</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">24</annotation></semantics></math> the narrower model
starts much earlier (410M at <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="48" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>48</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">48</annotation></semantics></math>k against 1.4B at the window edge).</p>
</div>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 8: </span>Pocket stability across training regimes. Top: Jaccard overlap of
pocket membership between consecutive anchors (<math id="A4.T8.m62" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k{=}1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k{=}1</annotation></semantics></math>, median over
anchors), at the group-level unit defined at the start of
Appendix <a href="#A4" title="Appendix D Pocket Trajectories, Persistence, and Overlap Registrations ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D</span></a>. Bottom: residence run lengths on the
pretraining side, counting consecutive anchors a group spends inside the
pocket set, with <math id="A4.T8.m63" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> the number of runs. Stability is stratified by segment
and the stratification pattern differs between the two regimes, so a blanket
ordering between them does not hold. At <math id="A4.T8.m64" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k{=}1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k{=}1</annotation></semantics></math> one pretraining anchor spans
about <math id="A4.T8.m65" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.8\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.8</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.8\%</annotation></semantics></math> of training against about <math id="A4.T8.m66" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\%</annotation></semantics></math> for one vision epoch, so the
sparser vision sampling mechanically depresses its values; the transient MLP
contrast runs against that bias and is the most robust entry. These overlaps
are registered as descriptions of pocket dynamics under the two regimes and
are not treated as cross-regime confirmation of a shared mechanism.</figcaption>
</figure>

<tr id="A4.T9.1.9" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A4.T9.1.9.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_tt" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;" colspan="7">
<span id="A4.T9.1.9.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:490.7pt;">
<span id="A4.T9.1.9.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.T9.1.9.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Criteria.</span> Null-line onset: the pooled membership-resample
<math id="A4.T9.m54" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{05}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>q</mi><mn>05</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{05}</annotation></semantics></math> of qkv FRR (layer level, <math id="A4.T9.m55" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau{=}5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau{=}5</annotation></semantics></math>, raw; median over layers)
stays below <math id="A4.T9.m56" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.90" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.90</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.90</annotation></semantics></math> for five consecutive <math id="A4.T9.m57" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>k anchors. Pocket onset: some
layer’s row-level <math id="A4.T9.m58" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{FRR}{&lt;}0.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>FRR</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0.7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{FRR}{&lt;}0.7</annotation></semantics></math> fraction stays above <math id="A4.T9.m59" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5\%</annotation></semantics></math> for
three consecutive anchors of the <math id="A4.T9.m60" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>k row-scan grid. Peak = maximum over
(layer, anchor) of the row-level <math id="A4.T9.m61" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{FRR}{&lt;}0.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>FRR</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0.7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{FRR}{&lt;}0.7</annotation></semantics></math> fraction; “later
wave” is the largest reading after the main peak’s anchor. At these
group sizes the membership-resample pass rate at <math id="A4.T9.m62" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta{=}0.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta{=}0.7</annotation></semantics></math> is
<math id="A4.T9.m63" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\approx}0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≈</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\approx}0</annotation></semantics></math>, so the fractions are read as absolute rather than as excess
over a null. <span id="A4.T9.1.9.1.1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Notes.</span> <sup id="A4.T9.1.9.1.1.1.3" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A4.T9.1.9.1.1.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">†</span></sup>160M descends in two stages
(moderate at <math id="A4.T9.m65" class="ltx_Math" alttext="13" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>13</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">13</annotation></semantics></math>k, deep at <math id="A4.T9.m66" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\sim}72" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>∼</mo><mn>72</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\sim}72</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="A4.T9.m67" class="ltx_Math" alttext="76" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>76</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">76</annotation></semantics></math>k); the deep stage sits near
this run’s smoothed loss minimum (<math id="A4.T9.m68" class="ltx_Math" alttext="77.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>77.3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">77.3</annotation></semantics></math>k). <sup id="A4.T9.1.9.1.1.1.4" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A4.T9.1.9.1.1.1.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">‡</span></sup>1.4B does not
meet the three-anchor criterion inside the window: its row-level fraction
starts rising at <math id="A4.T9.m70" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\sim}100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>∼</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\sim}100</annotation></semantics></math>k in L11–L15/L21/L23 and reaches <math id="A4.T9.m71" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3.0\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3.0</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.0\%</annotation></semantics></math> at
the window edge (<math id="A4.T9.m72" class="ltx_Math" alttext="128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>128</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">128</annotation></semantics></math>k) while still increasing, so this is a window-edge case rather
than a negative reading. 1B is read with the checkpoint-<math id="A4.T9.m73" class="ltx_Math" alttext="116000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>116000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">116000</annotation></semantics></math> masking
window applied (anchors whose <math id="A4.T9.m74" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau{=}5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau{=}5</annotation></semantics></math> window uses that checkpoint as
base or history, <math id="A4.T9.m75" class="ltx_Math" alttext="116" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>116</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">116</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="A4.T9.m76" class="ltx_Math" alttext="121" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>121</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">121</annotation></semantics></math>k, plus the future endpoint <math id="A4.T9.m77" class="ltx_Math" alttext="111" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>111</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">111</annotation></semantics></math>k; <math id="A4.T9.m78" class="ltx_Math" alttext="7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>7</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7</annotation></semantics></math> of
<math id="A4.T9.m79" class="ltx_Math" alttext="123" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>123</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">123</annotation></semantics></math> anchors dropped); its row-level fraction stays <math id="A4.T9.m80" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\leq}0.33\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mn>0.33</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\leq}0.33\%</annotation></semantics></math>
throughout the remaining window. 1B is registered
here for completeness but is left out of the cross-scale trend
figures and of the cross-scale appendix: it is the one suite member
trained in bf16 rather than fp16, and at <math id="A4.T9.m81" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16\times 2048" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>16</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>2048</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16\times 2048</annotation></semantics></math> its depth
ordering crosses the parameter-count ordering, so it does not sit on
the depth/width axis those readings use. Released checkpoint dtype is
fp16 at every size, so the container precision our pipeline reads is
not special for 1B. attn_out row scans exist for 70M/160M
only (410M/1B/1.4B requested); groups are flattened on
<math id="A4.T9.m82" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(d_{\mathrm{model}},d_{\mathrm{head}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>model</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>head</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(d_{\mathrm{model}},d_{\mathrm{head}})</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="A4.T9.m83" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{\mathrm{head}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>head</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{\mathrm{head}}</annotation></semantics></math> as the
unit, a convention less clean than for qkv (70M <math id="A4.T9.m84" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D{=}64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D{=}64</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math id="A4.T9.m85" class="ltx_Math" alttext="19.3\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>19.3</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">19.3\%</annotation></semantics></math>
vs. <math id="A4.T9.m86" class="ltx_Math" alttext="13.1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>13.1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">13.1\%</annotation></semantics></math> at <math id="A4.T9.m87" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D{=}512" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>512</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D{=}512</annotation></semantics></math>; 160M <math id="A4.T9.m88" class="ltx_Math" alttext="15.7\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>15.7</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">15.7\%</annotation></semantics></math> vs. <math id="A4.T9.m89" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16.7\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>16.7</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16.7\%</annotation></semantics></math>). The mlp column
reports the out-half (<math id="A4.T9.m90" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{\mathrm{out}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>out</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{\mathrm{out}}</annotation></semantics></math> columns) cut, the only mlp cut
carrying signal: in-half and magnitude cuts peak at <math id="A4.T9.m91" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\leq}1.6\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mn>1.6</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\leq}1.6\%</annotation></semantics></math> and
<math id="A4.T9.m92" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\leq}0.12\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mn>0.12</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\leq}0.12\%</annotation></semantics></math> across all five sizes, and the mlp carrier is the deepest
layer in every size. The row-length convention is invariant over
<math id="A4.T9.m93" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D{=}128..3072" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>128..3072</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D{=}128..3072</annotation></semantics></math>, so no per-size adjustment is applied. Large-size mlp
readings are quoted from full-protocol scans only; the <math id="A4.T9.m94" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10\%</annotation></semantics></math>-sampled
preview lane is not quoted as an S2 reading. All entries are single-run
readings on the public Pythia checkpoint series, registered as
descriptions of those runs.</span>
</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 9: </span>Row-level emergence readings across five pretraining scales, with
the onset criteria and the per-segment conventions given in the table
footer.</figcaption>
</figure>
