<section id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Signed norm-change proxy.</h5>

<div id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A signed norm-change proxy <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{i}=\sum_{t}w_{i}(t)\Delta w_{i}(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>t</mi></msub><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{i}=\sum_{t}w_{i}(t)\Delta w_{i}(t)</annotation></semantics></math> is built from checkpoint differences alone; preconditioning is not removed, and <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math> is not a
curvature-based importance measure. Against an equal-cardinality
hypergeometric null, <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="qkv" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">qkv</annotation></semantics></math> pocket coordinates overlap the top-<math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math>
movement set well above the null band (<math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="4.0\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>4.0</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.0\times</annotation></semantics></math> at <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="70" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>70</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">70</annotation></semantics></math>k, <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="9.0\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>9.0</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9.0\times</annotation></semantics></math>
at <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="129" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>129</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">129</annotation></semantics></math>k), the ViT-mid magnitude-bin families sit just above their upper
bound (<math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".142" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>.142</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.142</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".217" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>.217</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.217</annotation></semantics></math> against <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".125" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>.125</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.125</annotation></semantics></math>), ResNet <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3{\times}3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3{\times}3</annotation></semantics></math> exceeds its
bound by only <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.04" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.04</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.04</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m14" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.08\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.08</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.08\times</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{\times}1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{\times}1</annotation></semantics></math> falls below it
(Figure <a href="#A4.F13" title="Figure 13 ‣ Signed norm-change proxy. ‣ D.4 Overlap Registrations ‣ Appendix D Pocket Trajectories, Persistence, and Overlap Registrations ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a>). The attention output projection reverses at
late anchors, with its terminal pocket set displaced towards the low end
of the signed movement axis.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A4.F13" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2608.15483v1/app04_o1_movement_overlap.svg" id="A4.F13.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:698/274;" width="698" height="274"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 13: </span>Overlap between pocket coordinates and the top-<math id="A4.F13.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> set of the signed norm-change proxy, labelled movement in the panels, registered against an equal-cardinality hypergeometric null.
The proxy <math id="A4.F13.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{i}=\sum_{t}w_{i}(t)\Delta w_{i}(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>t</mi></msub><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{i}=\sum_{t}w_{i}(t)\Delta w_{i}(t)</annotation></semantics></math> is built from checkpoint
differences alone; preconditioning is not removed and <math id="A4.F13.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math> is not a
curvature-based importance measure. (a) observed precision of the top-<math id="A4.F13.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math>
movement set restricted to pocket coordinates, against the null <math id="A4.F13.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K/N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K/N</annotation></semantics></math> and
its <math id="A4.F13.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="95\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>95</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">95\%</annotation></semantics></math> interval, with the pretraining rows annotated by the ratio.
(b) quantile position of the pocket coordinates inside their family’s
movement distribution, with the diagonal as the no-association reference;
the <math id="A4.F13.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="qkv" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">qkv</annotation></semantics></math> set at <math id="A4.F13.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="129" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>129</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">129</annotation></semantics></math>k sits at median quantile <math id="A4.F13.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".93" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>.93</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.93</annotation></semantics></math> against about <math id="A4.F13.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".50" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>.50</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.50</annotation></semantics></math>
for the vision reference, so the whole set is displaced rather than a tail
of it. Pocket sets are the group-level flag at <math id="A4.F13.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau{=}5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau{=}5</annotation></semantics></math>, raw, head
granularity. The two anchors carry different pocket sets in both size and
membership, so a two-anchor comparison mixes a change in overlap with
turnover of the set itself. Each reading is a registration of a measured
overlap and is not used to support any statement about what pocket
membership represents.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Because the pocket sets themselves change size and membership over time,
the overlap is also measured anchor by anchor
(Figure <a href="#A4.F14" title="Figure 14 ‣ Signed norm-change proxy. ‣ D.4 Overlap Registrations ‣ Appendix D Pocket Trajectories, Persistence, and Overlap Registrations ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">14</span></a>). On <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="qkv" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">qkv</annotation></semantics></math> the ratio hugs the random line
before the collapse (<math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.98" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.98</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.98</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.25" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.25</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.25</annotation></semantics></math> over <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>7</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="19" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>19</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">19</annotation></semantics></math>k, when the set
holds <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="51" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>51</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">51</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>64</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">64</annotation></semantics></math> groups) and steps to <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3.77" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3.77</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.77</annotation></semantics></math> at <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>20</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">20</annotation></semantics></math>k, staying high for
the rest of training (cumulative median <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.m10" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="7.5\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>7.5</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7.5\times</annotation></semantics></math>, recent-window median
<math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.m11" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="9.6\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>9.6</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9.6\times</annotation></semantics></math> with a maximum of <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.m12" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="16.2\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>16.2</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16.2\times</annotation></semantics></math> at <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="23" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>23</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">23</annotation></semantics></math>k). ViT-mid patch
filters sit slightly above the band early and inside it from epoch <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="23" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>23</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">23</annotation></semantics></math>
apart from single-epoch excursions; ResNet <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3{\times}3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3{\times}3</annotation></semantics></math> sits
<em id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">below</em> the band over epochs <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>9</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>16</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16</annotation></semantics></math> and above it from epoch
<math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="17" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>17</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">17</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A4.F14" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2608.15483v1/app04_o3_overlap_time.svg" id="A4.F14.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:698/244;" width="698" height="244"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 14: </span>The same overlap resolved anchor by anchor, with the pocket set
re-matched at every anchor. The readout is the ratio of the observed
overlap to its hypergeometric expectation, with the grey band giving the
null <math id="A4.F14.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="95\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>95</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">95\%</annotation></semantics></math> interval. Two time conventions for the movement proxy are
reported side by side: one accumulates from the start of training, the
other over the last five checkpoint or epoch pairs, matching the probe’s
history window. (a) <math id="A4.F14.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="qkv" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">qkv</annotation></semantics></math>: the ratio hugs the random line over <math id="A4.F14.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>7</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7</annotation></semantics></math> to
<math id="A4.F14.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="19" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>19</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">19</annotation></semantics></math>k, steps to <math id="A4.F14.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3.77" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3.77</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.77</annotation></semantics></math> at <math id="A4.F14.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>20</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">20</annotation></semantics></math>k in one anchor, and stays high for the rest
of training. (b) the attention output projection, on small sets with heavy
turnover, where the two time conventions disagree and both are reported.
(c) ViT-mid patch filters sit slightly above the band early and inside it
from epoch <math id="A4.F14.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="23" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>23</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">23</annotation></semantics></math> apart from single-epoch excursions; the late approach to
one has a mechanical component, since the cut approaches saturation.
(d) ResNet <math id="A4.F14.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3{\times}3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3{\times}3</annotation></semantics></math> sits below the band over epochs <math id="A4.F14.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>9</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A4.F14.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>16</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16</annotation></semantics></math> and
above it from epoch <math id="A4.F14.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="17" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>17</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">17</annotation></semantics></math>. Every curve is a registration of a measured
overlap over time.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Normalization gain outliers.</h5>

<div id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Coordinates whose normalization gain is a robust-<math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math> outlier above <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math> at
the late anchor have higher median ESA than their non-outlier neighbours
in <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="12" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>12</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">12</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="13" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>13</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">13</annotation></semantics></math> pretraining tensors and higher median coherence in <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="11" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>11</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">11</annotation></semantics></math>
of <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="13" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>13</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">13</annotation></semantics></math>, with the rank correlation between the outlier score and
coherence between <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".78" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>.78</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.78</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".94" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>.94</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.94</annotation></semantics></math> in those <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="11" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>11</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">11</annotation></semantics></math> and negative in the two
exceptions (Figure <a href="#A4.F15" title="Figure 15 ‣ Normalization gain outliers. ‣ D.4 Overlap Registrations ‣ Appendix D Pocket Trajectories, Persistence, and Overlap Registrations ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">15</span></a>). A top-<math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1\%</annotation></semantics></math> control cut reproduces
every direction including the exceptions. Outlier sets overlap across
layers mainly between adjacent normalization pairs (median Jaccard
<math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".023" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>.023</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.023</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{90}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>90</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{90}</annotation></semantics></math> <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>.32</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.32</annotation></semantics></math>). Their formation times are not monotone: sets
grow from early training and first reach half of their final membership
between <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="11" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>11</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">11</annotation></semantics></math>k and <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="101" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>101</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">101</annotation></semantics></math>k depending on the tensor. On the ViT-mid control
the gain range is narrow and the outlier sets hold at most four
coordinates, and two of its three chains read with the opposite sign. The
final normalization tensor is saturated, with agreement and coherence
both at <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.0</annotation></semantics></math> on all <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="512" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>512</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">512</annotation></semantics></math> coordinates, and carries no resolution.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A4.F15" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2608.15483v1/app04_o2_ln_timeline.svg" id="A4.F15.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:698/454;" width="698" height="454"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 15: </span>Normalization gain outliers and per-coordinate dynamics on the
same gain trajectories. A coordinate is an outlier when the robust <math id="A4.F15.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math> of
its absolute gain at the late anchor exceeds <math id="A4.F15.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math>. (a) and (b) per-tensor
medians for outlier against non-outlier coordinates across the <math id="A4.F15.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="13" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>13</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">13</annotation></semantics></math>
pretraining gain vectors: median ESA is higher for the outliers in <math id="A4.F15.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="12" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>12</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">12</annotation></semantics></math> of
<math id="A4.F15.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="13" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>13</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">13</annotation></semantics></math> tensors and median drift coherence in <math id="A4.F15.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="11" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>11</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">11</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="A4.F15.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="13" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>13</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">13</annotation></semantics></math>, with connectors
marking the tensors where it is not. The final normalization tensor is
saturated, with agreement and coherence equal to <math id="A4.F15.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.0</annotation></semantics></math> on all <math id="A4.F15.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="512" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>512</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">512</annotation></semantics></math>
coordinates, so it carries no resolution and is drawn only for
completeness. (c) rank correlation between the outlier score and coherence
per tensor, positive in <math id="A4.F15.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="11" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>11</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">11</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="A4.F15.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="13" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>13</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">13</annotation></semantics></math> pretraining tensors and negative in
two. On the ViT-mid control one chain reads with the same sign and the
others with the opposite sign; its gain range is narrow and its outlier
sets hold at most four coordinates. A top-<math id="A4.F15.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1\%</annotation></semantics></math> control cut reproduces
every direction in both regimes.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Low-participation heads.</h5>

<div id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Eighteen <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="qkv" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">qkv</annotation></semantics></math> heads fall below the pooled-bulk fence on
dimension-normalized participation ratio; eight of them are 70M layer-4
q-heads, and the seven lowest are exactly the <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="70" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>70</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">70</annotation></semantics></math>k pocket set.
Participation ratio and pocket flag are computed from the same update
history, so this is registered as a co-location of two readouts of one
record.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Cross-probe overlap at group level.</h5>

<div id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">On the vision structural cuts the three group-level probes concentrate on
overlapping populations. Conditioning on <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{FRR}&lt;0.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>FRR</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0.7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{FRR}&lt;0.7</annotation></semantics></math> raises the
<math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{VCS}&gt;0.4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>VCS</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0.4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{VCS}&gt;0.4</annotation></semantics></math> rate from a base of <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="38.9\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>38.9</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">38.9\%</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="88.4\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>88.4</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">88.4\%</annotation></semantics></math> on ViT-mid,
and raises the <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{ESA}&gt;0.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ESA</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0.7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{ESA}&gt;0.7</annotation></semantics></math> rate by <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m6" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="3.4\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3.4</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.4\times</annotation></semantics></math> on ViT-mid to
<math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m7" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="23.8\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>23.8</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">23.8\times</annotation></semantics></math> on ResNet; all three thresholds are passed simultaneously by
<math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6.7\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>6.7</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6.7\%</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3.3\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3.3</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.3\%</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.3\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.3</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.3\%</annotation></semantics></math> of ViT-mid, ViT, and ResNet groups. At
these group sizes the thresholds are chance-immune. The three probes read
the same update history and are not independent instruments, and their
time profiles separate: pooled ESA and VCS shares decay monotonically
from <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="18.4\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>18.4</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">18.4\%</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="49.0\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>49.0</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">49.0\%</annotation></semantics></math> at anchor <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.9\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.9</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.9\%</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6.1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>6.1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6.1\%</annotation></semantics></math> at anchor
<math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="40" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>40</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">40</annotation></semantics></math>, while the FRR share peaks at anchors <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>20</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">20</annotation></semantics></math>. The
learning-rate schedule is not disentangled from these profiles.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Loss-curve landmarks.</h5>

<div id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The transition markers co-locate in time with loss-curve landmarks at
both sizes (70M: calibrated fade near <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>20</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">20</annotation></semantics></math>k, smoothed loss minimum
<math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="49.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>49.7</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">49.7</annotation></semantics></math>k, main row-level wave <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="80" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>80</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">80</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="85" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>85</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">85</annotation></semantics></math>k; 160M: loss minimum <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="77.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>77.3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">77.3</annotation></semantics></math>k,
deep null-line descent about <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="72" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>72</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">72</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A4.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="76" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>76</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">76</annotation></semantics></math>k). This is one run per size,
the loss minima are read from smoothed curves with a rule-dependent
resolution, and the event windows are wide relative to the anchor
spacing. The co-location is discussed in Section 4.3 and is
registered here only for completeness.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A5" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix E </span>Movement Directedness and Gradient-Coherence Correspondence</h2>

<div id="A5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Section 4.3 compares the probe readings with two quantities
that are defined without reference to any probe, and reports the
correlations <math id="A5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho=0.978" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.978</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho=0.978</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho=0.804" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.804</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho=0.804</annotation></semantics></math>. This appendix gives the two
definitions, their relation to existing gradient-coherence and
signal-to-noise measures, and the comparison in full.</p>
</div>
<section id="A5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.1 </span>Two Externally Defined Quantities</h3>

<section id="A5.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Movement directedness.</h5>

<div id="A5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For an anchor <math id="A5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math> and horizon <math id="A5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>, movement directedness is the net
displacement of the future window divided by the path length actually
travelled inside it,</p>
<table id="A5.E5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A5.E5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MD}_{S}(a,\tau)=\frac{\bigl\lVert w_{a+\tau,S}-w_{a,S}\bigr\rVert_{2}}{\sum_{t=a}^{a+\tau-1}\bigl\lVert\Delta w_{t,S}\bigr\rVert_{2}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>MD</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><mi>w</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>w</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em">∥</mo><msub><mrow></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0em">∑</mo><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>w</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em">∥</mo><msub><mrow></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MD}_{S}(a,\tau)=\frac{\bigl\lVert w_{a+\tau,S}-w_{a,S}\bigr\rVert_{2}}{\sum_{t=a}^{a+\tau-1}\bigl\lVert\Delta w_{t,S}\bigr\rVert_{2}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(5)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">It lies in <math id="A5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math>, equals one when the window is traversed in a straight
line, and falls towards zero when the steps cancel. It is a property of
the realized trajectory alone: no probe, no history window, and no model
of the dynamics enters it. It is also not causally prior to the probes,
since both read the same stored weights; the comparison below is a
correspondence between two summaries of one record.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Loss-side gradient coherence.</h5>

<div id="A5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The second quantity is built only from scalar training telemetry. Over
the same window it compares the realized loss decrease with the loss
decrease that the same gradient magnitudes would have produced had every
step been perfectly aligned,</p>
<table id="A5.E6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A5.E6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{GC}(a,\tau)=\frac{L_{a-1}-L_{a+\tau-1}}{\bigl(\sum_{s\in W}\eta_{s}\bigr)\;\bigl\langle\lVert g_{s}\rVert_{2}^{2}\bigr\rangle_{s\in W}}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>GC</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><msub><mo lspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>W</mi></mrow></msub><msub><mi>η</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.280em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∥</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∥</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>W</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{GC}(a,\tau)=\frac{L_{a-1}-L_{a+\tau-1}}{\bigl(\sum_{s\in W}\eta_{s}\bigr)\;\bigl\langle\lVert g_{s}\rVert_{2}^{2}\bigr\rangle_{s\in W}},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(6)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>W</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W</annotation></semantics></math> is the set of optimization steps inside the window, <math id="A5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>η</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> is
the learning rate at step <math id="A5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> is the gradient restricted to the
bulk backbone. The numerator is read from the loss curve and the
denominator from recorded per-step learning rates and gradient norms, so
the estimate contains no parameter-direction information at all. This is
what makes it a non-circular comparison for a directional probe.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.2 </span>Relation to Existing Coherence and Noise Measures</h3>

<div id="A5.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Both quantities have close relatives in the literature, and the
differences matter for how the comparison should be read.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Gradient coherence in the sense of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chatterjee (2020)</a></cite> is
defined on <em id="A5.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">gradients</em>: it measures how much per-example gradients
agree with one another within a batch, and it requires access to those
per-example gradients. Equation (<a href="#A5.E6" title="In Loss-side gradient coherence. ‣ E.1 Two Externally Defined Quantities ‣ Appendix E Movement Directedness and Gradient-Coherence Correspondence ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>) instead reads coherence
off the loss curve, as the fraction of the available first-order decrease
that the optimizer actually realized, and needs only telemetry that a
training run already logs. It therefore measures agreement <em id="A5.SS2.p2.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">across
steps</em> within a window rather than across examples within a step, and the
two can come apart whenever the loss surface curves inside the window.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Movement directedness is a trajectory-level quantity of the kind studied
by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">Singh et al. (2025)</a></cite>, and it is related to, but not the
same as, the observation that optimization concentrates in a
low-dimensional subspace <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gur-Ari et al. 2018</a>)</cite>. A trajectory can stay
inside a small subspace while doubling back inside it, which lowers
Eq. (<a href="#A5.E5" title="In Movement directedness. ‣ E.1 Two Externally Defined Quantities ‣ Appendix E Movement Directedness and Gradient-Coherence Correspondence ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>) without changing the subspace, and this is exactly
the distinction that separates the displacement-direction family from the
subspace-residual family in Section 3. Values of
Eq. (<a href="#A5.E5" title="In Movement directedness. ‣ E.1 Two Externally Defined Quantities ‣ Appendix E Movement Directedness and Gradient-Coherence Correspondence ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>) well below one over short windows are also the
signature of the diffusion-like regimes described by
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib50" title="" class="ltx_ref">Mandt et al. (2017)</a></cite> and <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Feng and Tu (2021)</a></cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">None of these quantities is used here to certify another. They are
registered as independent summaries of the same stored trajectories.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.3 </span>The Full Comparison</h3>

<div id="A5.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A5.F16" title="Figure 16 ‣ E.3 The Full Comparison ‣ Appendix E Movement Directedness and Gradient-Coherence Correspondence ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">16</span></a> shows both comparisons over the transfer
family of Appendix <a href="#A1.SS2" title="A.2 Additional Run Families ‣ Appendix A Experimental Coverage and Protocol Details ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.2</span></a>, on the bulk backbone scope at
<math id="A5.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau=5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau=5</annotation></semantics></math>: eight training conditions, five anchors each, over the seeds of
that family. The conditions differ in dataset, in whether the run is
fine-tuned or trained from scratch, in learning rate, and in schedule, so
the grid deliberately mixes regimes that a single training curve would
not connect.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A5.F16" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2608.15483v1/supp_figures/A_state_collapse_v2.png" id="A5.F16.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:656/285;" width="656" height="285" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 16: </span>Probe readings against two externally defined summaries of
realized optimization, over the eight conditions and five anchors of the
transfer family, on the bulk backbone scope at <math id="A5.F16.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau{=}5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau{=}5</annotation></semantics></math>. (a) ESA
against movement directedness, Eq. (<a href="#A5.E5" title="In Movement directedness. ‣ E.1 Two Externally Defined Quantities ‣ Appendix E Movement Directedness and Gradient-Coherence Correspondence ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>), the net
displacement of the future window divided by the path length travelled
inside it. (b) ESA against the loss-side gradient-coherence estimate,
Eq. (<a href="#A5.E6" title="In Loss-side gradient coherence. ‣ E.1 Two Externally Defined Quantities ‣ Appendix E Movement Directedness and Gradient-Coherence Correspondence ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>), which is built from the loss curve, the per-step
learning rates, and the per-step gradient norms, and carries no
parameter-direction information. Horizontal lines mark the random
sign-agreement level of <math id="A5.F16.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5</annotation></semantics></math>. Conditions differ in dataset, in whether
the run is fine-tuned or trained from scratch, in learning rate, and in
schedule. Both relations are retrospective correspondences between
summaries of the same stored trajectories.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A5.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Across that grid ESA forms a tight monotone relation with movement
directedness (<math id="A5.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho=0.978" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.978</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho=0.978</annotation></semantics></math>). Trajectories whose future window covers more
net distance relative to its path length retain more coordinate-wise
directional agreement, and conditions that sit far apart in loss, learning
rate, and dataset fall on one curve. The association with the loss-side
coherence estimate is weaker but still strong (<math id="A5.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho=0.804" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.804</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho=0.804</annotation></semantics></math>), which is
what should be expected of a quantity that discards all directional
information and keeps only the scalar bookkeeping.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Two readings follow. The probes respond to the realized geometry of
parameter motion rather than to checkpoint index, since the grid contains
conditions at very different points of very different schedules. And the
sub-<math id="A5.SS3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5</annotation></semantics></math> regimes that Section 4.3 reports in the pretraining
case study correspond to low directedness, that is, to windows whose steps
substantially cancel, rather than to an absence of measurable structure.</p>
</div>
<section id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Scope.</h5>

<div id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Both relations are retrospective and observational. The comparison is on
the vision side only, at one horizon and one scope, and the two quantities
are computed from the same stored trajectories as the probes, so a high
correlation registers consistency between summaries and not an independent
confirmation. The loss-side estimate additionally inherits every
confound of the loss curve it is read from, including schedule shape and
batch composition.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A6" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix F </span>Pythia Scale Extensions</h2>

<div id="A6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Section 4.3 uses Pythia-70M as its case study and defers the
rest to this appendix. Six sizes enter the cross-scale registry, and every
statement below is a registration of readings and co-occurrences rather
than a directional claim.</p>
</div>
<section id="A6.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.1 </span>Coverage and Protocol</h3>

<div id="A6.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The six sizes are 14M, 31M, 70M, 160M, 410M, and 1.4B. They share the
pretraining schedule that makes step numbers comparable: <math id="A6.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="143{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>143,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">143{,}000</annotation></semantics></math>
optimizer steps, a single cosine decay whose decay length equals the
training length so that there is no constant tail, a <math id="A6.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1\%</annotation></semantics></math> warmup of
<math id="A6.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}430" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,430</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}430</annotation></semantics></math> steps, a floor at <math id="A6.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10\%</annotation></semantics></math> of the peak rate, decoupled weight decay
<math id="A6.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.1</annotation></semantics></math> with normalization parameters and all biases exempt, and a global
batch of <math id="A6.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1024" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1024</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1024</annotation></semantics></math> sequences of <math id="A6.SS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2048" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2048</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2048</annotation></semantics></math> tokens, or <math id="A6.SS1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2{,}097{,}152" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2,097,152</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2{,}097{,}152</annotation></semantics></math> tokens per
step. Peak learning rate is the one recipe quantity that varies with size,
from <math id="A6.SS1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.0\times 10^{-3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.0</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.0\times 10^{-3}</annotation></semantics></math> at the three smallest to <math id="A6.SS1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.0\times 10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2.0</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.0\times 10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math> at
1.4B. Equal step therefore means equal token count, and the step-indexed
comparisons below are token-indexed comparisons as well. They are not
matched loss, matched compute, or matched training progress, and they
carry no further normalization.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The measurement protocol is identical at every size and is the one given
in Appendix <a href="#A1.SS3" title="A.3 Pretraining Checkpoint Coverage ‣ Appendix A Experimental Coverage and Protocol Details ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.3</span></a>: <math id="A6.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="123" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>123</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">123</annotation></semantics></math> anchors at steps <math id="A6.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="7000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>7000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7000</annotation></semantics></math> to
<math id="A6.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="129000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>129000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">129000</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A6.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{\mathrm{past}}=5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>past</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{\mathrm{past}}=5</annotation></semantics></math>, reference <math id="A6.SS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta w_{a-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta w_{a-1}</annotation></semantics></math>, Gavish–Donoho rank selection
on a <math id="A6.SS1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="256" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>256</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">256</annotation></semantics></math>-unit sample, raw and column-normalized FRR in parallel, a
per-anchor membership-resample null, and the calibrated readout at
<math id="A6.SS1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=0.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.05</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=0.05</annotation></semantics></math> reported as excess. Table <a href="#A6.T11" title="Table 11 ‣ F.1 Coverage and Protocol ‣ Appendix F Pythia Scale Extensions ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a> collects
the per-size readings.</p>
</div>

</table></div><div class="ltx_flex_break"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1">
<p id="A6.T11.3" class="ltx_p ltx_figure_panel">Anchors are steps <math id="A6.T11.m28" class="ltx_Math" alttext="7000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>7000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7000</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A6.T11.m29" class="ltx_Math" alttext="129000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>129000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">129000</annotation></semantics></math> at spacing <math id="A6.T11.m30" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1000</annotation></semantics></math>, identical for every
size. Loss minima are recomputed from the public telemetry with a <math id="A6.T11.m31" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm 1500" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>1500</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm 1500</annotation></semantics></math>-step
rolling median. <sup id="A6.T11.3.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A6.T11.3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">a</span></sup> The smoothed 410M loss is still descending at the right
edge of the anchor domain (step <math id="A6.T11.m33" class="ltx_Math" alttext="128{,}756" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>128,756</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">128{,}756</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A6.T11.m34" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.175" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2.175</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.175</annotation></semantics></math>) and reaches <math id="A6.T11.m35" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.173" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2.173</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.173</annotation></semantics></math> at
step <math id="A6.T11.m36" class="ltx_Math" alttext="143" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>143</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">143</annotation></semantics></math>k, so no bottoming event occurs inside the window.
<sup id="A6.T11.3.2" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A6.T11.3.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">b</span></sup> The local 1.4B telemetry file does not match the released <math id="A6.T11.m38" class="ltx_Math" alttext="143" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>143</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">143</annotation></semantics></math>k-step cosine schedule, so no loss landmark is quoted.
Empty cells mean not read out on the full protocol; they are deliberately not
filled from the sampled-preview instrumentation.</p></div><div class="ltx_flex_break"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1">

<p id="A6.T11.6" class="ltx_p ltx_figure_panel">Onsets use persistence criteria rather than visual reading. Null-line onset:
<math id="A6.T11.m67" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{null}_{q05}&lt;0.90" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>null</mi><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>05</mn></mrow></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0.90</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{null}_{q05}&lt;0.90</annotation></semantics></math> for five consecutive anchors. Row pocket onset:
peak-layer share of rows with <math id="A6.T11.m68" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{FRR}&lt;0.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>FRR</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0.7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{FRR}&lt;0.7</annotation></semantics></math> above <math id="A6.T11.m69" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5\%</annotation></semantics></math> for three
consecutive anchors, on <math id="A6.T11.m70" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D{=}512" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>512</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D{=}512</annotation></semantics></math> qkv rows, with row-length invariance checked
over <math id="A6.T11.m71" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D\in[128,3072]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>128</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3072</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D\in[128,3072]</annotation></semantics></math> on three sizes. Segment-level collapse onset: one anchor
after the last anchor at which the pooled excess reaches half its early-phase
mean, declared only when the tail-phase mean has returned to the null level.
The 70M collapse is a single-anchor step: head-level layer-mean excess
<math id="A6.T11.m72" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.304\to-0.029" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.304</mn><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.029</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.304\to-0.029</annotation></semantics></math>, a change of <math id="A6.T11.m73" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.333" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.333</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.333</annotation></semantics></math> that is <math id="A6.T11.m74" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="3.7\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3.7</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.7\times</annotation></semantics></math> the next largest in
the series, with layers above chance falling from <math id="A6.T11.m75" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A6.T11.m76" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>; across it the real
head groups are unchanged (<math id="A6.T11.m77" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{FRR}_{p50}=0.994\pm 0.001" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>FRR</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>50</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>0.994</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0.001</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{FRR}_{p50}=0.994\pm 0.001</annotation></semantics></math>) while the null
moves (<math id="A6.T11.m78" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{null}_{q05}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>null</mi><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>05</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{null}_{q05}</annotation></semantics></math> from <math id="A6.T11.m79" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.994" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.994</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.994</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A6.T11.m80" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.67" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.67</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.67</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="A6.T11.m81" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.85" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.85</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.85</annotation></semantics></math>).
<sup id="A6.T11.6.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A6.T11.6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">c</span></sup> Where the series dips and recovers, the first crossing is given in
parentheses. <sup id="A6.T11.6.2" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A6.T11.6.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">d</span></sup> 1.4B has a mid-layer extinction window at <math id="A6.T11.m84" class="ltx_Math" alttext="95" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>95</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">95</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A6.T11.m85" class="ltx_Math" alttext="118" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>118</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">118</annotation></semantics></math>k,
with the calibrated readout at L11/L15/L21/L23 falling to <math id="A6.T11.m86" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.02" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.02</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.02</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="A6.T11.m87" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.27" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.27</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.27</annotation></semantics></math> near
<math id="A6.T11.m88" class="ltx_Math" alttext="96" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>96</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">96</annotation></semantics></math>k and recovering from about <math id="A6.T11.m89" class="ltx_Math" alttext="120" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>120</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">120</annotation></semantics></math>k, but no global collapse.
<sup id="A6.T11.6.3" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A6.T11.6.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">e</span></sup> The 1.4B row-level population reaches <math id="A6.T11.m91" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3.0\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3.0</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.0\%</annotation></semantics></math> at the last anchor and is
still rising there.
<span id="A6.T11.6.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">The two onset columns are different instruments and must not be
merged.</span> The null-line and row-pocket columns are read on the row-level lane and
order with size; the segment-level collapse column is read on the calibrated
pooled lane and does not (<math id="A6.T11.m92" class="ltx_Math" alttext="70" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>70</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">70</annotation></semantics></math>M <math id="A6.T11.m93" class="ltx_Math" alttext="20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>20</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">20</annotation></semantics></math>k, <math id="A6.T11.m94" class="ltx_Math" alttext="410" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>410</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">410</annotation></semantics></math>M <math id="A6.T11.m95" class="ltx_Math" alttext="25" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>25</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">25</annotation></semantics></math>k, <math id="A6.T11.m96" class="ltx_Math" alttext="31" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>31</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">31</annotation></semantics></math>M <math id="A6.T11.m97" class="ltx_Math" alttext="28" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>28</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">28</annotation></semantics></math>k, <math id="A6.T11.m98" class="ltx_Math" alttext="14" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>14</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">14</annotation></semantics></math>M <math id="A6.T11.m99" class="ltx_Math" alttext="43" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>43</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">43</annotation></semantics></math>k,
<math id="A6.T11.m100" class="ltx_Math" alttext="160" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>160</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">160</annotation></semantics></math>M <math id="A6.T11.m101" class="ltx_Math" alttext="71" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>71</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">71</annotation></semantics></math>k). Any size-ordering statement names which instrument it uses.</p></div><div class="ltx_flex_break"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1">
<p id="A6.T11.7" class="ltx_p ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center">(c) Model excluded from every cross-scale reading</p></div><div class="ltx_flex_break"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1">
<table id="A6.T11.8" class="ltx_tabular ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_middle">
