<p id="A6.T11.9" class="ltx_p ltx_figure_panel">Pythia-1B contributes to no row, ordering, or trend in this appendix. Its
released checkpoints are stored in fp16 like every other size, so the
difference is in the training arithmetic and not in the container of the
weights we read; the size of any residual effect on the probes is not measured
here. Reasons (i) to (iii) are independent facts and none is evidence for the
others.</p></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 11: </span>Cross-scale readings. <span id="A6.T11.13" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(a)</span> sizes, coverage, and the
external landmarks available per size. <span id="A6.T11.14" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(b)</span> the internal transition
readings, all under persistence criteria rather than visual reading; the
two onset instruments are different lanes and are not merged.
<span id="A6.T11.15" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(c)</span> the one model excluded from every cross-scale reading, with
its three independent grounds.</figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Why Pythia-1B is excluded.</h5>

<div id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The suite contains a seventh model in this range, and it is left out of
every cross-scale statement below for three reasons that are separate
facts and should not be conflated. First, it is the only model of the
suite trained in bfloat16 upstream, following a half-precision loss spike
late in its run; the released checkpoints are stored in fp16 like every
other size, so the difference is in the training arithmetic and not in the
container we read, and the size of any residual effect on the probes is
not measured here. Second, its depth is not monotone in size: at <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>16</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16</annotation></semantics></math>
layers of width <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2048" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2048</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2048</annotation></semantics></math> it is shallower than both the <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="24\times 1024" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>24</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>1024</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">24\times 1024</annotation></semantics></math> model
below it and the <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="24\times 2048" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>24</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>2048</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">24\times 2048</annotation></semantics></math> model above it in parameter count, and the
depth and width reading of Appendix <a href="#A6.SS4" title="F.4 Where the Calibrated Signal Survives ‣ Appendix F Pythia Scale Extensions ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F.4</span></a> is
precisely a statement about depth and width. Third, one of its released
revisions carries the upstream defect described in
Appendix <a href="#A1.SS3" title="A.3 Pretraining Checkpoint Coverage ‣ Appendix A Experimental Coverage and Protocol Details ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.3</span></a>, which forces masked windows across the
very region that Appendix <a href="#A6.SS5" title="F.5 Co-location Registry for Late Events ‣ Appendix F Pythia Scale Extensions ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F.5</span></a> discusses. The first
reason alone would keep it out of a scale-ordered comparison; the three
together make the exclusion unambiguous. One cost of the exclusion is
recorded where it falls due, in Appendix <a href="#A6.SS4" title="F.4 Where the Calibrated Signal Survives ‣ Appendix F Pythia Scale Extensions ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F.4</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Reading discipline.</h5>

<div id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The calibrated readout detects within-group coherent motion against a
membership-redrawn null whose threshold adapts to the local geometry.
Horizontal comparisons of it <em id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">between segments</em> are therefore
downgraded, and only three comparison types are used: time shape at fixed
grouping, cross-size comparison under one grouping convention, and
between-layer comparison inside one segment. Sampled-preview
instrumentation exists for the larger sizes and no number here is taken
from it; where a full readout does not exist the cell is left empty rather
than filled.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.2 </span>The Auxiliary–Bulk Partition Holds at Every Size</h3>

<div id="A6.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A6.F17" title="Figure 17 ‣ F.2 The Auxiliary–Bulk Partition Holds at Every Size ‣ Appendix F Pythia Scale Extensions ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">17</span></a> reads the partition of
Appendix <a href="#A3.SS3" title="C.3 Pythia: Segment Taxonomy and the Vector Segment ‣ Appendix C Spatial Localization: the Auxiliary–Bulk Partition ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.3</span></a> at all six sizes under three probes,
one from each family. The separation is not a tendency that survives
aggregation: the median auxiliary series exceeds the median bulk series at
every one of the <math id="A6.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="123" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>123</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">123</annotation></semantics></math> anchors, at all six sizes, under all three probes.
The smallest median gaps anywhere in the panel occur at 1.4B late in
training, at <math id="A6.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.036" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.036</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.036</annotation></semantics></math> for ESA, <math id="A6.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.351" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.351</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.351</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="A6.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1-\mathrm{FRR}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>FRR</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1-\mathrm{FRR}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A6.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.115" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.115</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.115</annotation></semantics></math> for
the DMD direction cosine.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A6.F17" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2608.15483v1/app06_auxbulk_across_scales.svg" id="A6.F17.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:698/419;" width="698" height="419"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 17: </span>Auxiliary and bulk coordinates stay separated at every size and
every anchor. Rows: (a) ESA, (b) <math id="A6.F17.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1-\mathrm{FRR}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>FRR</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1-\mathrm{FRR}</annotation></semantics></math>, (c) DMD direction
cosine; columns: the six sizes. The solid line is the group median over
the pooled group set and the shaded band the interquartile range; orange
is auxiliary, the vector segment, and blue is bulk. Grey dashed
references mark <math id="A6.F17.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5</annotation></semantics></math> in (a) and <math id="A6.F17.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> in (c). All panels use one readout
protocol at <math id="A6.F17.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau{=}5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau{=}5</annotation></semantics></math> over the <math id="A6.F17.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="123" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>123</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">123</annotation></semantics></math> shared anchors, and because the
suite trains every size with the same <math id="A6.F17.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>M-token batch, a matched step
grid is also a matched token grid. Horizontal comparisons between sizes
are therefore at matched steps and tokens, and not at matched loss,
compute, or training progress. The median separation holds at every
anchor at all six sizes under all three probes; the smallest median gaps
are <math id="A6.F17.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.036" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.036</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.036</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A6.F17.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.351" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.351</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.351</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A6.F17.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.115" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.115</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.115</annotation></semantics></math> for the three rows, all at 1.4B late in
training. Interquartile ranges are disjoint at every anchor for (b) and
(c) at all sizes, and for (a) at every size except 1.4B, where they
overlap on <math id="A6.F17.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="30\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>30</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">30\%</annotation></semantics></math> of anchors. Bulk is the strict matrix set, with both
embedding segments dropped; under the looser alternative the bulk means
move by at most <math id="A6.F17.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.2\times 10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.2</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.2\times 10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math> for (a) and (b) but by up to
<math id="A6.F17.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6.3\times 10^{-3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>6.3</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6.3\times 10^{-3}</annotation></semantics></math> for (c), which is why the strict rule is used
throughout. Pythia-1B is excluded here and in every other cross-scale
panel, on the three independent grounds of
Table <a href="#A6.T11" title="Table 11 ‣ F.1 Coverage and Protocol ‣ Appendix F Pythia Scale Extensions ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a>(c).</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A6.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The interquartile bands are disjoint at every anchor for the
subspace-residual and predictor-based readouts at all six sizes, and for
ESA at every size except 1.4B, where they overlap on <math id="A6.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="30\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>30</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">30\%</annotation></semantics></math> of anchors in
the late window. The frozen-coordinate fraction is identically zero here,
at every segment and every anchor, so none of this contrast is carried by
coordinates that do not move.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Two conventions travel with the figure. Bulk is the strict matrix set,
<math id="A6.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="qkv" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">qkv</annotation></semantics></math> together with the attention output projection and the MLP, with both
embedding segments dropped. Under the looser alternative that keeps
everything not in the vector segment, the bulk means move by at most
<math id="A6.SS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.2\times 10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.2</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.2\times 10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math> for ESA and <math id="A6.SS2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1-\mathrm{FRR}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>FRR</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1-\mathrm{FRR}</annotation></semantics></math> but by up to
<math id="A6.SS2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6.3\times 10^{-3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>6.3</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6.3\times 10^{-3}</annotation></semantics></math> for the DMD cosine, which is why the strict rule is
fixed throughout this appendix. And the calibrated readout does not enter
this figure at all; where it appears later it is reported as excess over
its null level.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.3 </span>Segment Division of Labour</h3>

<div id="A6.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A6.F18" title="Figure 18 ‣ F.3 Segment Division of Labour ‣ Appendix F Pythia Scale Extensions ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">18</span></a> puts the four segments of every size on one
axis under two readouts, and the two readouts do not agree about how much
structure there is to see.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A6.F18" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2608.15483v1/app06_segment_across_scales.svg" id="A6.F18.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:698/349;" width="698" height="349"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 18: </span>Segment division of labour across sizes: ESA barely separates
the matrix segments while the calibrated readout does. Columns are the
six sizes. (a) ESA group median per segment. (b) pooled calibrated excess
per segment, drawn as a five-anchor centred rolling median, with the
onset markers computed on the unsmoothed series. The three matrix
segments share a blue system (<math id="A6.F18.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="qkv" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">qkv</annotation></semantics></math> solid, attention output dashed, MLP
dotted) and the vector segment is orange; grey dashed references mark
<math id="A6.F18.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5</annotation></semantics></math> in (a) and the null level <math id="A6.F18.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> in (b), where the floor at <math id="A6.F18.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.05</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.05</annotation></semantics></math> is
the zero-fraction case. The dark dotted line is the sustained collapse
onset of the <math id="A6.F18.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="qkv" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">qkv</annotation></semantics></math> series, and where the series dips and recovers the
first crossing is given in grey parentheses. Onsets are <math id="A6.F18.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>20</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">20</annotation></semantics></math>k (70M),
<math id="A6.F18.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="25" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>25</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">25</annotation></semantics></math>k (410M), <math id="A6.F18.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="28" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>28</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">28</annotation></semantics></math>k (31M), <math id="A6.F18.m26" class="ltx_Math" alttext="43" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>43</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">43</annotation></semantics></math>k (14M), and <math id="A6.F18.m27" class="ltx_Math" alttext="71" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>71</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">71</annotation></semantics></math>k (160M), with no
sustained collapse at 1.4B, so the ordering is not monotone in parameter
count under either crossing. In (a) the three matrix segments stay within
a median of <math id="A6.F18.m28" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.048" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.048</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.048</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A6.F18.m29" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.038" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.038</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.038</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A6.F18.m30" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.027" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.027</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.027</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A6.F18.m31" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.021" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.021</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.021</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A6.F18.m32" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.014" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.014</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.014</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A6.F18.m33" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.011" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.011</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.011</annotation></semantics></math> of
one another in ascending size order, so the spread between matrix
segments shrinks monotonically with size, while the vector segment stays
above all of them by at least <math id="A6.F18.m34" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.034" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.034</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.034</annotation></semantics></math> at every anchor and size.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A6.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Under ESA the three matrix segments are nearly indistinguishable, and they
become more so as the model grows: the median spread between them narrows
monotonically from <math id="A6.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.048" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.048</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.048</annotation></semantics></math> at 14M to <math id="A6.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.011" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.011</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.011</annotation></semantics></math> at 1.4B. The vector segment
stays above all three by at least <math id="A6.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.034" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.034</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.034</annotation></semantics></math> at every anchor and every size.
Read through coordinate signs alone, the bulk of a larger model looks more
internally uniform, not less.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Under the calibrated readout the same segments separate clearly, and <math id="A6.SS3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="qkv" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">qkv</annotation></semantics></math>
carries a distinct time shape: high early, then a sustained collapse to the
null level. The collapse onsets are <math id="A6.SS3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>20</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">20</annotation></semantics></math>k at 70M, <math id="A6.SS3.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="25" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>25</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">25</annotation></semantics></math>k at 410M, <math id="A6.SS3.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="28" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>28</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">28</annotation></semantics></math>k at
31M, <math id="A6.SS3.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="43" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>43</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">43</annotation></semantics></math>k at 14M, and <math id="A6.SS3.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="71" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>71</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">71</annotation></semantics></math>k at 160M, with no sustained collapse at 1.4B
inside the window. That ordering is <em id="A6.SS3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">not</em> monotone in parameter
count, under either of the two crossing conventions recorded in
Table <a href="#A6.T11" title="Table 11 ‣ F.1 Coverage and Protocol ‣ Appendix F Pythia Scale Extensions ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS3.p4.1" class="ltx_p">This is where the two instruments must be kept apart. The collapse just
described is read on the pooled calibrated lane. The null-line and
row-level pocket onsets of Appendix <a href="#A4.SS2" title="D.2 Emergence and Survival ‣ Appendix D Pocket Trajectories, Persistence, and Overlap Registrations ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D.2</span></a> are read on
the row-level lane, and those do order with size. A size-ordering
statement about this system is only meaningful once it names which of the
two it is about.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS3.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS3.p5.1" class="ltx_p">The corresponding segment-resolved pocket populations, including the
finding that the attention output projection carries the same wave as
<math id="A6.SS3.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="qkv" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">qkv</annotation></semantics></math> at row granularity and that only the output half of the MLP carries
signal, are reported in Appendix <a href="#A4.SS2" title="D.2 Emergence and Survival ‣ Appendix D Pocket Trajectories, Persistence, and Overlap Registrations ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D.2</span></a> and are not
repeated here.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.4 </span>Where the Calibrated Signal Survives</h3>

<div id="A6.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A6.F19" title="Figure 19 ‣ F.4 Where the Calibrated Signal Survives ‣ Appendix F Pythia Scale Extensions ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">19</span></a> resolves the <math id="A6.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="qkv" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">qkv</annotation></semantics></math> calibrated readout by layer
and step at all six sizes on one colour scale, with white at the null
level.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A6.F19" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2608.15483v1/app06_lrgfcal_depth_across_scales.png" id="A6.F19.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:698/369;" width="698" height="369" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 19: </span>Where the <math id="A6.F19.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="qkv" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">qkv</annotation></semantics></math> calibrated signal survives: layer against step
at six sizes on one colour scale. Each panel is one model, rows are
transformer blocks with layer <math id="A6.F19.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> at the bottom, and columns are the
<math id="A6.F19.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="123" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>123</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">123</annotation></semantics></math> shared anchors. The probe is reported as excess over its
<math id="A6.F19.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha{=}0.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.05</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha{=}0.05</annotation></semantics></math> null level, so <math id="A6.F19.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> is exactly the null and the raw pocket
fraction is the excess plus <math id="A6.F19.m26" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.05</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.05</annotation></semantics></math>; the colour ramp is anchored with
white at <math id="A6.F19.m27" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math>, every cell at or below the null renders white, and the ramp
is clipped at <math id="A6.F19.m28" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.60" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.60</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.60</annotation></semantics></math>, which affects <math id="A6.F19.m29" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.21\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.21</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.21\%</annotation></semantics></math> of cells. Ticks on the right
edge mark the layers whose tail-phase mean stays above the null. Early in
training the signal covers <math id="A6.F19.m30" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5/6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5/6</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A6.F19.m31" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6/6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6/6</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A6.F19.m32" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6/6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6/6</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A6.F19.m33" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10/12" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10/12</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A6.F19.m34" class="ltx_Math" alttext="23/24" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>23</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>24</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">23/24</annotation></semantics></math>, and
<math id="A6.F19.m35" class="ltx_Math" alttext="23/24" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>23</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>24</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">23/24</annotation></semantics></math> layers in ascending size order, and then contracts onto a
persistent band whose absolute layer index moves deeper as the model
deepens. 1.4B does not contract inside the window: <math id="A6.F19.m36" class="ltx_Math" alttext="22" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>22</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">22</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="A6.F19.m37" class="ltx_Math" alttext="24" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>24</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">24</annotation></semantics></math> layers
are still above the null in the tail phase, and it shows instead an
extinction window near <math id="A6.F19.m38" class="ltx_Math" alttext="96" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>96</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">96</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A6.F19.m39" class="ltx_Math" alttext="118" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>118</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">118</annotation></semantics></math>k followed by a recovery from about
<math id="A6.F19.m40" class="ltx_Math" alttext="120" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>120</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">120</annotation></semantics></math>k. The calibrated readout is identical under both bulk rules, since
the vector segment does not enter it.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A6.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Early in training the signal is broad, covering <math id="A6.SS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5/6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5/6</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A6.SS4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6/6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6/6</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A6.SS4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6/6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6/6</annotation></semantics></math>,
<math id="A6.SS4.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10/12" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10/12</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A6.SS4.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="23/24" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>23</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>24</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">23/24</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A6.SS4.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="23/24" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>23</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>24</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">23/24</annotation></semantics></math> layers at the six sizes in ascending order.
It then contracts onto a small persistent band whose absolute layer index
moves deeper as the model deepens: in the middle phase the band is layer 5
at 14M and 31M, layer 4 at 70M, layers 8 to 11 at 160M, and layers 21 to
23 at 410M. In the tail phase nothing survives at 14M, while the band sits
at layer 5 (31M), layer 4 (70M), layers 6 to 7 (160M), and layers 19 to 23
(410M). In relative depth the band sits in the deepest quarter of every
model that contracts at all.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS4.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS4.p3.1" class="ltx_p">1.4B does not contract inside the window: <math id="A6.SS4.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="22" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>22</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">22</annotation></semantics></math> of its <math id="A6.SS4.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="24" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>24</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">24</annotation></semantics></math> layers are
still above the null in the tail phase. It shows instead an extinction
window near <math id="A6.SS4.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="96" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>96</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">96</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A6.SS4.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="118" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>118</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">118</annotation></semantics></math>k in which the raw fraction drops to nearly zero
in most layers, with only the deepest block holding <math id="A6.SS4.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.15</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.15</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A6.SS4.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.44" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.44</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.44</annotation></semantics></math>,
followed by a recovery from about <math id="A6.SS4.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="120" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>120</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">120</annotation></semantics></math>k to the highest values of the run.</p>
</div>
<section id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Depth and width.</h5>

<div id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Parameter count alone does not order these transitions. Among the sizes
retained, the one contrast that survives holds depth fixed: at <math id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="24" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>24</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">24</annotation></semantics></math> layers
the narrower 410M reaches its row-level pocket onset at <math id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="48" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>48</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">48</annotation></semantics></math>k and its
null-line onset at <math id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="92" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>92</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">92</annotation></semantics></math>k, while the wider 1.4B has reached neither by
<math id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>128</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">128</annotation></semantics></math>k. Wider at equal depth is later. The complementary contrast, deeper
at equal width, rested on the pair that the exclusion of 1B removes, so
depth and width are confounded along the suite’s own scaling ladder among
the sizes retained. The depth half of a two-factor reading is therefore
registered as unsupported here rather than asserted.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.5 </span>Co-location Registry for Late Events</h3>

<div id="A6.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This subsection records where the internal readouts and the public loss
telemetry land relative to each other on the step axis. Nothing here is a
directional claim.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">At 70M the smoothed loss reaches its minimum at step <math id="A6.SS5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="50{,}345" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>50,345</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">50{,}345</annotation></semantics></math> and rises
afterwards, bulk ESA has a local rise peaking at <math id="A6.SS5.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.467" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.467</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.467</annotation></semantics></math> near <math id="A6.SS5.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="77" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>77</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">77</annotation></semantics></math>k before
descending to its global minimum <math id="A6.SS5.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.426" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.426</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.426</annotation></semantics></math> at <math id="A6.SS5.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="98" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>98</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">98</annotation></semantics></math>k, and the row-level main
wave peaks at <math id="A6.SS5.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="84" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>84</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">84</annotation></semantics></math>k. At 160M the loss minimum is at <math id="A6.SS5.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="76{,}409" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>76,409</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">76{,}409</annotation></semantics></math>, bulk ESA
reaches its global minimum <math id="A6.SS5.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.424" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.424</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.424</annotation></semantics></math> at <math id="A6.SS5.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="68" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>68</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">68</annotation></semantics></math>k and rises persistently from
<math id="A6.SS5.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="78" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>78</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">78</annotation></semantics></math>k to a plateau of <math id="A6.SS5.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.45" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.45</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.45</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A6.SS5.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.47" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.47</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.47</annotation></semantics></math>, and the pocket peak is at <math id="A6.SS5.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="92" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>92</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">92</annotation></semantics></math>k.
On both sizes the loss minimum, the ESA turn, and the main pocket wave
fall in the same stretch of training.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS5.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS5.p3.1" class="ltx_p">At 410M that coincidence does not hold, and this is the more informative
case. The smoothed loss has no minimum inside the anchor domain: it is
still descending at the right edge and remains flat or descending to the
end of training. The ESA readout nevertheless shows the same late rise, recomputed on the full-protocol extended panel: bulk group-level ESA (<math id="A6.SS5.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau{=}5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau{=}5</annotation></semantics></math>, group <math id="A6.SS5.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{50}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>50</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{50}</annotation></semantics></math>) sits on a <math id="A6.SS5.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.436" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.436</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.436</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="A6.SS5.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.441" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.441</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.441</annotation></semantics></math> plateau from <math id="A6.SS5.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="60" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>60</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">60</annotation></semantics></math>k to <math id="A6.SS5.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="85" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>85</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">85</annotation></semantics></math>k, climbs steadily from about <math id="A6.SS5.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="85" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>85</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">85</annotation></semantics></math>k, and peaks at <math id="A6.SS5.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.48" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.48</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.48</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="A6.SS5.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.49" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.49</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.49</annotation></semantics></math> over <math id="A6.SS5.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="111" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>111</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">111</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A6.SS5.p3.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="117" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>117</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">117</annotation></semantics></math>k. The late ESA
rise therefore occurs without a loss-bottoming event, and the co-location
seen at the two smaller sizes should not be carried to larger sizes as if
it were a general pairing.</p>
</div>
<section id="A6.SS5.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">One monotone ordering.</h5>

<div id="A6.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A6.F20" title="Figure 20 ‣ One monotone ordering. ‣ F.5 Co-location Registry for Late Events ‣ Appendix F Pythia Scale Extensions ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">20</span></a> reports the internal diagnostics of the
predictor-based family on the bulk set. The fitted operator’s step
amplitude falls progressively below the realized step, and the onset of
that deficit is earlier the larger the model: <math id="A6.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="58" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>58</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">58</annotation></semantics></math>k, <math id="A6.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="31" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>31</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">31</annotation></semantics></math>k, <math id="A6.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="21" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>21</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">21</annotation></semantics></math>k, <math id="A6.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>15</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">15</annotation></semantics></math>k,
<math id="A6.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="14" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>14</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">14</annotation></semantics></math>k, and <math id="A6.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="11" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>11</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">11</annotation></semantics></math>k across the six sizes in ascending order. This is the only
cross-scale ordering in this appendix that is monotone in parameter count.
By the last anchor the bulk median amplitude ratio has fallen to <math id="A6.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.13" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.13</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.13</annotation></semantics></math> to
<math id="A6.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.38" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.38</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.38</annotation></semantics></math> at every size while the largest eigenvalue modulus settles into
<math id="A6.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.59" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.59</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.59</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A6.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.68" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.68</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.68</annotation></semantics></math>, with 14M the exception at <math id="A6.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.78" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.78</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.78</annotation></semantics></math>: the fitted operator
keeps a stable spectrum while the amplitude of the step it predicts falls
well below the step actually taken.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A6.F20" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2608.15483v1/app06_dmddiag_across_scales.svg" id="A6.F20.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:698/235;" width="698" height="235"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 20: </span>Internal predictor-family diagnostics on the bulk set across six
sizes. (a) median predicted-over-realized step amplitude of the fit;
(b) median largest eigenvalue modulus of the fitted operator; (c) the
onset step of the amplitude deficit against non-embedding parameter count
on a log axis. Line shade encodes size on a single ramp and every curve is
additionally labelled at its right end, so colour is never the only
encoding. Onset is the first anchor opening five consecutive anchors whose
median amplitude ratio is below <math id="A6.F20.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5</annotation></semantics></math>, marked by the grey dashed reference
in (a). The deficit sets in earlier the larger the model, at <math id="A6.F20.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="58" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>58</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">58</annotation></semantics></math>k, <math id="A6.F20.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="31" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>31</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">31</annotation></semantics></math>k,
<math id="A6.F20.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="21" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>21</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">21</annotation></semantics></math>k, <math id="A6.F20.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>15</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">15</annotation></semantics></math>k, <math id="A6.F20.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="14" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>14</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">14</annotation></semantics></math>k, and <math id="A6.F20.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="11" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>11</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">11</annotation></semantics></math>k in ascending size order, which is the only
cross-scale ordering in this appendix that is monotone in parameter count.
By the last anchor the bulk median amplitude ratio has fallen to <math id="A6.F20.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.13" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.13</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.13</annotation></semantics></math> to
<math id="A6.F20.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.38" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.38</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.38</annotation></semantics></math> at every size while the eigenvalue modulus settles into <math id="A6.F20.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.59" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.59</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.59</annotation></semantics></math> to
<math id="A6.F20.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.68" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.68</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.68</annotation></semantics></math>, with 14M the exception at <math id="A6.F20.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.78" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.78</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.78</annotation></semantics></math>.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS5.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">The late cluster.</h5>

<div id="A6.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Several unrelated readouts move inside a narrow late window. On 70M and
160M the auxiliary DMD amplitude ratio falls to exactly zero and stays
there from anchors <math id="A6.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="118" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>118</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">118</annotation></semantics></math>k and <math id="A6.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="117" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>117</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">117</annotation></semantics></math>k respectively, while the bulk series
over the same anchors is unaffected. On 70M a secondary row-level wave
appears near <math id="A6.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="115" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>115</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">115</annotation></semantics></math>k. On 410M the ESA peak, the pocket peak at <math id="A6.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="116" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>116</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">116</annotation></semantics></math>k, and
an MLP output-half patch in the middle layers all fall in <math id="A6.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="110" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>110</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">110</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A6.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="120" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>120</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">120</annotation></semantics></math>k.
Whether this is one phenomenon or several is open. Two constraints are
worth recording: the learning-rate schedule has no breakpoint anywhere
near it, since the decay is a single cosine with no constant tail, and the
auxiliary series that goes to zero does so exactly, which is the signature
of a degenerate fit rather than of a small value.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.6 </span>Open Questions</h3>

<div id="A6.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Four items are registered as open rather than resolved.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The late cluster above may be one event or several, and the exact-zero
auxiliary amplitude ratio is as consistent with an instrument boundary as
with a property of the trajectory. Distinguishing the two requires a
readout that does not go through the same fit.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS6.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS6.p3.1" class="ltx_p">1.4B sits at the edge of the observation window. Its row-level population
reaches <math id="A6.SS6.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3.0\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3.0</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.0\%</annotation></semantics></math> at the last anchor and is still rising, and its calibrated
band has not contracted. It is therefore a sample of a transition
beginning at the window edge, not of a transition that did or did not
happen, and it should not be read as a negative case.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS6.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS6.p4.1" class="ltx_p">The local 1.4B loss telemetry does not match the released <math id="A6.SS6.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="143{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>143,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">143{,}000</annotation></semantics></math>-step cosine schedule, so no loss landmark is quoted
for it and no co-location statement is made at that size.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS6.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS6.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Excluding 1B removes the only pair of sizes that share a width, so the
depth leg of the depth and width reading has no support among the sizes
retained. Recovering it would require either a fourth model at <math id="A6.SS6.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="24" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>24</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">24</annotation></semantics></math> layers
and width <math id="A6.SS6.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2048" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2048</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2048</annotation></semantics></math> or an assessment of how much the training-arithmetic
difference actually moves these probes.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A7" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix G </span>Architecture- and Recipe-Conditioned Results</h2>

<div id="A7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Section 4.4 uses optimizer-family variation as its compact
example and defers the rest to this appendix: the size-controlled
architecture comparison, the controlled weight-decay and momentum dose
studies, the wider optimizer panel, and the comparison between
predictability and optimizer quality.</p>
</div>
<section id="A7.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">G.1 </span>Size-Controlled Architecture Comparison</h3>

<div id="A7.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A7.F21" title="Figure 21 ‣ G.1 Size-Controlled Architecture Comparison ‣ Appendix G Architecture- and Recipe-Conditioned Results ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">21</span></a> compares three architectures trained on the
same dataset with SAM under a cosine schedule. ViT-mid and the ResNet have
nearly matched parameter counts, and ViT-mid retains higher bulk ESA at
every measured anchor. The separation is present from early training: at
epoch <math id="A7.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5</annotation></semantics></math> the two ViT scales read about <math id="A7.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.72" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.72</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.72</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A7.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.71" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.71</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.71</annotation></semantics></math> against <math id="A7.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.65" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.65</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.65</annotation></semantics></math>
for the ResNet, and around epoch <math id="A7.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="40" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>40</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">40</annotation></semantics></math> the three read about <math id="A7.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.60" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.60</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.60</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A7.SS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.60" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.60</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.60</annotation></semantics></math>,
and <math id="A7.SS1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.52" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.52</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.52</annotation></semantics></math>. The smaller ViT follows the same higher-ESA profile while
holding roughly one fifth as many parameters as ViT-mid, so parameter
count alone does not order the three.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A7.F21" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2608.15483v1/supp_figures/fig_44_arch.png" id="A7.F21.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:600/437;" width="600" height="437" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 21: </span>Size-controlled architecture comparison under SAM. Curves report
canonical bulk ESA across ten anchors for ViT-tiny, ViT-mid, and the
parameter-matched ResNet; ViT-mid and the ResNet have nearly equal
parameter counts. The dashed line marks the random sign-agreement level
of <math id="A7.F21.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5</annotation></semantics></math>. Each model uses its own standard learning rate, so the
comparison controls scale but not every hyperparameter.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A7.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Because each model uses its own standard learning rate, this comparison
does not isolate architecture from every hyperparameter difference. What
it establishes under the stated conditions is a stable
architecture-associated contrast: ViT-class models retain more bulk
directional persistence than the size-matched ResNet throughout the
measured trajectory.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">G.2 </span>Optimizer Families along Training Loss</h3>

<div id="A7.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Optimizer families traverse the loss trajectory at different rates, so
comparing them at matched epochs mixes the effect of the update rule with
the effect of elapsed training. Figure 6 therefore aligns
them on training loss and restricts the comparison to the loss range that
all displayed families share. Matched loss does not equate optimizer
state, and the alignment removes an elapsed-training confound rather than
all confounds.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Over the shared range the families occupy distinct profiles. SAM sits in
the highest regime, at roughly <math id="A7.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.58" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.58</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.58</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A7.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.73" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.73</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.73</annotation></semantics></math> bulk ESA over the
displayed interval. Muon stays near the <math id="A7.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5</annotation></semantics></math> sign-agreement reference.
Adam lies about <math id="A7.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.08" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.08</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.08</annotation></semantics></math> below plain SGD over most of their overlap. SGD and
AdaGrad approach a similar low-loss level near <math id="A7.SS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.545" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.545</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.545</annotation></semantics></math> despite following
different profiles earlier. Optimization position therefore organizes how
predictability evolves, while the update rule conditions its level and its
local directional structure.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The ordering is architecture-conditioned rather than universal. The
weight-decay and momentum ladders below are the more controlled
comparison, because each of their arms changes exactly one named
hyperparameter relative to plain SGD.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">G.3 </span>Weight-Decay and Momentum Dose Ladders</h3>

<div id="A7.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A7.F22" title="Figure 22 ‣ G.3 Weight-Decay and Momentum Dose Ladders ‣ Appendix G Architecture- and Recipe-Conditioned Results ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">22</span></a> reports the two dose ladders for ViT-mid under
the canonical vision grouping, read through all three probe families
against reversed training loss. The ladders also show why the families are
retained jointly, since one intervention can register differently through
coordinate signs, vector direction, and containment in the recent-history
span.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A7.F22" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2608.15483v1/supp_figures/fig_44_dose_ladder.png" id="A7.F22.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:656/235;" width="656" height="235" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 22: </span>Controlled weight-decay and momentum dose ladders for ViT-mid.
Panels report (a) bulk ESA, (b) bulk VCS, and (c) bulk FRR against
reversed training loss under the canonical <math id="A7.F22.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K{=}16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K{=}16</annotation></semantics></math> vision grouping. Each
arm changes only the indicated weight-decay or momentum value relative to
plain SGD, and curves are compared over their overlapping loss ranges.
The two ladders order the three readouts in opposite directions, and the
subspace-residual readout separates from plain SGD at a dose where the
two displacement-direction readouts do not.</figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Weight decay.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The weight-decay ladder shows a consistent dose ordering on all three
readouts. ESA increases with the decay coefficient at shared loss
positions and approaches <math id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.90" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.90</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.90</annotation></semantics></math> at the largest dose. VCS rises towards a
similar level, so the full displacement direction becomes more persistent,
and FRR falls to about <math id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.28" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.28</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.28</annotation></semantics></math>, so the future displacement is more strongly
contained in the span of recent updates.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The readouts differ in sensitivity at the low end. At
<math id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda=10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda=10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math>, ESA and VCS remain near the plain-SGD profile while FRR
has already separated from it, at about <math id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.66" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.66</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.66</annotation></semantics></math> against <math id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.79" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.79</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.79</annotation></semantics></math>. The
subspace-residual probe therefore resolves a low-dose change that the
displacement-direction probes do not. The mechanism is visible in the
update rule: SGD with weight decay adds a component proportional to
<math id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-\lambda w" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>w</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\lambda w</annotation></semantics></math>, which is a slow and coherent drift, and the monotone
response of all three readouts shows that this component is picked up at
the sign, vector, and subspace levels alike. These are raw probe profiles
over the realized trajectory, not a decomposition of the weight-decay
mechanism.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Momentum.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The momentum ladder runs the other way. At shared loss positions, a larger
momentum coefficient depresses both displacement-direction readouts and
lifts FRR by a smaller amount. The response is clearest at the vector
level: VCS falls further than ESA, whose change is only about <math id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.02" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.02</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.02</annotation></semantics></math> to
<math id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.03" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.03</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.03</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Under this protocol higher momentum therefore reduces the forms of bulk
short-horizon redundancy these probes capture. The statement is about the
realized parameter trajectory and not about the smoothness of the
underlying gradient estimate; smoothing the gradient and making the
resulting parameter displacement predictable at short horizons are
distinct properties. Two common interventions can thus reorganize the
realized trajectory in opposite directions across the same probe panel.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Both ladders exclude the two collapsed momentum runs recorded in
Appendix <a href="#A1.SS2" title="A.2 Additional Run Families ‣ Appendix A Experimental Coverage and Protocol Details ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.2</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">G.4 </span>Predictability Is Not an Optimizer Ranking</h3>

<div id="A7.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Section 4.4 cautions that higher predictability should not be
read as better optimization. Two measurements support that caution.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">First, the two orderings are not aligned. Within each architecture, the
rank correlation between anchor-averaged bulk ESA and final test accuracy
across the measured optimizer cells is negative at every architecture, with
a median of <math id="A7.SS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.71" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.71</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.71</annotation></semantics></math> over the five architectures and a range from <math id="A7.SS4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.89" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.89</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.89</annotation></semantics></math> to
<math id="A7.SS4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.20</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.20</annotation></semantics></math>. The cell counts behind those five correlations are <math id="A7.SS4.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>6</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A7.SS4.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>6</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A7.SS4.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>7</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7</annotation></semantics></math>,
<math id="A7.SS4.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>7</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A7.SS4.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>, so the weakest of them rests on four points and should not be
read on its own. Reading a higher probe value as a better optimizer would
therefore invert the accuracy ordering in these cells rather than
reproduce it. This is a correspondence between two summaries of the same
runs and is confounded in the obvious way, since different families reach
different loss positions in <math id="A7.SS4.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="50" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>50</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">50</annotation></semantics></math> epochs; it is registered as a caution
against the ranking reading and not as a claim that predictability
predicts accuracy with either sign.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS4.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SS4.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Second, the weight-decay ladder provides the same conclusion inside a
single controlled arm. Predictability increases monotonically along that
ladder, yet the <math id="A7.SS4.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\times 10^{-3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\times 10^{-3}</annotation></semantics></math> arm terminates at a higher loss and
reaches about <math id="A7.SS4.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.707" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.707</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.707</annotation></semantics></math> final accuracy against about <math id="A7.SS4.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.755" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.755</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.755</annotation></semantics></math> for the
<math id="A7.SS4.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{-3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{-3}</annotation></semantics></math> arm. Temporal redundancy and training quality move in opposite
directions along a ladder in which only one hyperparameter changes.</p>
</div>
<section id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Scope.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">These comparisons are representative rather than exhaustive. The
architecture and optimizer panels use the standard configuration of each
model, and the dose ladders cover one ViT-mid setting. What they establish is
not a ranking of architectures or of update rules, but that the three
probe families resolve, and resolve differently, the changes that model
structure and training recipe impose on the realized trajectory.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A8" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix H </span>Online Selective Prediction</h2>

<div id="A8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Section 4 is retrospective throughout: every probe reads a
stored trajectory after the fact. The conclusion of the main paper points
to one narrow online check of whether the measured spatial organization is
useful as a prior over where to attempt prediction during training. This
appendix gives that check in full.</p>
</div>
