<td id="A8.T12.1.7.5" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><math id="A8.T12.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{0.32\%}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold">0.32</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{0.32\%}</annotation></semantics></math></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 12: </span>Online comparison on CIFAR-10 over three seeds under pure SGD,
with momentum and weight decay both zero. All three arms share the same
predictor and the same coordinate-wise acceptance mask; the arms differ
only in which parameters are eligible for write-back. “Accepted” is the
fraction of parameters that actually received a written-back forecast.
Values are means over seeds with one standard deviation, and each arm is
read at the epoch chosen on a held-out split within its own run.</figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="A8.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">H.1 </span>Protocol and Selection Rule</h3>

<div id="A8.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The online method writes a forecast back into a coordinate only when that
forecast passes a coordinate-wise acceptance test on scale control and
dynamic consistency; coordinates that fail continue to follow the
baseline optimizer. That acceptance mask is the immediate safeguard and is
unchanged in every arm below.</p>
</div>
<div id="A8.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The variable under test is not the mask but the <em id="A8.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">eligibility set</em> it
is applied to. Two settings are compared against ordinary training. The
full-scope arm makes every trainable parameter eligible. The restricted
arm keeps the identical predictor and identical acceptance mask but makes
only auxiliary parameters eligible, in the exact sense of
Appendix <a href="#A3.SS1" title="C.1 The Partition Rule ‣ Appendix C Spatial Localization: the Auxiliary–Bulk Partition ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.1</span></a>. The restriction is deliberately coarse:
it uses the role-level separation that the retrospective measurements
report, and it makes no attempt to detect the localized, time-varying
pockets inside bulk tensors online. Nothing in the eligibility rule reads
the future, and nothing reads test labels.</p>
</div>
<div id="A8.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The comparison uses ViT-tiny and ViT-mid under pure SGD, with momentum and
weight decay both set to zero, over three seeds. Each arm reports the test
accuracy at the epoch chosen on a held-out split of the training data, and
the gain is taken against the baseline of the same seed.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">H.2 </span>Multi-Seed Results</h3>

<div id="A8.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A8.T12" title="Table 12 ‣ Appendix H Online Selective Prediction ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a> and Figure <a href="#A8.F23" title="Figure 23 ‣ H.2 Multi-Seed Results ‣ Appendix H Online Selective Prediction ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">23</span></a> give the
comparison. On both architectures the restricted arm produces the larger
mean gain while accepting write-back for less than <math id="A8.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1\%</annotation></semantics></math> of parameters,
<math id="A8.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.80\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.80</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.80\%</annotation></semantics></math> on ViT-tiny and <math id="A8.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.32\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.32</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.32\%</annotation></semantics></math> on ViT-mid. The full-scope arm accepts
about <math id="A8.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="24\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>24</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">24\%</annotation></semantics></math> of parameters and yields smaller mean gains, <math id="A8.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.62" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.62</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.62</annotation></semantics></math>
percentage points on ViT-tiny and <math id="A8.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.73" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.73</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.73</annotation></semantics></math> on ViT-mid. The restricted arm also shows the lower across-seed variability: its standard deviation is <math id="A8.SS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.09" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.09</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.09</annotation></semantics></math> percentage points at both scales, against <math id="A8.SS2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.18" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.18</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.18</annotation></semantics></math> to
<math id="A8.SS2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.43" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.43</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.43</annotation></semantics></math> for the full-scope arm.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A8.F23" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2608.15483v1/supp_figures/claimE_vit_pdt_curves_compact.png" id="A8.F23.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:698/269;" width="698" height="269" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 23: </span>Multi-seed online comparison under pure SGD for ViT-tiny and
ViT-mid. Curves show seed means with <math id="A8.F23.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm 1</annotation></semantics></math> standard-deviation bands for
ordinary training, full-scope eligibility, and auxiliary-only
eligibility.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A8.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The improvement is therefore not obtained by predicting more. Within these
two cells, narrowing eligibility to the region that the retrospective
measurements identify as higher-confidence gives a larger and more stable
gain than making everything eligible, despite an accepted fraction roughly <math id="A8.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="30" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>30</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">30</annotation></semantics></math>- and <math id="A8.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="70" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>70</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">70</annotation></semantics></math>-fold smaller.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">H.3 </span>What This Does and Does Not Show</h3>

<div id="A8.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The result is consistent with the auxiliary–bulk separation reported in
Section 4.2, and that is the extent of the claim. Four
limits travel with it.</p>
</div>
<div id="A8.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">It does not isolate the role restriction as the causal source of the
improvement, since the two arms differ in accepted fraction as well as in
eligibility. It does not show that auxiliary parameters are uniformly
predictable, only that the region is higher-confidence on average. It is
not a wall-clock acceleration result, because no accounting of predictor
overhead is attempted here. And it covers two model–training cells at one
optimizer setting, so it is an initial indication rather than a
demonstration that the measurement framework transfers to online use.</p>
</div>
<div id="A8.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The coordinate-wise acceptance mask, not the role restriction, remains the
operative safeguard in every arm. The static role-level eligibility rule
implements neither the retrospective probe panel nor any detection of the
localized pockets inside bulk tensors that
Appendix <a href="#A4" title="Appendix D Pocket Trajectories, Persistence, and Overlap Registrations ‣ Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D</span></a> describes.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</article>
